title: Phase 2: tie each bead to its tracker story and pipeline
description:
## Outcome
Opening an epic shows the work-tracker story it points at, every bead under it, and the pipeline state of its
repository, each item marked as confirmed, kept from an earlier collection, partial, outside the collected
scope, or unconfirmed; an agent that knows only an identifier asks one route and gets the same answer across
every registered project.

## Context
The second phase of the work hub, after the framed dashboard of phase 1. Its plan, reviewed in two rounds, is
kept outside the repository; each child carries what it needs from it.

## Success criteria
- [ ] A bead's external reference survives every read and write path — hou-04l.1
- [ ] The reference is shown, edited and found from the drawer, the form, the filters and the palette — hou-04l.2
- [ ] The snapshot path, ticket host and GitHub owners are validated settings — hou-04l.3
- [ ] The snapshot is read with every degraded state the format allows — hou-04l.4
- [ ] Each project carries its pipeline repository, edited in Settings — hou-04l.5
- [ ] No link outside the allowed host and owners can be produced — hou-04l.6
- [ ] One pure resolver answers a bead's whole chain with a state per part — hou-04l.7
- [ ] Pages and agents get the chain from two read routes — hou-04l.8
- [ ] The drawer and an expanded epic show the chain — hou-04l.9
- [ ] The setup guide covers the chain's keys and the snapshot file — hou-04l.10
- [ ] The full test matrix is green on main after the code lands — hou-04l.11
- [ ] The collector writes the format-v1 file on the work machine — hou-04l.12
- [ ] The change route Houston builds matches the dashboard's — hou-04l.13
- [ ] An epic's chain is correct on the work machine — hou-04l.14

title: Carry external_ref through the bead schema and the three stores
description:
## What changes for the user
Today a bead cannot say which work-tracker story, task or bug it belongs to: the field the trackers already support is dropped when Houston reads a bead and cannot be written. Once this lands a bead keeps its reference through every read and write, on `br`, `bd` and the demo, and a duplicate is refused with the tracker's own message.

## Outcome
`external_ref` is in `beadSchema` (nullable, optional), in the create and update input schemas (trimmed, at most 128 characters, an empty string clears on update), and written by the `br`, `bd` and demo stores; tests prove the round trip against a real `br` tracker and a stubbed `bd`.

## Context
`br` 0.7.6 was checked in a throwaway tracker: it stores the reference, removes the key on an empty value, and refuses one reference on two beads of the same tracker. `bd` is not installed on this machine; its flag comes from its documentation and is tested through a stubbed runner.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`,
  `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py`; pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- This phase builds the chain: from a bead to the work-tracker story or ticket its `external_ref`
  names, the epic it belongs to, the beads under an epic, and the delivery pipeline of the project's
  repository, read from a snapshot file a local collector writes on the work machine. The phase's
  plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries everything it needs from it.

## Preconditions of this phase

- The phase 1 beads that "Order and size" names land before the steps that use them. This phase
  uses phase 1's config machinery (step 2: typed keys validated on read with a warning, an atomic
  write, a key cleared through the config route removed from the file), its capabilities route
  (step 3), its capabilities client and hook (step 5, `lib/api-client.ts` and
  `hooks/use-capabilities.ts`), and its doc-link checker (step 7, `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`).
- Read before writing routes: `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md`
  and `.../03-file-conventions/dynamic-routes.md`. Route params are a `Promise` and are awaited.
- Pure test modules load through a TypeScript-transpile-then-`vm` loader built on the one of
  `scripts/test-epic-descendants.mjs:12-23`, which resolves `./name` to `lib/name.ts` and
  anything else through `require`, with `esModuleInterop: true` added as
  `scripts/test-sprints.mjs:19` has it: without it, `import fs from "node:fs"` (`lib/bd.ts:3`,
  `lib/config.ts:2`) compiles to `node_fs_1.default`, which is `undefined` for a Node built-in. So a
  new module under `lib/` that a pure test loads imports other `lib/` modules by a relative `./`
  path, never through the `@/` alias and never `server-only`. Scripts that load `lib/config.ts`
  use the child-process loader phase 1 defines ("Two facts every config test needs" in its plan:
  `esModuleInterop: true`, `console` and `URL` in the sandbox, the test re-executing itself
  through `process.argv[1]` with an environment variable naming the case, so no helper file lands
  under `scripts/`, in a throwaway working directory with `BEADS_REPO` removed, never a bare
  `import()` of `lib/config.ts`, because Node refuses its extensionless relative imports).
- Every fixture is synthetic: numbers like `INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`;
  repositories `org/repo-a`; the instance `example.com`.
- The repository is public and each branch is pushed on its own, so the internal-name sweep runs
  before every branch's first push, over that branch's diff and commit messages, with the list of
  names kept in the user's private notes outside the repository, as in phase 1. A failed or
  unavailable sweep blocks the push; the bead records only that it passed. Step 10 runs it once
  more over the whole phase.
- Every step ends with what proves it, including one guard broken on purpose (`AGENTS.md`,
  "Landing work"), whose red assertion the bead's close reason names. Server-backed and browser
  guards are broken through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after the last one); pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node scripts/<test>.mjs`, because that tool always
  builds and starts a server, and a mutant that breaks the server's start would be reported as
  caught without the pure assertion ever running.
## Facts verified for this phase

`br` 0.7.6, in a throwaway tracker outside any repository, 2026-11-25:

- `br create --external-ref STRY00000001` stores it; `br show --json` and the tracker's
  `.beads/issues.jsonl` carry `external_ref`. The JSONL is what the hub's `br` store reads for
  its list (`lib/br.ts:13-18,180-182`), and `br show --json` is what it reads for one bead.
- `br update <id> --external-ref ""` removes it: the key is then absent, not `null` and not
  `""`, in both.
- **`br` refuses a reference another bead of the same tracker already carries:**
  `Configuration error: External reference 'STRY00000002' already exists on issue tst-3u2`.
  Setting a bead's own current value again succeeds.
- The value is stored as given; `stry00000002` was accepted.

So in one repository a tracker number names one bead at most, and the cross-project route of
step 8 is where several beads can come back for one number (a story spanning two repositories
has an epic in each).

`bd` is not installed on this machine. Its flag name, `--external-ref`, comes from its own
CLI documentation and is exercised here only through a stubbed runner.

The hierarchy lives in `parent-child` dependency edges, not in `bead.parent`: `bd export --json`
omits `parent`, and `lib/beads-view.ts:195-206` says so where `parentOf` resolves the edge.
## Specification
- `beadSchema` (`lib/schema.ts:104-137`): `external_ref: z.string().nullable().optional()`,
  typed like `started_at` and `closed_at` (`:120-122`). Without the key, `z.object` strips it
  on parse (`:133-135`); typed with a default of `""` like the text fields (`:108-111`), a
  `null` from a tracker would fail validation and the bead would be skipped
  (`lib/br.ts:135-140`, and silently in `lib/bd.ts:88-90`).
- `updateInputSchema` (`:165-187`): `external_ref: z.string().trim().max(128)`, refusing any ASCII
  control character (`0x00`-`0x1f`, `0x7f`), `.optional()`. Absent leaves it alone, an empty
  string clears it, as `parent` and `labels` already do (`:172-186`). Without the refusal a NUL
  reaches `execFile`, which throws on it, and the store answers 400 with Node's own message
  instead of `invalid_input`.
- `createInputSchema` (`:152-162`): the same field, with no `.default("")`. `CreateInput` is
  `z.infer` of the schema (`:163`), its output type, so a default would make the field required in
  `components/create-bead-modal.tsx:208-218` and break this step's build.
- `br` store: `updateArgs` (`lib/br.ts:150-163`) adds `--external-ref=<value>` when the patch
  field is not `undefined`, in the `--name=value` form every flag there uses (`:80-83`); create
  (`:208-218`) passes it when non-empty.
- `bd` store: `--external-ref` and the value go as separate arguments, the way that store passes
  every flag; create (`lib/bd.ts:180-201`) passes them only when the value is non-empty, update
  (`:203-232`) whenever the patch field is not `undefined`, so `""` clears, as `parent` does
  (`:214`).
- Demo store: create (`lib/demo-store.ts:30-53`) sets the field only when non-empty; update
  (`:56`) ignores `external_ref: undefined` and deletes the field on `""`, so a demo bead looks
  like a `br` bead with no reference and `Object.assign` never wipes it by accident.
- A duplicate reference: `br`'s refusal reaches the client as an error through `fail()`
  (`lib/api.ts`), and the drawer shows it through the mutation toast
  (`hooks/use-beads.ts:109-126`). Nothing in the hub re-checks uniqueness; the tracker owns it.

Proof:

- `scripts/test-br-store.mjs` (server-backed, throwaway `br` tracker; already in the list of
  scripts that fail under a read-only launch): create with a reference, including one starting
  with `-`, then list and get carry it; `PATCH` with a new value, including one starting with `-`
  (the `--name=value` form exists for exactly that, `lib/br.ts:80-83`); `PATCH` with `""` leaves
  the key absent in both the list and the single read; `PATCH` without the field leaves it as it
  was; a value with surrounding spaces is stored trimmed; a 129-character value and a value with a
  NUL or a line feed inside it answer 400 `invalid_input`; a second bead given the first one's
  reference answers 400 with a message naming the first bead, and the second bead is unchanged.
- A new pure script, `scripts/test-external-ref.mjs`, with the loader of "Preconditions"
  (`vm.runInThisContext`, any `./` module, memoized by name, `esModuleInterop: true`), extended
  with module stubs that also apply to nested loads (`lib/demo-store.ts` loads `./bd` and
  `./demo-data`; `lib/filters.ts` loads `./schema`, `./attribution` and `./aggregate`), and one
  module cache per set of stubs, so a `./bd` loaded through `lib/demo-store.ts` without the
  `node:child_process` stub is never the one the `bd` cases get. `scripts/test-label-edits.mjs`'s
  loader knows only `./schema` (`:22`) and its stub always throws (`:30-33`), so it is not the
  model. Cases: `beadSchema` accepts the field absent, `null` and a string; `createInputSchema`
  and `updateInputSchema` trim it, accept 128 characters, refuse 129 and a control character, and
  keep `""` apart from `undefined` on update; the demo store's create and update keep, clear
  (no own property left) and never wipe it; the `bd` store's create sends the flag only for a
  non-empty value, and its update sends it with the value, with `""` to clear, and not at all for
  `undefined`, through a stubbed `node:child_process` whose `execFile` resolves to `{ stdout }`
  through `util.promisify.custom` (the store wraps it with `util.promisify`, `lib/bd.ts:16,37`)
  and answers JSON for `create` and the follow-up `show`, and empty output for `update`, which
  goes through `runBdRaw` (`:229`).
- Broken on purpose, one at a time: dropping the `!== undefined` check in `lib/br.ts` turns the
  clear case of `scripts/test-br-store.mjs` red (through `scripts/mutate-check.py`); dropping it
  in `lib/bd.ts`, and separately dropping the demo store's deletion on `""`, each turn a case of
  `scripts/test-external-ref.mjs` red (run directly).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `scripts/with-server.sh 3211 node scripts/test-br-store.mjs` exits 0 with every new case of the Specification, including the duplicate refusal naming the other bead and a value starting with a hyphen.
- [ ] `node scripts/test-external-ref.mjs` exits 0 with the schema, input-schema, demo-store and stubbed-`bd` cases of the Specification.
- [ ] A bead read from a tracker with `external_ref: null` is not skipped.
- [ ] The deliberate break named in the Specification turns its assertion red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: a reference survives create, update, clear and both read paths on `br`, and the `bd` and demo stores match.


## Tests
- integration: `scripts/test-br-store.mjs` against a throwaway `br` tracker, through `scripts/with-server.sh`.
- unit: `scripts/test-external-ref.mjs`, pure, with the general `./` loader and a stubbed `node:child_process`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `lib/schema.ts`, `lib/br.ts`, `lib/bd.ts`, `lib/demo-store.ts`, `scripts/test-br-store.mjs`, `scripts/test-external-ref.mjs`
**Reads only:** `lib/api.ts`, `hooks/use-beads.ts`, `scripts/test-epic-descendants.mjs`, `scripts/test-label-edits.mjs`, `scripts/with-server.sh`

Four modules of one layer (schema and stores) and two tests. Size M.
close_reason: external_ref in beadSchema (nullable, no default) and in the create and update input schemas (trimmed, 128 max, control characters refused, no default); br passes --external-ref=<value> on create when non-empty and on update whenever present, bd passes the flag and value apart, the demo store keeps, clears and never wipes it. Deliberate breaks red: dropping !== undefined in lib/br.ts failed 'patch clears with an empty string: answer' (mutate-check), in lib/bd.ts failed 'bd update runs for ""', dropping the demo deletion failed 'demo clear answers a bead without the key'. A null external_ref bead is listed, not skipped. Review breaks (LF allowed, demo clear to undefined, demo value altered, br create always sending the flag) all red. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build, test-external-ref and test-br-store (with-server) pass.

title: Run the full test matrix on main after the phase 2 code lands
description:
## Outcome
Every test script of the repository has run once on `main`, after the phase 2 code beads landed and before
the work machine's final check, each under the launch mode it expects, with each row's command and exit
status recorded in the epic.

## Context
Phase 2 changes a dozen shared files (`lib/schema.ts`, `lib/config.ts`, `lib/filters.ts`, both stores, the
drawer, the create form, the epic view, the palette, Settings). This bead is the one check that every
script still passes together. It lands as a tracker-only pull request carrying the recorded matrix.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`,
  `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py`; pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- This phase builds the chain: from a bead to the work-tracker story or ticket its `external_ref`
  names, the epic it belongs to, the beads under an epic, and the delivery pipeline of the project's
  repository, read from a snapshot file a local collector writes on the work machine. The phase's
  plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries everything it needs from it.

## Specification
- Each step is one bead, on its own branch and worktree, landed through a pull request with the
  local gate of `AGENTS.md` ("Landing work"). Steps that may be developed in parallel still land
  one pull request at a time (`AGENTS.md:57-58`), so two landings never carry different copies of
  `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
- Step 1, then 2.
- Step 3 after phase 1's config, capabilities route and capabilities hook beads (phase 1 steps 2,
  3 and 5). Steps 4, 5 and 6 after 3; they touch disjoint files and may be developed in parallel.
- Step 7 after 1, 4, 5 and 6. Step 8 after 7. Step 9 after 2, 5 and 8. Step 10 after 9 and after
  phase 1 step 7, which adds `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs` and edits the same three documents.
- After step 10 lands, a verification bead runs the full test matrix once on `main`: pure scripts
  bare; scripts with a pure and a server half bare, then through the wrapper in their launch mode
  (without `SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1` for the three that are also edit-only, `test-label-edits`,
  `test-sprint-run` and `test-sprints`, and both ways for the rest); the nine read-only-only
  browser scripts with `SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1`; the other edit-only scripts without it; every other
  server or browser script both ways. The command and exit status of each row go into the epic,
  landed by that bead's tracker-only pull request. This phase changes a dozen shared files
  (`lib/schema.ts`, `lib/config.ts`, `lib/filters.ts`, both stores, the drawer, the create form,
  the epic view, the palette, Settings), which is why the whole matrix runs.
- Work side: item 1 can start at any time; item 2 also; item 3 after the verification bead, item 1,
  and phase 0's work-side installation bead.

Ten implementation beads for the steps, one verification bead for the matrix, three work-side
beads, and one epic. Steps 4 (two modules, a fixture and a two-part pure script) and 7 (one module
and one pure script) are the largest; each has one test script and one concern, so neither is
split.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pure scripts run bare; scripts with a pure and a server half run bare and through `scripts/with-server.sh` in their launch mode; the nine read-only-only browser scripts with `SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1`; the other edit-only scripts without it; every other server or browser script both ways.
- [ ] Every row exits 0; a failing row opens a bead for its fix and this bead stays open until it passes.
- [ ] The epic carries one line per row: the command and its exit status.
- [ ] Done when: the whole matrix is green on `main` and recorded in the epic.

## Tests
- gate: the repository's whole test suite, as listed in `AGENTS.md` ("Running the tests").

title: Make the collector write the format-v1 snapshot beside its own
description:
## What changes for the user
Until this is done the chain shows every snapshot item as unconfirmed, because no file in the format Houston
reads exists. Once it is done the collector writes that file next to its own on every collection, and the
chain fills in with real states.

## Outcome
The collector on the work machine writes a format-v1 file beside its own snapshot, atomically, with the
generic names below for every key and fixed value Houston's code matches on, and leaves its own file
untouched.

## Context
The collector is local code on the work machine and is never changed in this repository. Text that is only
shown keeps its real wording in that file, which never leaves the machine; only the repository's fixtures
use invented text. The work machine pulls this public repository and never pushes, so the user reports the result in
generic words and the bead is closed on the development machine in a tracker-only pull request. The
public tracker never gets a real ticket number, a host, a repository or team name, a header, an error
text, a screenshot, or any other work data.

## Specification
1. The collector writes a format-v1 file next to its own snapshot, in the same atomic way, and
   leaves its own file untouched; the framed dashboard keeps reading the old one. The generic names
   apply to every key and fixed value the hub's code matches or branches on: the keys of the source

title: Confirm the route the current dashboard opens a change with
description:
## Outcome
The route the current dashboard builds to open a change by its number is known, compared with the
standard change form Houston uses, and written down with the host replaced by `example.com`.

## Context
Houston links a change number that is not in the changes source to the standard change form,
`https://<serviceNowHost>/change_request.do?sysparm_query=number=<number>`, a provisional choice made
without seeing the work dashboard. The work machine pulls this public repository and never pushes, so the user reports the result in
generic words and the bead is closed on the development machine in a tracker-only pull request. The
public tracker never gets a real ticket number, a host, a repository or team name, a header, an error
text, a screenshot, or any other work data.

## Specification
2. The change-lookup route: open a change by its number from the current dashboard, and compare the
   route with the one in provisional decision 3, writing it down with the host replaced by
   `example.com`. If they differ, a follow-up bead changes the builder of step 6.

## Options
- **A · The routes match.** What changes: nothing; the provisional decision becomes final.
- **B · They differ.** What changes: a follow-up bead changes the link builder to the route the dashboard uses, with its test.

## What decides it
The route the current dashboard opens when a change number is clicked, compared with the standard form.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The dashboard's change route is recorded with the host replaced by `example.com`.
- [ ] If it differs from the standard form, a follow-up bead exists and this bead names it.
- [ ] Done when: the change link Houston builds is known to match what the dashboard opens.

title: Check an epic's chain on the work machine
description:

work machine shows its real story, its beads and the pipeline state of its repository.

## Outcome

number, the epic's chain shows every part with a state.

## Context
The work machine pulls this public repository and never pushes, so the user reports the result in
generic words and the bead is closed on the development machine in a tracker-only pull request. The
public tracker never gets a real ticket number, a host, a repository or team name, a header, an error
text, a screenshot, or any other work data.

## Specification
3. On the work machine, from the Houston checkout, `scripts/update.sh`; then set the three keys and
   each project's `pipelineRepo`; give an epic its story number; open it. The story, its beads and
   the pipeline state of its repository show, each with a state; their links open the instance's
   and GitHub's pages in a new tab; `GET /api/links/<that story number>` returns the epic and the
   ticket.

title: Show, edit and search external_ref in the drawer, the form, the filters and the palette
description:
## What changes for the user
Today there is no way to see or type which story a bead belongs to, and no way to find an epic by its story number. Once this lands the drawer shows and edits the reference, the create form takes it, the board, the list, a new epic-view filter and the palette all find a bead or an epic by it, and a typed reference survives a stray click outside.

## Outcome
The drawer, the create form, `matchesFilters`, the epic view (with a new filter bound to the URL's `q`) and the command palette handle `external_ref`; a browser test with fixtures proves each, under both launch modes.

## Context
The board and the list leave epics out, so a filter there alone would never find an epic; the epic view gets its own filter. New labels are Portuguese, the inherited drawer's edit button keeps its English title, which existing tests match. The schema field comes from the preceding bead.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`,
  `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py`; pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- This phase builds the chain: from a bead to the work-tracker story or ticket its `external_ref`
  names, the epic it belongs to, the beads under an epic, and the delivery pipeline of the project's
  repository, read from a snapshot file a local collector writes on the work machine. The phase's
  plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries everything it needs from it.

## Preconditions of this phase

- The phase 1 beads that "Order and size" names land before the steps that use them. This phase
  uses phase 1's config machinery (step 2: typed keys validated on read with a warning, an atomic
  write, a key cleared through the config route removed from the file), its capabilities route
  (step 3), its capabilities client and hook (step 5, `lib/api-client.ts` and
  `hooks/use-capabilities.ts`), and its doc-link checker (step 7, `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`).
- Read before writing routes: `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md`
  and `.../03-file-conventions/dynamic-routes.md`. Route params are a `Promise` and are awaited.
- Pure test modules load through a TypeScript-transpile-then-`vm` loader built on the one of
  `scripts/test-epic-descendants.mjs:12-23`, which resolves `./name` to `lib/name.ts` and
  anything else through `require`, with `esModuleInterop: true` added as
  `scripts/test-sprints.mjs:19` has it: without it, `import fs from "node:fs"` (`lib/bd.ts:3`,
  `lib/config.ts:2`) compiles to `node_fs_1.default`, which is `undefined` for a Node built-in. So a
  new module under `lib/` that a pure test loads imports other `lib/` modules by a relative `./`
  path, never through the `@/` alias and never `server-only`. Scripts that load `lib/config.ts`
  use the child-process loader phase 1 defines ("Two facts every config test needs" in its plan:
  `esModuleInterop: true`, `console` and `URL` in the sandbox, the test re-executing itself
  through `process.argv[1]` with an environment variable naming the case, so no helper file lands
  under `scripts/`, in a throwaway working directory with `BEADS_REPO` removed, never a bare
  `import()` of `lib/config.ts`, because Node refuses its extensionless relative imports).
- Every fixture is synthetic: numbers like `INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`;
  repositories `org/repo-a`; the instance `example.com`.
- The repository is public and each branch is pushed on its own, so the internal-name sweep runs
  before every branch's first push, over that branch's diff and commit messages, with the list of
  names kept in the user's private notes outside the repository, as in phase 1. A failed or
  unavailable sweep blocks the push; the bead records only that it passed. Step 10 runs it once
  more over the whole phase.
- Every step ends with what proves it, including one guard broken on purpose (`AGENTS.md`,
  "Landing work"), whose red assertion the bead's close reason names. Server-backed and browser
  guards are broken through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after the last one); pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node scripts/<test>.mjs`, because that tool always
  builds and starts a server, and a mutant that breaks the server's start would be reported as
  caught without the pure assertion ever running.

## Specification
- Drawer (`components/bead-detail-drawer.tsx`):
  - read mode shows "Referência externa" with the trimmed value among the rows near the parent
    link (`:549-579`), and nothing when it is absent, `null` or blank; while editing
    (`editing && !readOnly`, `:486`), the input below takes that row's place, so the label is never
    shown twice;
  - edit mode, which today edits title and description (`:486-506`, `:659-745`), always renders a
    labelled "Referência externa" input, also when the bead has none and while the description
    preview is shown. `startEdit` (`:315-320`) resets that draft from `bead.external_ref ?? ""`, as
    it resets the others, and so does the initial state when the drawer opens straight into edit,
    because the drawer's body does not remount when the bead updates in place (`:184`). `saveEdit`
    (`:322-330`) keeps sending `title` and `description`, which
    `scripts/test-all-panel-writes.mjs:522-525` expects, and adds `external_ref`, trimmed, only when
    it differs from `(bead.external_ref ?? "").trim()`, so a value the CLI stored untrimmed is not
    sent back on a title-only edit. The input saves on the same submit key as the
    title and description (`:494`, `:682`). The edit button keeps its title
    "Edit title & description" (`:436`), which `scripts/test-epic-focus.mjs:53` and
    `scripts/test-all-panel-writes.mjs:513,715,731` match;
  - the unsaved check (`:305-307`) also compares that draft with the bead's value, so a typed
    reference survives a stray outside click, the way the title and description drafts do
    (`:156-167`).
- Create form (`components/create-bead-modal.tsx`): `FormState` (`:28-37`) gets the field, it is
  rendered with the others (`:284-455`), `hasText` (`:153`) counts it, and `submit`
  (`:206-238`) sends it when non-blank.
- Text filter: `matchesFilters` (`lib/filters.ts:182-191`) also matches `external_ref`, so the
  board and the list find a bead by its tracker number. Its doc comment (`:7-8`) becomes
  "id / title / assignee / labels / external_ref", which is what it matches.
- Epic view (`components/epics-view.tsx`): it has no text filter (`:65`, `:84-86`, `:137-144`),
  and the board and the list leave epics out, so a filter there alone would never find an epic.
  It gets an input, "Filtrar épicos", with `data-search` so the `/` shortcut focuses it
  (`hooks/use-app-keyboard.ts:137`), bound to the URL's `q` parameter through `useUrlFilters`
  (`hooks/use-url-filters.ts:25`), matching an epic's displayed id, title and `external_ref`.
  - The focused epic stays visible whatever the filter. Today a focused closed epic is kept in
    two moves: `:85` keeps it for the first render so the focus effect can find and scroll to it,
    then `:99` turns "hide closed" off just before `:101` clears the focus on the next frame. The
    text filter follows the same two moves: `:85` also keeps the focused epic for the first
    render, and the focus effect (`:98-103`) clears `q` (keeping the other URL parameters) when the
    focused epic does not match it. Keeping only the first move would show the epic for one frame
    and lose it when the focus clears. The clear goes through a small addition to `useUrlFilters`
    that sets the pending search to `""` and writes the URL in `"replace"` mode. `setFilters`
    (`hooks/use-url-filters.ts:54-63`) would push a history entry here, since nothing has been
    typed yet (`:57`), so Back would return to the filtered view; a bare `updateUrl` would skip the
    pending search, and `useSearchParams` can reflect the change a render late (`:31-35`), which
    filters the epic out for that render, once the focus has cleared.
  - The header's "of N" count (`:133`) also shows when the text filter narrows the list. The
    header (`:128`) wraps (`flex-wrap`), so the input does not push it past a narrow screen.
  - When the text filter is not empty and leaves no epic, the empty state says "Nenhum épico
    corresponde ao filtro." instead of the "No epics yet" text of `:351`; with an empty filter
    that text stays as it is.
  - It works on `/all` too.
- Command palette (`components/command-palette.tsx:400`): the bead item's `value` gets the
  trimmed reference appended only when it is non-empty, never the strings "undefined" or "null",
  so the palette's own filter matches it. The palette is mounted only in the project shell
  (`components/keyboard-layer.tsx:89`); that does not change.

Proof: a new browser script, `scripts/test-external-ref-ui.mjs`, answering the API from
fixtures, including `GET /api/viewer-mode` answered `{ readOnly: false }`, so it passes under
both launch modes (under a read-only launch the edit button and the create form are otherwise
disabled, `components/bead-detail-drawer.tsx:434`, `components/app-shell.tsx:267`):

- the drawer shows the reference; edit, type a new one, click outside: the drawer stays open;
  save: the `PATCH` body carries `external_ref: "<new>"` beside title and description; an edit of
  the title alone sends no `external_ref`, also on a bead whose stored value has surrounding
  spaces; clear: the body carries `external_ref: ""`; while editing, "Referência externa" appears
  once; cancel and edit again: the draft shows the bead's value, not the abandoned one;
- the create form keeps a typed reference on an outside click and sends it in its body;
- `?q=STRY00000001` on the board shows only the bead carrying it;
- the epic view's filter finds an epic by its reference on a project page and on `/all`; jumping to
  an epic from the list while `q` excludes it (at a viewport of at least 1024 pixels, since the
  list's parent chip is `hidden lg:flex`, `components/list-view.tsx:377`) clears `q`, adds no
  history entry, and leaves the epic shown and expanded once the focus effect has settled; a
  non-empty filter with no match shows "Nenhum épico corresponde ao filtro."; at a 390-pixel
  viewport the epic view's header does not overflow horizontally;
- on a project page, where the keyboard layer and the palette are mounted (`/all` has neither),
  `/` on the epic view focuses "Filtrar épicos"; Control+Enter in the drawer's reference input
  saves; the palette lists the bead when its reference is typed, and does not match "undefined"
  or "null" for a bead without one. The palette's filter matches a subsequence, so the fixture's
  ids and titles do not contain the letters of "null" or "undefined" in order.

The pure half of `scripts/test-external-ref.mjs` adds `matchesFilters` cases for the field.
Broken on purpose, one at a time: dropping the filter match turns the board case red and the
`matchesFilters` case of `scripts/test-external-ref.mjs` red; dropping the `q` clear in the focus
effect turns the jump case red; sending `external_ref` on every save turns the title-only case red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `scripts/with-server.sh 3211 node scripts/test-external-ref-ui.mjs` exits 0, and again under `SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1`, with every case of the Specification.
- [ ] `node scripts/test-external-ref.mjs` gains the `matchesFilters` cases for the field and exits 0.
- [ ] `scripts/test-epic-focus.mjs`, `scripts/test-all-panel-writes.mjs`, `scripts/test-unsaved-dismiss.mjs` and `scripts/test-keyboard.mjs` pass under the launch mode `AGENTS.md` gives each.
- [ ] The deliberate break named in the Specification turns its assertion red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: a story number typed in the drawer finds its epic from the epic view and the palette.


## Tests
- e2e: `scripts/test-external-ref-ui.mjs`, Playwright with fixtures.
- unit: the `matchesFilters` cases in `scripts/test-external-ref.mjs`.
- regression: the existing drawer, epic-view and keyboard scripts.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `components/bead-detail-drawer.tsx`, `components/create-bead-modal.tsx`, `lib/filters.ts`, `components/epics-view.tsx`, `components/command-palette.tsx`, `hooks/use-url-filters.ts`, `scripts/test-external-ref-ui.mjs`, `scripts/test-external-ref.mjs`
**Reads only:** `hooks/use-app-keyboard.ts`, `components/keyboard-layer.tsx`, `scripts/test-epic-focus.mjs`, `scripts/test-all-panel-writes.mjs`, `scripts/test-unsaved-dismiss.mjs`, `scripts/test-keyboard.mjs`, `scripts/with-server.sh`

Five components or modules across the UI and two tests. Size L; the field lands in every place a user meets it at once, or it is half-visible.
close_reason: external_ref is shown and edited in the bead drawer and the create form, matched by the board and list search (matchesFilters), filtered in the epic view by id, title and reference with a no-match state, and found by the command palette. Every listed break turned a named assertion red through mutate-check, and the matchesFilters cases of scripts/test-external-ref.mjs went red under their breaks. The lane found test-keyboard intermittently red on this branch (5 of 40 runs, 0 of 40 on its base): the epic filter carries data-search, so typing right after 'g b' could land in it while the view switched; review applied the lane's fix, waiting for the Board heading (0 of 70 runs afterwards). After merging main, the browser fixture answered the sidebar's new capabilities read. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build, test-external-ref, test-external-ref-ui default and SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1, test-epic-focus and test-keyboard read-only, test-all-panel-writes, test-unsaved-dismiss and test-search-typing pass.

title: Add the snapshotPath, serviceNowHost and githubOrgs config keys
description:
## What changes for the user
Today Houston knows nothing about where the work snapshot lives or which hosts a link may point at. Once this lands the three settings can be set and cleared like the work dashboard's address, each refused when malformed, and pages learn whether the chain is configured.

`lib/config-values.ts` holds the validators (also those of the pipeline repository and the ticket-number shape); the three keys go through phase 1's config machinery with atomic patch validation; the capabilities answer gains `chain`.

Phase 1 built the config machinery (typed keys, warning on an invalid value on disk, atomic write, removal) and the capabilities route and hook; this bead extends them.

## Preconditions of this phase

- The phase 1 beads that "Order and size" names land before the steps that use them. This phase

  write, a key cleared through the config route removed from the file), its capabilities route
  (step 3), its capabilities client and hook (step 5, `lib/api-client.ts` and

- Read before writing routes: `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md`
  and `.../03-file-conventions/dynamic-routes.md`. Route params are a `Promise` and are awaited.
- Pure test modules load through a TypeScript-transpile-then-`vm` loader built on the one of
  `scripts/test-epic-descendants.mjs:12-23`, which resolves `./name` to `lib/name.ts` and
  anything else through `require`, with `esModuleInterop: true` added as
  `scripts/test-sprints.mjs:19` has it: without it, `import fs from "node:fs"` (`lib/bd.ts:3`,

  new module under `lib/` that a pure test loads imports other `lib/` modules by a relative `./`
  path, never through the `@/` alias and never `server-only`. Scripts that load `lib/config.ts`
  use the child-process loader phase 1 defines ("Two facts every config test needs" in its plan:
  `esModuleInterop: true`, `console` and `URL` in the sandbox, the test re-executing itself

  under `scripts/`, in a throwaway working directory with `BEADS_REPO` removed, never a bare
  `import()` of `lib/config.ts`, because Node refuses its extensionless relative imports).
- Every fixture is synthetic: numbers like `INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`;
  repositories `org/repo-a`; the instance `example.com`.
- The repository is public and each branch is pushed on its own, so the internal-name sweep runs
  before every branch's first push, over that branch's diff and commit messages, with the list of
  names kept in the user's private notes outside the repository, as in phase 1. A failed or

- Every step ends with what proves it, including one guard broken on purpose (`AGENTS.md`,

  guards are broken through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after the last one); pure-script

  builds and starts a server, and a mutant that breaks the server's start would be reported as

## Specification
Three keys, each through phase 1's machinery (typed in `AppConfig`, validated when read with a
warning, accepted and refused by the config route with `invalid_config`, removed from the file
when cleared):

- `snapshotPath`: a primitive string starting with `/` (checked directly, since the module has
  no `node:path`), with no ASCII control character and no surrounding whitespace.
- `serviceNowHost`: a bare host name of at least two dot-separated lowercase labels, each of
  letters and digits with hyphens only inside, the last one holding at least one letter, so a
  single-label name and an IPv4 literal are refused; no leading or trailing dot or hyphen, no empty
  label, no scheme, port, path or user information.
- `githubOrgs`: a list of lowercase owner names (letters and digits, hyphens only inside),
  possibly empty. On disk, a value that is not a list, or a list with any invalid entry, is ignored
  whole, with a warning, rather than filtered.

`saveConfig` takes `string | null` for `snapshotPath` and `serviceNowHost` and `string[] | null`
for `githubOrgs`, `null` removing the key from memory and from the file, as phase 1's
`workDashboardUrl` does: every key a patch clears is deleted, never set to `undefined`, and all of

before anything is saved and throws `ConfigError(..., "invalid_config")`, so a patch with one valid
key and one invalid one writes nothing.

The validators live in a new pure module, `lib/config-values.ts`, with no imports and no
TypeScript syntax that type stripping cannot erase, together with the `pipelineRepo` validator of
step 5 and the ticket-number shape of provisional decision 4, so steps 5 and 6 share one
definition. Each answers `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, reason }`, as phase 1's
`checkWorkDashboardUrl` does.

`GET /api/capabilities` adds `chain: boolean`, true when `snapshotPath` is set; the client type
and `hooks/use-capabilities.ts` expose `chain` as `data?.chain === true`, so it is false when a
fixture answers `{}` or phase 1's `{ workDashboardUrl: null }`.

Proof: a new pure script, `scripts/test-config-values.mjs`, with an accepted and a refused value
per rule: `https://example.com`, `example.com:443`, `Example.com`, `user@example.com`,
`.example.com`, `a..b`, `-bad.com`, `bad-.com`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, a relative path, a path
with surrounding spaces, a path containing a NUL, `Org-A`, `-org` and `org-` in the list, `org/..`
and `org/.` for the repository, with one-character labels and owners (`a.co`, `a`) accepted; and
for the ticket-number shape, `CHG00000001` and `A1` accepted, `chg1`, `CHG`, `1`, `CHG1?x=1`, a

title: Read and validate the format-v1 snapshot, with one lookup by source class
description:
## What changes for the user
Today Houston cannot read anything the work collector gathers. Once this lands it reads the snapshot file, tolerates every degraded state the format allows, and answers whether an identifier is found, outside the collected scope, or unconfirmed, without ever calling a ticket closed.

## Outcome
`lib/snapshot-format.ts` (pure) types and validates the part of format version 1 this phase reads and implements `lookupTicket`; `lib/snapshot.ts` (server only) reads the file with a cache keyed on exact file identity; a pure test over a synthetic fixture covers each state.

## Context
The difficulty is critical because a wrong answer is silent: a lookup that says absent where it should say unconfirmed would tell the user a ticket is outside scope while the collection simply failed. The format's contract is a sanitized document kept with the plan; the Specification carries every field this bead needs.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`,
  `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py`; pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- This phase builds the chain: from a bead to the work-tracker story or ticket its `external_ref`
  names, the epic it belongs to, the beads under an epic, and the delivery pipeline of the project's
  repository, read from a snapshot file a local collector writes on the work machine. The phase's
  plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries everything it needs from it.

## Preconditions of this phase

- The phase 1 beads that "Order and size" names land before the steps that use them. This phase
  uses phase 1's config machinery (step 2: typed keys validated on read with a warning, an atomic
  write, a key cleared through the config route removed from the file), its capabilities route
  (step 3), its capabilities client and hook (step 5, `lib/api-client.ts` and
  `hooks/use-capabilities.ts`), and its doc-link checker (step 7, `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`).
- Read before writing routes: `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md`
  and `.../03-file-conventions/dynamic-routes.md`. Route params are a `Promise` and are awaited.
- Pure test modules load through a TypeScript-transpile-then-`vm` loader built on the one of
  `scripts/test-epic-descendants.mjs:12-23`, which resolves `./name` to `lib/name.ts` and
  anything else through `require`, with `esModuleInterop: true` added as
  `scripts/test-sprints.mjs:19` has it: without it, `import fs from "node:fs"` (`lib/bd.ts:3`,
  `lib/config.ts:2`) compiles to `node_fs_1.default`, which is `undefined` for a Node built-in. So a
  new module under `lib/` that a pure test loads imports other `lib/` modules by a relative `./`
  path, never through the `@/` alias and never `server-only`. Scripts that load `lib/config.ts`
  use the child-process loader phase 1 defines ("Two facts every config test needs" in its plan:
  `esModuleInterop: true`, `console` and `URL` in the sandbox, the test re-executing itself
  through `process.argv[1]` with an environment variable naming the case, so no helper file lands
  under `scripts/`, in a throwaway working directory with `BEADS_REPO` removed, never a bare
  `import()` of `lib/config.ts`, because Node refuses its extensionless relative imports).
- Every fixture is synthetic: numbers like `INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`;
  repositories `org/repo-a`; the instance `example.com`.
- The repository is public and each branch is pushed on its own, so the internal-name sweep runs
  before every branch's first push, over that branch's diff and commit messages, with the list of
  names kept in the user's private notes outside the repository, as in phase 1. A failed or
  unavailable sweep blocks the push; the bead records only that it passed. Step 10 runs it once
  more over the whole phase.
- Every step ends with what proves it, including one guard broken on purpose (`AGENTS.md`,
  "Landing work"), whose red assertion the bead's close reason names. Server-backed and browser
  guards are broken through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after the last one); pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node scripts/<test>.mjs`, because that tool always
  builds and starts a server, and a mutant that breaks the server's start would be reported as
  caught without the pure assertion ever running.

## Specification
Two modules.

`lib/snapshot-format.ts`, pure (it imports `zod` and nothing local), types the part of format
version 1 that the hub reads, from the snapshot contract kept beside this plan
(`evidence/Snapshot contract.md`).

- The root: `schema_version` exactly `1`, and `sources`, checked only as a plain non-array
  object. Anything else (the comparison, the morning summary, and every source this phase does
  not read) is ignored.
- Each of the nine sources this phase reads is parsed on its own, so a malformed source this
  phase does not read never fails the file, and a malformed known envelope becomes the fallback
  envelope described below. They are the ticket sources `incidents`,
  `changes`, `work_tracker_stories`, `work_tracker_bugs`, `work_tracker_tasks`,
  `work_tracker_subtasks` and `ritms`; `approvals`; and `pipeline`.
- The envelope: `label`, `provider` (nullable), `status` (closed set `not_collected`, `ok`,
  `partial`, `error`, `auth_expired`), `complete`, `last_attempt_at` (nullable),
  `last_success_at` (nullable), `error` (nullable), and `records`, checked first only as a list of
  anything and then parsed record by record, so one invalid record never fails its envelope. A
  malformed known envelope becomes `{ label: <the source's key>, provider: null, status: "error",
  complete: false, last_attempt_at: null, last_success_at: null, error: "invalid envelope",
  records: [] }`, so a reason built from it is never empty.
- Every record field below that the contract types as an integer (a run's `id`, a pull request's
  `number`, an issue's `run_id` and `limit`, the entries of `existing_prs`) is a positive safe
  integer (`z.number().int().positive()`, which in zod 4.6.7 also refuses `2**53`; `JSON.parse`
  cannot read a larger one exactly anyway); every other scalar record field is a string, nullable
  only where named.
- Ticket records: `key`, `number` (it can be `""` in the tracker lists and request items),
  `title`, `state`, `link`, and an optional `sprint`, which only the four tracker lists carry
  (`evidence/Snapshot contract.md:355`).
- Approval records, in `approvals`: `key`, `number`, `title`, `state`, `link` and `record_type`.
  An approval's `number`, `title` and `record_type` describe the ticket it refers to, while its
  `key` and `link` are the approval's own.
- Pipeline records, in `pipeline`, a union on `kind`, with the optional and nullable fields the
  contract gives them:
  - `run`: `id`, `repo`, `created_at`, `status`, `conclusion` (null while the run has not
    finished), `head` (nullable), optional `changes` (a list of strings), optional `existing_prs`
    (a list of integers);
  - `pr`: `number`, `repo`, `base`, `head`, `anomalies` (a list of strings);
  - `issue`, itself two shapes: the budget issue (`part: "budget"`, `limit`, no `repo` and no
    `run_id`); and a repository or run issue (any other non-empty `part`, with a required `repo`
    and `error`, a `run_id` that is an integer for a run-level failure such as `annotations` or
    `trigger` and null or absent for a repository-level one, no `limit`), so a malformed
    repository issue without `repo` is refused instead of read as a budget issue
    (`evidence/Snapshot contract.md:430-434`).

Degraded states the format allows, and what the reader makes of them:

- a known source absent from the file: an envelope with `status: "not_collected"`,
  `complete: false`, no records;
- a record that fails validation: left out, and its source is incomplete, with the effective
  status `partial` (provisional decision 5). Likewise an envelope saying `status: "ok"` with
  `complete: false` has the effective status `partial`, as the contract reads it, so a reason never
  reports a source as "ok" while calling it incomplete;
- a file that is not JSON, or whose `schema_version` is not `1`: unreadable.

Freshness of a source, read from its envelope first, because a source that kept old records
after a failure carries no trace of the failure in the records themselves:

- `confirmed`: `status` is `ok` and `complete` is true;
- `historical`: otherwise, when `last_success_at` is an ISO-8601 date-time
  (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, optional fractional seconds, which Python's `isoformat()` writes when
  the microseconds are not zero, then `Z` or `±HH:MM` with an hour of `00`-`23` and a minute of
  `00`-`59`) whose date exists (its year, month and day read back unchanged from
  `new Date(Date.UTC(y, m - 1, d))`) and which parses to a finite date, and no record was dropped by
  validation; the item shows that time. `Date.parse` alone accepts strings like `"1"` and rolls
  `2026-02-31T00:00:00Z` over to 3 March;
- `partial`: otherwise.

One lookup, `lookupTicket(snapshot, identifier)`, used by both routes of step 8:

- the identifier is trimmed; an empty one matches nothing;
- it is compared with each ticket record's trimmed, non-empty `number`, without regard to case,
  in every ticket source, in the fixed order listed above, and in no other kind of source;
- found: the record, its source and the source's freshness;
- not found: `absent` when every ticket source is `ok` and complete, `unconfirmed` otherwise.
  Pipeline, load and observability sources never take part, so a failure there never taints the
  answer;
- approvals whose trimmed, non-empty `number` matches the identifier the same way, without regard
  to case, are returned with every answer, found, absent or unconfirmed, each with the freshness
  of the `approvals` source. An approval is never the
  primary record of a number, so it never makes an answer `found`.

`lib/snapshot.ts`, server only, exports a synchronous `readSnapshot()` for the file at
`snapshotPath`; with the key unset it clears the cache and answers "unavailable". Otherwise it
opens the path with `O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK`, so a named pipe cannot block the server before the
regular-file check refuses it, and closes the descriptor in `finally` on every path. It takes
`fstat` with `bigint: true` (device, inode, size, modification and change times in nanoseconds),
checks it is a regular file, and compares the path and that key with the cached entry before
reading anything: on a match it returns the cached result without reading; otherwise it reads the
bytes from that same descriptor, parses them and caches the result under the path and the key, so
the key describes exactly the bytes read and is never truncated to milliseconds. The config route
can change the path at runtime, and the collector rewrites the file atomically, which changes the
inode. A missing, non-regular or unreadable file clears the cache and answers "unavailable" with
its reason, and the resolver then makes every snapshot item unconfirmed. Being synchronous, two
requests never race on the cache. (The TypeScript target is ES2017, so the bigint values are
compared with `===`, with no `0n` literals.)

Proof:

- a new pure script, `scripts/test-snapshot.mjs`, over a synthetic fixture,
  `scripts/fixtures/snapshot-v1.json`, which includes a waiting run (`conclusion: null`), a
  repository-level issue (`run_id: null`, no `limit`), a run-level issue (`run_id` an integer, no
  `limit`) and a budget issue (no `repo`, `run_id` or `error`, with `limit`):
  - each freshness value, from three envelopes; a record dropped by validation makes its source
    `partial` even with `last_success_at` set; an unparseable `last_success_at` is not
    `historical`; a `last_success_at` with fractional seconds is `historical`, and
    `2026-02-31T00:00:00Z` and an offset of `+24:00` are not;
  - found, absent, and unconfirmed because one ticket source other than the first (`incidents`) is
    partial, so the first-source-only mutation below can fail; a miss is unconfirmed, not absent,
    when a ticket source says `ok` and `complete: true` but one of its records was dropped;
  - a ticket source missing from the file makes a lookup unconfirmed;
  - a malformed envelope in a source this phase does not read changes nothing; a malformed
    `pipeline` envelope does not change a ticket lookup;
  - an approval returned with its found change, an approval returned with an absent answer for a
    change outside the collected scope, and one returned with an unconfirmed answer;
  - a lowercase identifier finds an uppercase number and an uppercase approval's number; an empty
    identifier finds nothing, even with a record whose `number` is `""`;
  - the four pipeline records of the fixture named above parse;
  - `schema_version: 2` and `sources: []` are unreadable; a repository issue without `repo` is
    dropped as invalid; an `ok` envelope with `complete: false` has the effective status `partial`;
    `last_success_at: "1"` is not historical.
- `lib/snapshot.ts` in a child process whose `./` loader memoizes modules by name (so
  `saveConfig` and `lib/snapshot.ts` share one `lib/config.ts`) and sets `esModuleInterop`, with
  `server-only` stubbed, a counting spy on `node:fs`'s `readFileSync` that counts only reads of a
  numeric descriptor (so `lib/config.ts` reading `config.json` by path is not counted), and
  throwaway files: unset path, missing file, a directory, invalid JSON, a valid file read once
  across repeated calls (one read), parsed again after an atomic rewrite of equal length through a
  temporary file and a rename (two reads), after the path changes to another file, and
  `snapshotPath` cleared after a successful read answering unavailable.
- Broken on purpose: deciding `absent` from the first ticket source only turns the partial case
  red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `node scripts/test-snapshot.mjs` exits 0 with every case of the Specification, over `scripts/fixtures/snapshot-v1.json`.
- [ ] The child-process cases for `lib/snapshot.ts` count one read across repeated calls and a second read after an atomic rewrite of equal length.
- [ ] Deciding absent from the first ticket source only turns the partial case red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: every freshness and lookup state of the Specification is a named assertion over the synthetic fixture.


## Tests
- unit: `scripts/test-snapshot.mjs`, pure, plus child-process cases for `lib/snapshot.ts` with `server-only` stubbed.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `lib/snapshot-format.ts`, `lib/snapshot.ts`, `scripts/test-snapshot.mjs`, `scripts/fixtures/snapshot-v1.json`
**Reads only:** `lib/config.ts`, `scripts/test-epic-descendants.mjs`

Two new modules, one test and one fixture. Size L: a schema-shaped module whose fixture and test are large, but no existing file changes.
close_reason: lib/snapshot-format.ts validates the format-v1 snapshot (schema_version 1 exactly, sources an object, each envelope's status a closed set, records checked one by one with bad ones counted and dropped, a source with a dropped record partial), derives per-source freshness (confirmed, partial, historical with a strict ISO last_success_at, not_collected, fallback) and answers one lookup per source class with a case-insensitive trimmed identifier; lib/snapshot.ts reads the file once per identity (path, device, inode, size, mtime), non-blocking and regular files only, closing every descriptor, and clears the cache on an unset or unavailable path. The fixture is synthetic. Deciding absent from the first ticket source only failed 'unconfirmed because changes is partial'; 30 mutations, two equivalent (offset bounds the parser already enforces). Review break: the identifier no longer trimmed failed 'the identifier is trimmed'. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build and test-snapshot pass.

title: Attach a pipeline repository to each project and edit it in Settings
description:
## What changes for the user
Today a project knows nothing about the repository its delivery pipeline runs for. Once this lands a project carries its pipeline repository, set and cleared from its Settings page, kept across restarts, and refused when it is not a valid owner and name.

## Outcome
`ProjectEntry` gains `pipelineRepo`, kept by `sanitizeProjects`; `renameProject` becomes `updateProject`; the project route, the doctor route, the client types and the Settings card handle it; a pure, server and browser test prove it.

## Context
Without the `sanitizeProjects` change the key would be dropped on load and then wiped from the file by the next write, which replaces the project list whole. The demo project is not in the list, so its Settings shows no field.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`,

  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.

  guards are broken and run directly with `node`.

  and `.../03-file-conventions/dynamic-routes.md`. Route params are a `Promise` and are awaited.
- Pure test modules load through a TypeScript-transpile-then-`vm` loader built on the one of
  `scripts/test-epic-descendants.mjs:12-23`, which resolves `./name` to `lib/name.ts` and
  anything else through `require`, with `esModuleInterop: true` added as
  `scripts/test-sprints.mjs:19` has it: without it, `import fs from "node:fs"` (`lib/bd.ts:3`,

  use the child-process loader phase 1 defines ("Two facts every config test needs" in its plan:

- Every fixture is synthetic: numbers like `INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`;
  repositories `org/repo-a`; the instance `example.com`.
- The repository is public and each branch is pushed on its own, so the internal-name sweep runs
  before every branch's first push, over that branch's diff and commit messages, with the list of
  names kept in the user's private notes outside the repository, as in phase 1. A failed or

## Specification
- `ProjectEntry` (`lib/config.ts:16-23`) gets `pipelineRepo?: string`, `owner/name` in lowercase:
  owner of letters and digits with hyphens only inside; name of letters, digits, hyphens, dots and
  underscores, never `.` or `..`. The validator is the one of step 3 in `lib/config-values.ts`.
- `sanitizeProjects` (`:190-209`) copies the known fields one by one, so without a change it would
  drop the key on load, and `persist` would then wipe it from the file on the next write, because
  it replaces `projects` whole. It copies a valid value; a value present on disk but invalid,
  `""` and `null` included, is left out with a warning; an absent key is normal and warns
  nothing.

  validates a non-empty `pipelineRepo` before changing anything, and throws
  `ConfigError(..., "invalid_config")` on a refusal, so an invalid repository sent with a new name

  neither is, or when the name is blank); `updateProject` answers an invalid repository with
  400 `invalid_config` and an unknown id with 404. The client gets `api.projects.update` in place
  of `rename` (`lib/api-client.ts:318-322`); nothing in the UI calls `rename` today.
- The doctor route builds the project by hand (`app/api/p/[projectId]/doctor/route.ts:16`) from
  `getProject()`, which returns `ProjectEntry | DemoProject`; it adds `pipelineRepo` when
  `"pipelineRepo" in project` and it is set, a narrowing the build needs. `DoctorResponse.project`
  (`lib/api-client.ts:94`) and `ProjectInfo` (`:76-83`) type it. `GET /api/projects` passes it
  through already (`annotate`, `app/api/projects/route.ts:10-20`).
- Settings, Project card (`components/settings-view.tsx:126-148`), read-only today: an input
  "Repositório do pipeline" in a child component of its own, with a "Salvar" button and its own
  submit-key handler, never the form's `saveOnSubmitKey` (`:116-120`), which saves the global
  config. It trims the value before sending (the route stays strict), and shows the route's
  refusal under it, cleared on edit and on success. It is rendered only when the doctor answer
  names a project and the project is not the demo, which is not in the project list, so
  `PATCH /api/projects/demo` would always answer 404. The child is keyed on the project's id and
  `pipelineRepo`, so a refetch resyncs the input; `SettingsForm`'s `key` (`:26-28`) does not change,
  because adding `pipelineRepo` to it would remount the whole form on this save and drop unsaved
  edits to the actor, the allowlist and the poll interval (`:85-91`). A save invalidates the
  doctor, projects and chain queries. The mobile guidance text of
  the card (`:146`, asserted by `scripts/test-mobile-navigation.mjs:84`) stays. `/api/projects` is
  outside viewer mode (`proxy.ts:57-61`), as the app's own settings are.

`scripts/test-pipeline-repo-ui.mjs`.

  invalid one dropped with a warning, and the value survives an unrelated write; `updateProject`

title: Build outbound links only to the allowed ticket host and GitHub owners
description:
## What changes for the user
Today nothing decides where a link from Houston may point. Once this lands a ticket link is used only when it points exactly at the configured ticket host over HTTPS, pipeline links are built only for allowed GitHub owners, and anything else is shown as plain text.

## Outcome
`lib/outbound-links.ts`, pure, builds or vets ticket, pull-request, run and change links by the rules below; a pure table test proves every refusal.

## Context
Critical because a wrong answer is a link to an arbitrary host opened from the user's work tool. The host, owner and repository rules come from `lib/config-values.ts`, added by the config-keys bead.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`,
  `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py`; pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- This phase builds the chain: from a bead to the work-tracker story or ticket its `external_ref`
  names, the epic it belongs to, the beads under an epic, and the delivery pipeline of the project's
  repository, read from a snapshot file a local collector writes on the work machine. The phase's
  plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries everything it needs from it.

## Preconditions of this phase

- The phase 1 beads that "Order and size" names land before the steps that use them. This phase
  uses phase 1's config machinery (step 2: typed keys validated on read with a warning, an atomic
  write, a key cleared through the config route removed from the file), its capabilities route
  (step 3), its capabilities client and hook (step 5, `lib/api-client.ts` and
  `hooks/use-capabilities.ts`), and its doc-link checker (step 7, `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`).
- Read before writing routes: `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md`
  and `.../03-file-conventions/dynamic-routes.md`. Route params are a `Promise` and are awaited.
- Pure test modules load through a TypeScript-transpile-then-`vm` loader built on the one of
  `scripts/test-epic-descendants.mjs:12-23`, which resolves `./name` to `lib/name.ts` and
  anything else through `require`, with `esModuleInterop: true` added as
  `scripts/test-sprints.mjs:19` has it: without it, `import fs from "node:fs"` (`lib/bd.ts:3`,
  `lib/config.ts:2`) compiles to `node_fs_1.default`, which is `undefined` for a Node built-in. So a
  new module under `lib/` that a pure test loads imports other `lib/` modules by a relative `./`
  path, never through the `@/` alias and never `server-only`. Scripts that load `lib/config.ts`
  use the child-process loader phase 1 defines ("Two facts every config test needs" in its plan:
  `esModuleInterop: true`, `console` and `URL` in the sandbox, the test re-executing itself
  through `process.argv[1]` with an environment variable naming the case, so no helper file lands
  under `scripts/`, in a throwaway working directory with `BEADS_REPO` removed, never a bare
  `import()` of `lib/config.ts`, because Node refuses its extensionless relative imports).
- Every fixture is synthetic: numbers like `INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`;
  repositories `org/repo-a`; the instance `example.com`.
- The repository is public and each branch is pushed on its own, so the internal-name sweep runs
  before every branch's first push, over that branch's diff and commit messages, with the list of
  names kept in the user's private notes outside the repository, as in phase 1. A failed or
  unavailable sweep blocks the push; the bead records only that it passed. Step 10 runs it once
  more over the whole phase.
- Every step ends with what proves it, including one guard broken on purpose (`AGENTS.md`,
  "Landing work"), whose red assertion the bead's close reason names. Server-backed and browser
  guards are broken through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after the last one); pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node scripts/<test>.mjs`, because that tool always
  builds and starts a server, and a mutant that breaks the server's start would be reported as
  caught without the pure assertion ever running.

## Specification
A new pure module, `lib/outbound-links.ts`, importing only `./config-values`, so the host, owner
and repository rules are the ones of steps 3 and 5.

- A ticket record carries its own link. It is used, as the parser's canonical `href`, only when
  the raw string has no whitespace anywhere, no control character (`0x00`-`0x1f`, `0x7f`) and no
  backslash; it starts with a literal `https://` whose authority, up to the first `/`, `?` or `#`,
  is a host name with no `@` and at most a `:` followed by digits; it parses as `https:`;
  `serviceNowHost` is valid and equals the URL's host name exactly; the user name and password are
  empty; and the URL's `port` is empty, which the parser also yields for an explicit `:443`. The
  parser silently repairs `https://@example.com/`, `https:@example.com/`, `https:///example.com/`
  and `https://example.com:/` into `https://example.com/` (checked on Node v24.18.0), so only the
  raw-string rule refuses them; an `@` in the path or the query stays allowed.
- A pipeline run or pull request carries no link. One is built from a repository that passes the
  `pipelineRepo` rule and whose owner is in `githubOrgs`, and a positive safe integer id:
  `https://github.com/<owner>/<name>/pull/<number>` or `.../actions/runs/<id>`.
- A change number from a run's `changes` links to its record in the changes source when the
  record is there, matched trimmed and without regard to case as `lookupTicket` matches, through
  the ticket rule; if that record's own link fails the rule, there is no
  link. Only when no record of that number is in the changes source, and the trimmed number has
  the ticket-number shape, is the standard change form on a valid `serviceNowHost` built
  (provisional decisions 3 and 4).
- `serviceNowHost` or `githubOrgs` unset, or a value that fails its rule: no link, and the
  identifier is shown as plain text.

Proof: a new pure script, `scripts/test-outbound-links.mjs`, with a refused case for each rule
(`http:`, another host, `https://example.com./`, `:8443`, user information, `https://@example.com/`,
`https:@example.com/`, `https:///example.com/`, `https://example.com:/`, a space inside, a
backslash, a leading space, a tab, a NUL, an uppercase repository, `org/..`, an owner outside the
list, `serviceNowHost` and `githubOrgs` each unset and each invalid, `0`, `-1`, `1.5`, `NaN`,
`2**53`, a change record whose link fails, a malformed fallback number such as `CHG1?x=1`) and an
accepted case for each kind, including `https://example.com:443/`, a link with an `@` in its
query, a change found in the changes source linking to the record's own link, and a change absent
from it getting the standard change form. Broken on purpose: accepting `http:` turns it red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `node scripts/test-outbound-links.mjs` exits 0 with a refused case for each rule and an accepted case for each link kind listed in the Specification.
- [ ] Accepting an http link turns a named assertion red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: no link outside the allowed host and owners can be produced, proven case by case.


## Tests
- unit: `scripts/test-outbound-links.mjs`, a pure table test.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `lib/outbound-links.ts`, `scripts/test-outbound-links.mjs`
**Reads only:** `lib/config-values.ts`

One new module and its test. Size S.
close_reason: lib/outbound-links.ts builds every outbound link of the chain: a ticket record's own link only when its raw string passes the raw-shape rule (no whitespace, control character or backslash, a literal https:// with a plain host authority) and it parses as https on exactly serviceNowHost with no user information or port; pull request and run links only for a pipelineRepo-valid repository under an allowed GitHub owner with a positive safe integer id; a change through its record's own link, or the standard change form only when no record exists and the number has the ticket shape; nothing when a setting is unset or invalid. Accepting http failed 'http: ticket link: a link is https'; every refused case and accepted kind is a named assertion (two parser-checked conditions are equivalent mutants behind the raw-shape rule). Review breaks: a failing record link falling back to the standard form failed 'change whose record link is http, never falling back', a case-sensitive record match failed 'change found in the changes source'. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build and test-outbound-links pass.

title: Resolve a bead's chain: tracker item, epic or descendants, and pipeline state
description:
## What changes for the user

## Outcome
`lib/chain.ts`, pure, takes a bead, its project's beads, the project, the snapshot and the link settings, and returns the chain of the Specification; a pure test proves each state with beads whose hierarchy is in dependency edges only.

## Context
Critical because every wrong state is silent: a pipeline reported absent while a collection issue was present would hide a failed run.   write, a key cleared through the config route removed from the file), its capabilities route
  (step 3), its capabilities client and hook (step 5, `lib/api-client.ts` and
  `hooks/use-capabilities.ts`), and its doc-link checker (step 7, `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`).
- Read before writing routes: `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md`
  and `.../03-file-conventions/dynamic-routes.md`. Route params are a `Promise` and are awaited.
- Pure test modules load through a TypeScript-transpile-then-`vm` loader built on the one of
  `scripts/test-epic-descendants.mjs:12-23`, which resolves `./name` to `lib/name.ts` and
  anything else through `require`, with `esModuleInterop: true` added as
  `scripts/test-sprints.mjs:19` has it: without it, `import fs from "node:fs"` (`lib/bd.ts:3`,

  use the child-process loader phase 1 defines ("Two facts every config test needs" in its plan:
  `esModuleInterop: true`, `console` and `URL` in the sandbox, the test re-executing itself
  through `process.argv[1]` with an environment variable naming the case, so no helper file lands
  under `scripts/`, in a throwaway working directory with `BEADS_REPO` removed, never a bare
  `import()` of `lib/config.ts`, because Node refuses its extensionless relative imports).

  before every branch's first push, over that branch's diff and commit messages, with the list of
