  builds and starts a server, and a mutant that breaks the server's start would be reported as
  caught without the pure assertion ever running.

## Specification
A new pure module, `lib/chain.ts`. It imports `./snapshot-format`, `./outbound-links`, and from
`./beads-view` `descendantsOf` (`lib/beads-view.ts:237`), `makeIndex` (`:159`) and `parentOf`
(`:205`), with types from `./schema`. The enclosing-epic walk follows `parent-child` edges through
`parentOf`, never `bead.parent`, which `bd` does not export: walking `bead.parent` would return no
epic for every bead of a real tracker.

Input: the bead, every bead of its project, the project as the structural type
`{ id: string; pipelineRepo?: string }`, which both `ProjectEntry` and `DemoProject` satisfy (the
demo has no `pipelineRepo`), so the module imports nothing from `lib/config.ts` and its
`server-only`; the snapshot or its unavailability; and the link settings. Output, as JSON, with
camelCase keys throughout, so `docs/chain.md`, the client and phase 3's command read one shape:

- `bead`: `{ id, projectId, type, status, title, externalRef? }`, `type` being the bead's
  `issue_type` and `externalRef` its trimmed `external_ref`, left out when that is absent, `null`
  or blank;
- `tracker`: the item its `externalRef` names, or `null` when it has none (no lookup is made);
- for an epic only, `descendants`: every bead under it at any depth, each
  `{ id, type, status, title, externalRef?, tracker }`, `tracker` being a tracker item or `null`
  as above;
- for any other bead only, `epic`: the nearest enclosing epic,
  `{ id, status, title, externalRef?, tracker }`, or `null` when there is none; the walk starts with
  the bead itself marked visited and stops at a bead already visited, so a bead that is its own
  parent ends it too;
- `pipeline`, only when the project has a `pipelineRepo`:
  `{ state: "found", freshness, lastConfirmedAt?, runs, prs, issues, changes }`,
  `{ state: "absent" }`, or `{ state: "unconfirmed", reason, issues? }`:
  - `runs`: `{ id, createdAt, status, conclusion, head, link, existingPrs: { number, link }[] }`,
    those whose `repo` is the project's `pipelineRepo`, newest first (`created_at` compared with `<`
    and `>`, not with a locale, then `id`, descending);
  - `prs`: `{ number, base, head, anomalies, link }`, those whose `repo` is the project's, by
    `number` descending, which within one repository follows creation time;
  - `issues`: `{ part, repo?, runId?, error?, limit? }`, the budget issue and those whose `repo` is
    the project's, `runId` left out when null or absent;
  - `changes`: `{ number, link }[]`, from this repository's runs in the order above, trimmed, blanks
    dropped, de-duplicated without regard to case, keeping the first spelling met (the collector
    writes them as `CHG` and digits, `evidence/Derived rules.md:143`);
  - each `link` is built by step 6, or null. With the snapshot unavailable, the pipeline is
    `{ state: "unconfirmed", reason }`;
- `snapshot`: `{ available, reason? }`.

A tracker item is one of:

- `{ state: "found", freshness, source, number, title, status, sprint?, link, lastConfirmedAt?,
  approvals }`, where `status` is the snapshot record's `state` field, `sprint` is left out when
  empty, and `link` passed step 6 (or is null);
- `{ state: "absent", approvals }`;
- `{ state: "unconfirmed", reason, approvals }`.

Each approval is `{ number, title, recordType, state, link, freshness, lastConfirmedAt? }`, with the
freshness of the `approvals` source and a link that passed step 6. Everywhere, `lastConfirmedAt` is
present only when the freshness is `historical`: never for `confirmed`, and never for a pipeline
that an issue made `partial` although its envelope has a `last_success_at`. So a story known only through a
pending approval, or another team's change waiting for the user's approval, is an absent or
unconfirmed item that still carries the approval.

`reason` is deterministic: the snapshot's unavailability reason when it is unavailable; otherwise,
for a ticket, the ticket sources that are not `ok` and complete, in the fixed order of step 4,
with their effective status; for the
pipeline, the pipeline envelope's effective status and its error when that is a non-empty string
(never the text "null" or an empty clause), or the collection or budget issue that made it
unconfirmed.

The pipeline state, from the direction plan's rule:

- runs or pull requests present, together with a collection issue for the repository or the
  budget issue: found, `partial`, and the issues shown;
- runs or pull requests present otherwise: found, with the pipeline source's freshness;
- none present, with such an issue, or with a pipeline source that is not `ok` and complete:
  `unconfirmed`, never `absent`;
- none present and the source `ok` and complete: `absent`.

Phase 3 adds a `notes` part to this output; nothing here depends on it.

Proof: a new pure script, `scripts/test-chain.mjs`, over the fixture of step 4 and synthetic beads
whose hierarchy is in `parent-child` edges only, with no `parent` field: an epic with descendants
two levels deep; a task whose epic is two levels up; a bead that is its own parent and a
three-bead parent cycle, each ending the walk; a pipeline envelope in `error` with `error: null`
whose reason names the status without "null"; a bead with
a blank reference and no lookup; each tracker state; each pipeline state, including the budget
issue and a `partial` pipeline without `lastConfirmedAt`; a second repository's runs, pull
requests, changes and repository issue left out without changing the first repository's state; run and pull-request order; a project without `pipelineRepo`, and the demo, have no pipeline
part; an unavailable snapshot makes every item unconfirmed with its reason; a story known only
through a pending approval. Broken on purpose: reporting `absent` when an issue is present turns its
case red; walking `bead.parent` turns the two-levels-up case red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `node scripts/test-chain.mjs` exits 0 with every case of the Specification, over the snapshot fixture and synthetic beads with no parent field.
- [ ] Reporting absent while an issue is present, and walking the parent field instead of the edge, each turn a named assertion red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: the chain of an epic and of a task two levels under it carry the states of the Specification, proven over the fixture.


## Tests
- unit: `scripts/test-chain.mjs`, pure.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `lib/chain.ts`, `scripts/test-chain.mjs`
**Reads only:** `lib/snapshot-format.ts`, `lib/outbound-links.ts`, `lib/beads-view.ts`, `lib/schema.ts`, `scripts/fixtures/snapshot-v1.json`

One new module and its test. Size L by the logic, not the file count.

  `scripts/test-epic-descendants.mjs:12-23`, which resolves `./name` to `lib/name.ts` and
  anything else through `require`, with `esModuleInterop: true` added as
  `scripts/test-sprints.mjs:19` has it: without it, `import fs from "node:fs"` (`lib/bd.ts:3`,
  `lib/config.ts:2`) compiles to `node_fs_1.default`, which is `undefined` for a Node built-in. So a
  new module under `lib/` that a pure test loads imports other `lib/` modules by a relative `./`
  path, never through the `@/` alias and never `server-only`. Scripts that load `lib/config.ts`
  use the child-process loader phase 1 defines ("Two facts every config test needs" in its plan:
  `esModuleInterop: true`, `console` and `URL` in the sandbox, the test re-executing itself
  through `process.argv[1]` with an environment variable naming the case, so no helper file lands
  under `scripts/`, in a throwaway working directory with `BEADS_REPO` removed, never a bare
  `import()` of `lib/config.ts`, because Node refuses its extensionless relative imports).
- Every fixture is synthetic: numbers like `INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`;
  repositories `org/repo-a`; the instance `example.com`.
- The repository is public and each branch is pushed on its own, so the internal-name sweep runs
  before every branch's first push, over that branch's diff and commit messages, with the list of
  names kept in the user's private notes outside the repository, as in phase 1. A failed or
  unavailable sweep blocks the push; the bead records only that it passed. Step 10 runs it once
  more over the whole phase.
- Every step ends with what proves it, including one guard broken on purpose (`AGENTS.md`,
  "Landing work"), whose red assertion the bead's close reason names. Server-backed and browser
  guards are broken through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after the last one); pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node scripts/<test>.mjs`, because that tool always
  builds and starts a server, and a mutant that breaks the server's start would be reported as
  caught without the pure assertion ever running.

## Specification
- `GET /api/p/[projectId]/beads/[id]/chain`: the project's store lists its beads (the chain needs
  the descendants and the parents), then the resolver. An unknown project or bead answers 404. It
  awaits `params` as the read routes do (`app/api/p/[projectId]/activity/route.ts:7,13`).
- `GET /api/links/[id]`, for agents, who know an identifier and not a project. It answers
  `{ id, snapshot, ticket, beads, unreadable }`, from one `readSnapshot()` per request, passed to
  the ticket lookup and to every matched bead's chain, so a rewrite during the request never
  splits one answer across two snapshots:
  - `id` is the identifier, trimmed, at most 128 characters, non-blank and free of ASCII control
    characters, as a reference is (step 1); anything else answers 400;
  - `unreadable`: every registered project is read in parallel, each bounded by the per-project
    limit `lib/all-projects.ts` already uses (`PROJECT_READ_LIMIT_MS`, 15 s, `:15,44-50`). That
    module keeps its bounded reader private (`failureText`, `:38-42`; `withLimit` and `readOne`,
    `:44-66`) and its exported `readAllProjects` (`:72-90`) takes only `{ id, name }` and namespaces
    every bead id, so a generic `readProjects<T extends ProjectRef>` is extracted and exported,
    returning each project's entry, of the caller's type, with its local bead ids, which
    `readAllProjects` then namespaces. It adds no runtime import, so the loader of
    `scripts/test-all-projects.mjs:15-23`, which stubs only `server-only`, `./store` and
    `./beads-watch` (`:78`), still loads the module. A project that throws or times out is
    listed with its id, name and error, so "no bead" is never confused with "could not look", and
    one stuck tracker never hangs the answer;
  - `beads`: at most one entry for every bead whose id is the identifier or whose `external_ref`
    matches it, both trimmed and compared without regard to case, in every project, each
    `{ projectId, projectName, chain }`, so `houston links` needs no second request;
  - `ticket`: the identifier itself as a tracker item of step 7, with links checked by step 6, and
    `{ state: "unconfirmed", reason, approvals: [] }` when the snapshot is unavailable; returned
    even when no bead carries the identifier;
  - `snapshot`: `{ available, reason? }`.
- Both are reads, so viewer mode leaves them alone (`proxy.ts:57-62`). Every answer of both,
  400 and 404 included, carries `Cache-Control: no-store`, set on the `NextResponse` as
  `app/api/viewer-mode/route.ts:7,10-12` does: `ok()` and `fail()` set no such header
  (`lib/api.ts:7-45`), so copying the activity route as it stands would drop it.
- `docs/chain.md` describes both answers field by field, naming no file that step 9 adds, so the
  doc checker stays green at this step. Phase 3's `houston links` command is a client of the second
  one.

Proof: a new server-backed script, `scripts/test-chain-routes.mjs`, skipped when `br` is not
installed. It creates two throwaway `br` trackers with the `br` CLI in temporary directories (an
epic with a story reference, a child, a grandchild task with a task reference; a second tracker
with an epic carrying the same story reference), registers both through `POST /api/projects`, sets
`pipelineRepo`, points `snapshotPath` at a temporary copy of the fixture, and sets `serviceNowHost`
to `example.com` and `githubOrgs` to `["org"]`.

- The chain of the epic and of the grandchild have the shape and states of step 7, with their
  links; every answer of both routes, 400 and 404 included, carries `cache-control: no-store`.
- Rewriting the copy atomically (a temporary file and a rename) with a changed record: the next
  answer reflects it.
- Removing the copy: every snapshot item is unconfirmed.
- With `snapshotPath` cleared, `GET /api/links/STRY00000001` still answers 200, with
  `snapshot.available` false and the ticket unconfirmed; the chain of a demo bead
  (`/api/p/demo/beads/<id>/chain`) answers 200 with no `pipeline` part.
- `GET /api/links/STRY00000001`, and the lowercase `stry00000001`, return both epics; a bead id
  returns its bead; an incident number
  no bead carries returns the ticket and no bead. A third project, registered while its tracker is
  readable and then broken by deleting its `.beads/issues.jsonl` (`POST /api/projects` refuses a
  folder without `.beads`; `scripts/test-all-projects.mjs:210-212` does the same), is named under
  `unreadable`.
- An unknown project (`@all` included) and an unknown bead on the chain route answer 404; a
  129-character identifier, a whitespace-only one (`/api/links/%20%20`; a bare `/api/links/`
  matches no route and answers 404) and one holding a NUL (`%00`) on the links route answer 400.
- In `finally` it removes the three projects it registered, clears the keys (`snapshotPath: ""`,
  `serviceNowHost: ""`, `githubOrgs: null`) and deletes its directories.

The server registers its own checkout as a project when started with no project list
(`lib/config.ts:274-287`); the links route reads that tracker too. The test asserts only on its own
projects and uses identifiers no real tracker carries. It writes beads with the `br` CLI, not
through the API, so it passes under both launch modes. Broken on purpose, one at a time: leaving
failed projects out of `unreadable` turns the third-project case red; answering the chain route
through `ok()` turns its `cache-control` assertion red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `scripts/with-server.sh 3211 node scripts/test-chain-routes.mjs` exits 0, and again under `SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1`, with every case of the Specification.
- [ ] A project whose tracker breaks after registration is named under `unreadable`, and leaving failed projects out turns that case red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `node scripts/test-doc-links.mjs` passes with `docs/chain.md` added.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: a story number returns the epics that carry it in two projects, proven against real `br` trackers.


## Tests
- integration: `scripts/test-chain-routes.mjs`, server-backed, with throwaway `br` trackers made by the `br` CLI.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `app/api/p/[projectId]/beads/[id]/chain/route.ts`, `app/api/links/[id]/route.ts`, `lib/all-projects.ts`, `docs/chain.md`, `scripts/test-chain-routes.mjs`
**Reads only:** `lib/chain.ts`, `lib/snapshot.ts`, `lib/store.ts`, `lib/config.ts`, `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`, `scripts/test-all-projects.mjs`, `scripts/with-server.sh`

Two routes, one shared reader, one document and one test. Size M.

title: Show the related items in the bead drawer and in an expanded epic
description:
## What changes for the user
Today opening an epic shows its title and children and nothing about the story or the pipeline. Once this lands a "Relacionados" section in the drawer and in an expanded epic shows the story with its state, the epic or the descendants, the pipeline with its runs and changes, and pending approvals, each marked confirmed, historical, partial, outside the collected scope or unconfirmed.

## Outcome
A chain client call, a `use-chain` hook with cache invalidation on bead changes, a `chain-section` component in the drawer and the epic view (loaded only when an epic is expanded), and a browser test with fixtures.

## Context
The section is shown only when the chain is configured. On the all-projects page the epic's id is namespaced; the request takes the project and the local id from `projectOf` and `displayId`, never `splitId`, because a project's own bead id may contain a colon.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`,
  `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py`; pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- This phase builds the chain: from a bead to the work-tracker story or ticket its `external_ref`
  names, the epic it belongs to, the beads under an epic, and the delivery pipeline of the project's
  repository, read from a snapshot file a local collector writes on the work machine. The phase's
  plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries everything it needs from it.

## Preconditions of this phase

- The phase 1 beads that "Order and size" names land before the steps that use them. This phase
  uses phase 1's config machinery (step 2: typed keys validated on read with a warning, an atomic
  write, a key cleared through the config route removed from the file), its capabilities route
  (step 3), its capabilities client and hook (step 5, `lib/api-client.ts` and
  `hooks/use-capabilities.ts`), and its doc-link checker (step 7, `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`).
- Read before writing routes: `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md`
  and `.../03-file-conventions/dynamic-routes.md`. Route params are a `Promise` and are awaited.
- Pure test modules load through a TypeScript-transpile-then-`vm` loader built on the one of
  `scripts/test-epic-descendants.mjs:12-23`, which resolves `./name` to `lib/name.ts` and
  anything else through `require`, with `esModuleInterop: true` added as
  `scripts/test-sprints.mjs:19` has it: without it, `import fs from "node:fs"` (`lib/bd.ts:3`,
  `lib/config.ts:2`) compiles to `node_fs_1.default`, which is `undefined` for a Node built-in. So a
  new module under `lib/` that a pure test loads imports other `lib/` modules by a relative `./`
  path, never through the `@/` alias and never `server-only`. Scripts that load `lib/config.ts`
  use the child-process loader phase 1 defines ("Two facts every config test needs" in its plan:
  `esModuleInterop: true`, `console` and `URL` in the sandbox, the test re-executing itself
  through `process.argv[1]` with an environment variable naming the case, so no helper file lands
  under `scripts/`, in a throwaway working directory with `BEADS_REPO` removed, never a bare
  `import()` of `lib/config.ts`, because Node refuses its extensionless relative imports).
- Every fixture is synthetic: numbers like `INC00000001`, `STRY00000001`, `CHG00000001`;
  repositories `org/repo-a`; the instance `example.com`.
- The repository is public and each branch is pushed on its own, so the internal-name sweep runs
  before every branch's first push, over that branch's diff and commit messages, with the list of
  names kept in the user's private notes outside the repository, as in phase 1. A failed or
  unavailable sweep blocks the push; the bead records only that it passed. Step 10 runs it once
  more over the whole phase.
- Every step ends with what proves it, including one guard broken on purpose (`AGENTS.md`,
  "Landing work"), whose red assertion the bead's close reason names. Server-backed and browser
  guards are broken through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after the last one); pure-script
  guards are broken and run directly with `node scripts/<test>.mjs`, because that tool always
  builds and starts a server, and a mutant that breaks the server's start would be reported as
  caught without the pure assertion ever running.

## Specification
- `lib/api-client.ts` adds `chain(projectId, id, signal)`, calling the chain route of the
  project's base path, with the id through `encodeURIComponent` as the other bead calls do
  (`lib/api-client.ts:151-152`), and `{ cache: "no-store", signal }`.
- `hooks/use-chain.ts`: one TanStack Query read per bead, under the key
  `["chain", projectId, beadId]`, with `retry: false` (TanStack's three default retries would hold
  the error notice back about seven seconds, as phase 1 found for its own reads), passing
  TanStack's `signal`, enabled only when asked and never for the pseudo project `@all`.
  `mutationToast` (`hooks/use-beads.ts:109-126`) invalidates `["chain", String(key[1])]`, the
  project of the beads key it is given (`:119`); the `onSettled` of `useSetStatus`
  (`hooks/use-beads.ts:104-105`), which does not go through `mutationToast`, invalidates
  `["chain", String(ctx.key[1])]`, the project the write went to, never the page's `pageProject`
  (`:77`), which is `@all` for a card moved on `/all`; `useBeadsStream`
  (`hooks/use-beads-stream.ts:26-29`) invalidates `["chain", projectId]`; `useAllBeadsStream`
  (`hooks/use-all-beads.ts:25-27`) invalidates `["chain"]`. So saving a reference, changing a
  status (also on the demo, where no stream connects, `hooks/use-beads-stream.ts:19`), or a
  descendant changing refreshes an open section.
- `components/chain-section.tsx`, "Relacionados", with `lang="pt-BR"` on its root (provisional
  decision 1):
  - the tracker item (number, title, state, sprint, link) with its freshness in words
    ("confirmado", "histórico, confirmado em <data>", "parcial"), the date formatted in `pt-BR`
    with numeric fields (`day: "2-digit"`, `month: "2-digit"`, `year: "numeric"`, `hour` and
    `minute` `"2-digit"`), which gives `DD/MM/YYYY`, and shown as plain text when it does not parse
    (the existing date helpers, `lib/beads-view.ts:293-304`, format in `en-US` with a short month
    name, which in `pt-BR` would read "25 de nov. de 2026");
  - "fora do escopo coletado" for absent, never "fechado", because the collector only sees open
    items assigned to the user and the latest pipeline runs; "não confirmado" with the reason;
  - pending approvals (number, title, record type when non-empty, state) with their own freshness
    and link, in every tracker state;
  - the epic, for a bead, and the descendants, for an epic, each with its own tracker item's
    number, state, freshness and link when it has one, as read-only summary rows without
    `data-keyboard-bead-id`, so the keyboard layer (`hooks/use-app-keyboard.ts:10`,
    `scripts/test-keyboard.mjs:56-59`) does not take them for child cards (the drawer and the epic
    view already own the clickable and keyboard navigation, and on `/all` their ids differ);
  - the pipeline's own state in the same words (confirmed, historical with its date, partial,
    outside the collected scope, not confirmed with the reason), then its runs with their links and
    the links of their existing pull requests, its pull requests with their links and anomalies,
    its issues, in the found and the unconfirmed state alike, and its change numbers with their
    links;
  - a loading notice, an error notice with a retry, and a quiet notice, "Nenhum item ligado a este
    bead.", when a bead has no tracker item, no epic, an empty list of descendants, and no
    pipeline;
  - every external link opens in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Drawer: the section goes after "Links & attachments" (`components/bead-detail-drawer.tsx:766-771`)
  when the capabilities read says `chain`. On `/all` the drawer is already scoped to the real
  project (`components/project-scope.tsx:36-55`), so its project id is the bead's own.
- Epic view: inside an expanded epic (`components/epics-view.tsx:287-345`), when the capabilities
  read says `chain`, as in the drawer, and loaded only while the epic is expanded, never for every
  epic on mount. Without that gate, the browser scripts that expand an epic and answer an unknown
  request with `{}` (`scripts/test-epic-focus.mjs:44`, `scripts/test-project-chip.mjs:68`,
  `scripts/test-all-page-writes.mjs:136`) would feed that `{}` to the section. `EpicsView` takes
  `projectId` from `useApp()` beside the fields it reads today (`:55-63`). The target is
  `projectOf(e)?.id ?? projectId` and `displayId(e)` (`lib/aggregate.ts:92-100`), as the board and
  the list resolve it
  (`components/board/board.tsx:164`, `components/list-view.tsx:160`), and no request is made when
  that is still `@all`. Not `splitId`: a project's own bead id may contain a colon
  (`lib/aggregate.ts:59-60`), and `splitId` would misroute it on a project page.

Proof: a new browser script, `scripts/test-chain-ui.mjs`, with fixtures answering the chain route
and `GET /api/viewer-mode` answered `{ readOnly: false }`, so it passes under both launch modes:

- the drawer shows each tracker and pipeline state's wording, including a pending approval beside
  "fora do escopo coletado"; a `pt-BR` date checked against the `DD/MM/YYYY` pattern, so the test
  does not depend on the machine's time zone, and the plain text for a date that does not parse;
  `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` on every external link and no link where `link`
  is null; the epic's and each descendant's tracker item, an existing pull request's link, a pull
  request's anomalies, an approval's record type, and the issues of an unconfirmed pipeline; and
  the loading, error (with its retry) and empty notices;
- saving a reference in the drawer sends a new chain request, and so does changing the bead's
  status from the drawer;
- the epic view sends no chain request before an epic is expanded and one after, on a project page
  and on `/all`, where the request names the real project and the local id; a local id with a colon
  on a project page is requested whole, its colon encoded as `%3A` in the request path;
- with `chain` false in the capabilities answer, no section and no chain request, neither from the
  drawer nor from an expanded epic.

Broken on purpose, one at a time: loading on mount, instead of on expand, turns the request-count
case red; dropping the capabilities gate of the epic view turns the `chain: false` case red;
dropping `rel="noopener noreferrer"` turns the external-link case red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `scripts/with-server.sh 3211 node scripts/test-chain-ui.mjs` exits 0, and again under `SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1`, with every case of the Specification.
- [ ] `scripts/test-keyboard.mjs` still passes: the summary rows carry no keyboard bead id.
- [ ] Loading on mount instead of on expand turns the request-count case red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: opening an epic shows its story, its beads and its pipeline with a state each, proven with fixtures on a project page and on the all-projects page.


## Tests
- e2e: `scripts/test-chain-ui.mjs`, Playwright with fixtures for the chain route and the viewer mode.
- regression: `scripts/test-keyboard.mjs`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `lib/api-client.ts`, `hooks/use-chain.ts`, `hooks/use-beads.ts`, `hooks/use-beads-stream.ts`, `hooks/use-all-beads.ts`, `components/chain-section.tsx`, `components/bead-detail-drawer.tsx`, `components/epics-view.tsx`, `scripts/test-chain-ui.mjs`
**Reads only:** `lib/aggregate.ts`, `components/project-scope.tsx`, `lib/beads-view.ts`, `hooks/use-app-keyboard.ts`, `scripts/test-keyboard.mjs`, `scripts/with-server.sh`

A new component and hook, three hooks gaining one invalidation each, two components hosting the section, and one test. Size L.

title: Marker: the houston notes service is delivered in kernl
description:
## Outcome
The `houston` notes service and CLI are on the kernl repository's `master`, so the work machine can build
the binary and run the notes service's first run.

## Context
`br` links no dependency across two trackers, so this bead stands in for the kernl epic named in its
`external_ref`. It blocks only the first run on the work machine: the hub's own phase 3 beads build against
the service's pinned answers with stub services. It is closed when kernl's steps A1 to A12 are merged (the
thirteenth, the `links` verb, waits on Houston's own phase 2 and does not hold up the first run).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The children A1 to A12 of the kernl epic named in `external_ref` are closed.
- [ ] `br show` of each, run in the kernl tracker, reports the status closed with a close reason.
- [ ] Done when: `go build ./cmd/houston` succeeds on kernl's `master`.

## Tests

## Blast radius
No file is edited: this bead only records another tracker's state.

title: Phase 3: a notes engine of Houston's own, notes in the chain, search and Obsidian links
description:
## Outcome
Houston carries a notes engine of its own, a Go module in `notes/` copied from kernl, which builds the `houston` executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault without touching the synced folder more than it must, answers which notes cite an identifier and runs a ranked search with snippets, and a CLI for it. In the hub, an epic's "Relacionados" panel lists its planning, implementation and evidence notes, a search page finds any note in under a second, a result opens in Obsidian, and the notes database is copied once a day to a synced folder.

## Context
The third phase of the work hub. The user decided on 2026-11-25 that Houston is self-contained: the engine is copied from kernl, the user's own notes application, at commit `488fbbe` into `notes/` as a fork, and nothing is written in kernl's repository or tracker. The hub's steps build against the refs and search answers the engine pins, with stub services, and do not wait for the engine; only the first run on the work machine does. The plan, reviewed in three rounds and re-planned once for the copy, is kept outside the repository; each child carries what it needs from it.

## Success criteria
- [ ] The notes engine is a Go module of Houston's own, and a check keeps the left-out packages out — hou-oc5.10
- [ ] The notes config loads from file and environment and refuses unsafe serving, and the lock takes an explicit path — hou-oc5.11
- [ ] The notes routes run on the graph and the vault root alone, deletes going to the vault's trash — hou-oc5.12
- [ ] `houston serve` answers health during the first index and always shuts down cleanly — hou-oc5.13
- [ ] The service refuses browser and non-loopback requests — hou-oc5.14
- [ ] `houston preflight` reports what the first index would change, writing nothing — hou-oc5.15
- [ ] Identity, fences, placeholders and writes are safe on a synced vault — hou-oc5.16
- [ ] Notes declare kind and refs, and one route lists the notes citing identifiers — hou-oc5.17
- [ ] Search ranks, snippets, filters, pages and finds identifiers exactly — hou-oc5.18
- [ ] Wikilinks resolve the way Obsidian resolves them, in all three places — hou-oc5.19
- [ ] The engine is safe and ready on a large synced vault, and the measurement's decision is recorded — hou-oc5.20
- [ ] `houston` has the note, graph, health and search verbs, with kernl named in no message — hou-oc5.21
- [ ] `houston links` prints what the hub knows about an identifier — hou-oc5.22
- [ ] One install command builds the notes service and installs it beside the hub, and an update rebuilds it — hou-oc5.1
- [ ] The hub reaches the notes service through one client that degrades to unavailable — hou-oc5.2
- [ ] An epic's Relacionados panel lists its notes by kind, with the one-hop notes — hou-oc5.3
- [ ] A search page finds notes with ranked snippets, filters and paging — hou-oc5.4
- [ ] A note opens in Obsidian from search and from the panel — hou-oc5.5
- [ ] The documents describe notes in Houston — hou-oc5.6
- [ ] The whole local gate, the Go gate included, passes once against `main` with every step of the engine and the hub merged — hou-oc5.6
- [ ] The notes database is backed up once a day, seven copies kept — hou-oc5.23
- [ ] The notes service runs on the work vault — hou-oc5.7
- [ ] Search is measured against real questions — hou-oc5.8
- [ ] The work machine's placeholders and file limit are known — hou-oc5.9

## Closing
The epic closes when every child is closed and the run of the whole gate that hou-oc5.6 defines has passed against `main`; its closing comment answers each success criterion on one line, quoting the criterion's opening words, the child, and the evidence.

title: Build and install the notes service beside the hub, and document its first run
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the install script knows only the hub, and the update script rebuilds only the hub. Once this lands one install command also builds the notes service from this repository and installs it as a login agent with its vault, database, port and a raised open-file limit, an update rebuilds and restarts it too, and the setup guide walks through its first run on the work vault.

## Outcome

title: Copy the notes engine into a Go module of Houston's own, with its dependency check
description:
## What changes for the user
Today Houston has no notes engine of its own: the only one lives inside the user's other notes application, so showing notes in the hub would mean installing and updating that whole application on the work machine. Once this lands Houston's own repository carries the engine, builds and tests it by itself, and refuses any change that would drag the other application's unrelated parts back in.

## Outcome
`notes/` holds the Go module `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes` (`go 1.26`): kernl's notes engine as it is at commit `488fbbe5cd0d939ae92b92051ef2a88b0b3acdf5`, with its import paths rewritten and nothing else changed except one kernl-only test removed; a local `internal/config` with the two types the engine needs; a minimal `cmd/houston` that prints its usage; `notes/README.md` recording the provenance and `notes/LICENSE` the original MIT text. `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh` fails on any package the copy leaves out, `AGENTS.md` documents the Go gate, and `.gitignore` ignores a stray `notes/houston` binary.

## Context
The user decided on 2026-11-25 that Houston is self-contained: the engine is copied, not shared, and kernl (the user's own notes application, a separate Go repository) is not touched. A scratch copy of `488fbbe`, made the same way on Go 1.26.11, built, passed `go vet ./...`, and passed `go test ./...` in all 20 packages, about 10,700 lines of Go and 16,500 lines of tests, so the copy itself is scripted work. The reasoning is in the dependency check, which must match package paths up to a `/` boundary (so `internal/applog` is not mistaken for `internal/app`) and must fail when `go list` itself fails. Every later step of the engine runs that check, so a package left out today (kernl's application container, chat, dispatch, planning and the rest, which would bring its whole orchestrator back) can never return through a stray import.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead creates the notes module, the check script and the documentation of the Go gate; its own landing runs that gate for the first time.

## Facts verified for this step
Checked while the plan was written, on 2026-11-25.

- The package set of A1, checked 2026-11-25 with a scratch copy on Go 1.26.11 (Linux):
  `git archive 488fbbe` of `internal/graph` without `traverse`, `internal/vault` without
  `companion` and `layout`, `internal/logging`, and `internal/notes/{blocks,suggest,tags}.go` with
  their tests; import paths rewritten to `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes/internal/`; an
  `internal/config` holding only `ServerConfig` and `VaultConfig`; and `TestExampleConfigParses`
  removed. It builds, `go vet ./...` passes, and `go test ./...` passes in all 20 packages: about
  10,700 lines of Go and 16,500 lines of tests. `go mod tidy`, given kernl's versions, keeps
  fsnotify v1.10.1, uuid v1.6.0, yaml.v3 v3.0.1, modernc.org/sqlite v1.60.1 and pgregory.net/rapid
  v1.3.0, drops `github.com/hymkor/trash-go` and `golang.org/x/mod`, and writes `go 1.26.0`.
- Why each package is in or out, from the imports: `internal/vault` imports kernl's
  `internal/config` only for `VaultConfig` (`internal/vault/config.go:20,34,52,57`,
  `service.go:23,35`); `internal/notes/blocks.go:31,67` calls `SplitFrontmatter`, defined in
  `suggest.go:51`, so `suggest.go` comes along; `autosave.go` serves only kernl's save route
  (`internal/api/notes.go:122`) and `diff_parser.go` has no caller outside its package;
  `internal/graph/traverse` is imported by nothing in kernl outside its own tests;
  `internal/vault/layout` is imported only by `companion`, by kernl's project, task, bookmark and
  ingest handlers, by `internal/inbox`, `internal/bookmarks` and `cmd/kernl`.
- `internal/vault/config_test.go:84-145` (`TestExampleConfigParses` and its helpers) reads kernl's
  `kernl.yaml.example` through `config.Load`, which the copy has neither of.
- `github.com/hymkor/trash-go`, used by kernl's `DELETE /api/vault/file`
  (`internal/api/vault.go:461`), implements only the Linux FreeDesktop trash on every non-Windows system (`main_unix.go`,
  `//go:build !windows`): on macOS it moves files to `~/.local/share/Trash`, and a rename across
  volumes fails. The copy does not take it (A3).

## Reading the citations
- A path under `internal/` or `cmd/kernl/` with a line number is kernl at `488fbbe`, the copy's
  source. Paths under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/` and `docs/` are Houston's.
- In the copy, kernl's `internal/<package>/<file>` is `notes/internal/<package>/<file>`, with the
  same name and, until a step edits that file, the same line numbers, since the copy's rewrite of
  import paths keeps every line count. The one exception is `internal/vault/config_test.go` after
  line 84, where the copy removed a kernl-only test.
- kernl's `internal/api/<file>` is ported into `notes/internal/api/<file>`; `cmd/kernl/<file>` into
  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.
- A cited kernl path that the copy does not take (`internal/app`, `internal/planning`,
  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.
- Line numbers are starting points; the search or test named as proof is what decides.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A1. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A2** adds the notes config loader (`LoadNotes`, `ValidateForServe`) and the database lock with an explicit path (`notes/internal/graph/dbfile`).
- **A3** ports kernl's notes-side HTTP routes into `notes/internal/api`, written against the graph and the vault root.
- **A4** adds `houston serve`, which starts the server before the first index, and `houston health`.
- **B6** updates the README and the test guide, and defines the run of the whole gate that closes the phase's epic.

## Specification
`notes/` in the houston repository, with its own `go.mod` (module
`github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`, `go 1.26`), holding kernl's notes engine as it is at
`488fbbe5cd0d939ae92b92051ef2a88b0b3acdf5`.

- Copied with `git archive 488fbbe -- <paths>` from a clone of kernl and unpacked under `notes/`, so
  only the commit's tracked files come along and kernl's package paths are kept under that prefix:
  - `internal/graph` and its sub-packages `edges`, `nodes`, `relate`, `revisions`, `schema` (the
    migrations 0001 to 0008, 0005 skipped as in the source), `search`, `tags`, `testutil`,
    `internal/ids`, `internal/migrate` (with its `testdata`) and `internal/sqlite`: the store, every
    query the ported routes run, and the test substrate. Not `traverse`, which nothing imports.
  - `internal/vault` and its sub-packages `frontmatter` (with its `testdata`), `reconcile`, `watcher`
    and `wikilink`: the indexer. Not `companion` (kernl's companion notes for tasks, projects and
    bookmarks) nor `layout` (where kernl files those), which only kernl's other features import.
  - `internal/notes`: `blocks.go` (the prepend, insert and append of `POST /api/vault/append`),
    `suggest.go` (`blocks.go:31,67` calls its `SplitFrontmatter`), `tags.go` (`GET /api/notes/tags`)
    and their tests. Not `autosave.go` and `diff_parser.go`, which serve only kernl's editor.
  - `internal/logging`: the logger and the request middleware.
- Not copied: `internal/app`, `internal/chat`, `internal/dispatch`, `internal/epic`,
  `internal/session`, `internal/terminal`, `internal/backend`, `internal/approvals`,
  `internal/inbox`, `internal/ingest`, `internal/planning` (with `planning/linksuggest`),
  `internal/memory`, `internal/vault/companion`, `web`, and every other package of kernl. What the
  service needed from `internal/app` is replaced where it is used: the handlers are written against
  the graph and the vault config (A3), the lock takes an explicit path (A2).
- Replaced by a small local package: kernl's `internal/config` (its `config.go` alone is 504 lines
  of agent, orchestrator, inbox and planning settings) is imported by `internal/vault` only for
  `VaultConfig`. The copy's
  `internal/config/config.go` holds `ServerConfig` (kernl `config.go:120-127`) and `VaultConfig`
  with its `Enabled` method (`config.go:172-189`), as they are; A2 adds the loader beside them.
- Every import path `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/kernl/internal/` becomes
  `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes/internal/`. Nothing else in a copied file changes in this
  step except one removal: `TestExampleConfigParses` and its helpers
  (`internal/vault/config_test.go:84-145`), which read kernl's `kernl.yaml.example` through
  `config.Load`, with the `runtime` import (`:7`) they leave unused.
- `go.mod` requires the source's versions (fsnotify v1.10.1, uuid v1.6.0, yaml.v3 v3.0.1,
  modernc.org/sqlite v1.60.1, and pgregory.net/rapid v1.3.0 for the property tests); `go mod tidy`
  adds the indirect ones and writes `go 1.26.0`; `go.sum` is committed.
- Provenance: `notes/README.md` names the source, `https://github.com/gabrielassisxyz/kernl` at
  commit `488fbbe5cd0d939ae92b92051ef2a88b0b3acdf5`, gives the exact `git archive` and rewrite
  commands, lists the packages taken and left out with the reason for each, maps the paths as "How
  to read a citation" above does, and says that the copy is a fork whose fixes do not travel to
  kernl, nor kernl's to it. `notes/LICENSE` is kernl's MIT license text with its copyright lines,
  "Copyright (c) 2024 acartine (original engine: https://github.com/acartine/foolery)" and
  "Copyright (c) 2026 gabrielassisxyz (Kernl)".
- A minimal `notes/cmd/houston/main.go`: `help`, `--help` and `-h` print the usage; any other verb
  exits 2 with an unknown-command message. A4 adds the first real verbs. It exists in this step so
  the gate below has a binary to build and check from the first landing.
- The gate. `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh` runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston` inside `notes/` and
  fails, naming each offender, on any package of the module that is, or lies under, `internal/app`,
  `internal/chat`, `internal/dispatch`, `internal/epic`, `internal/session`, `internal/terminal`,
  `internal/backend`, `internal/approvals`, `internal/inbox`, `internal/ingest`,
  `internal/planning`, `internal/memory`, `internal/vault/companion` or `web`, matched up to a `/`
  boundary; on any package of `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/kernl`; on
  `github.com/hymkor/trash-go`; and whenever `go list` itself fails. None of them exists in the
  copy; the check keeps it that way. `AGENTS.md` gains a section on `notes/` (this step owns that
  edit; B6 only adds test scripts to the lists that exist): it is a Go module copied from kernl (see
  `notes/README.md`), it needs Go 1.26 or later, and a change that touches `notes/` or the check
  script passes, besides the present gate, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and
  `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston` run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`. The
  "Landing work" gate bullet points at that section. `-o /dev/null` because a plain
  `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston`, which `.gitignore` gains for the same
  reason.

Proof: inside `notes/`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`
pass, `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh` passes, and the tree is clean afterwards; `diff -r` of the copy
against a fresh `git archive 488fbbe` of the same paths put through the same rewrite shows only the
removal named above and the new files (`go.mod`, `go.sum`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`,
`internal/config/config.go`, `cmd/houston/main.go`); `npm run lint` and `npm run build` still pass
with `notes/` in the tree; `houston help` exits 0 and an unknown verb exits 2. Broken on purpose: a
package `notes/internal/app` imported by `cmd/houston` makes the check fail naming it, and so does
an import of `github.com/hymkor/trash-go`, while a package named `notes/internal/applog` passes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Inside notes/, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` (every copied package) and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston` pass, and `git status` shows a clean tree afterwards.

title: Add the notes config loader and a database lock with an explicit path
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the copied engine cannot be configured on its own, and kernl keeps its database inside the synced vault, where a live database file and its write-ahead log ride the sync. Once this lands the notes service reads its vault, address and database path from a small config file of its own or from environment variables, keeps the database outside the vault, refuses to serve from an empty vault or on a network interface, and refuses to start twice on one database with a message that says how to fix it.

## Outcome
`notes/internal/graph/dbfile` has `Acquire(dbPath)`, kernl's lock with an explicit path, which creates the database's directory first and names `houston serve` in its contention message; `notes/internal/config` has `NotesConfig`, `LoadNotes` and `ValidateForServe` with the defaults, overrides, home expansion and refusals of the Specification, each covered by a table test.

## Context
In kernl the lock and the database path come from its application container, which the copy does not take, and the database sits inside the vault. Here the path comes from config, by default under the user's state directory, outside the vault; `sqlite.Open` does not create directories, so on a fresh machine the lock must. The loader reads only the three sections the notes service needs, so a file with other sections still loads, and an exported empty variable changes nothing. The command that calls all of this, `houston serve`, comes with the next step of the engine; this bead provides the pieces and their tests.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead works inside the notes module, so the Go gate applies to it.

## Facts verified for this step
Checked while the plan was written, on 2026-11-25.

- `vault.New` needs `vault.ApplyDefaults` first (`cmd/kernl/serve.go:316`): with `MoveWindowMs`
  zero, the flush ticker (`internal/vault/service.go:185`) is created with a zero duration, which
  panics.
- In kernl the graph database lives inside the vault, `<root>/.kernl-graph.db`
  (`internal/app/app.go:185,194-226`), and its write-ahead log rides the sync. `sqlite.Open`
  (`internal/graph/internal/sqlite/sqlite.go:25`) does not create parent directories; kernl's
  `MkdirAll` is in `graphDBFilePath` (`internal/app/app.go:222`), which the copy does not take.

## Decisions this step follows
The user accepted these on 2026-11-25; the Specification cites them by number.

- **Provisional decision 1.** The notes service reads its config from `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/houston/notes.yaml`, beside the hub's `config.json`. Not `os.UserConfigDir`, which on macOS is `~/Library/Application Support`. Environment variables `HOUSTON_VAULT`, `HOUSTON_DB` and `HOUSTON_ADDR` override the file; `HOUSTON_ADDR` is `host:port` (a value with a scheme is refused with a hint to drop it, since `HOUSTON_HUB_URL` takes one), and the CLI prepends `http://`. An `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` that is not absolute is ignored, as the XDG specification says.
- **Provisional decision 2.** Its database defaults to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/houston/notes.db`, outside the vault, with a relative `XDG_STATE_HOME` ignored the same way. Accepted with a daily backup added (B7).

## Reading the citations
- A path under `internal/` or `cmd/kernl/` with a line number is kernl at `488fbbe`, the copy's
  source. Paths under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/` and `docs/` are Houston's.
- In the copy, kernl's `internal/<package>/<file>` is `notes/internal/<package>/<file>`, with the
  same name and, until a step edits that file, the same line numbers, since the copy's rewrite of
  import paths keeps every line count. The one exception is `internal/vault/config_test.go` after
  line 84, where the copy removed a kernl-only test.
- kernl's `internal/api/<file>` is ported into `notes/internal/api/<file>`; `cmd/kernl/<file>` into
  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.
- A cited kernl path that the copy does not take (`internal/app`, `internal/planning`,
  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.
- Line numbers are starting points; the search or test named as proof is what decides.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A2. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A1** copies kernl's notes engine into `notes/`, a Go module of Houston's own, and adds the dependency check `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh` and the Go gate.
- **A3** ports kernl's notes-side HTTP routes into `notes/internal/api`, written against the graph and the vault root.
- **B7** adds the daily backup of the notes database to a synced folder.

## Specification
The lock: `notes/internal/graph/dbfile` takes kernl's lock (`internal/app/lock.go`) with an explicit
path in place of kernl's config.

- `dbfile.Acquire(dbPath string)` returns a release function and creates the database's directory
  (`os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dbPath), 0o755)`) before opening `dbPath + ".lock"`, because
  `sqlite.Open` does not create it and the default directory does not exist on a fresh machine.
- Contention answers `GraphLockedError` (`lock.go:31-35`) with the path and the recorded pid. Its
  message names `houston serve` and gives a Fix line of its own (stop the other process, or point
  `db` or `HOUSTON_DB` at another file), in place of kernl's, which names `kernl serve` and points
  at kernl's `AGENTS.md` (`lock.go:168`).
- kernl's path helpers (`graphDBDir`, `graphDBFilePath`, `GraphDBPath`,
  `internal/app/app.go:185-243`) are not taken: the path comes from the config (provisional
  decision 2), never from the vault root. The tests of `lock_test.go` come along, the white-box ones
  of `isLockContention` and `readRecordedPID` (`:88-134`) included.

The config: in `notes/internal/config`, beside the two types A1 copied, `NotesConfig`
(`Vault VaultConfig`, `Server ServerConfig`, `DBPath string` from the YAML key `db`) and
`LoadNotes(path string) (*NotesConfig, error)`:

- a missing file (`os.ErrNotExist`) starts from zero values; a file that exists and does not parse
  is an error;
- it reads only `vault`, `server` and `db`, ignoring every other key;
- defaults: `server.host` `127.0.0.1`, `server.port` `3301`, `db` per provisional decision 2, with
  `XDG_STATE_HOME` used only when it is absolute, so the database never lands in the working
  directory. Vault defaults are applied by the caller through `vault.ApplyDefaults`
  (`internal/vault/config.go:20-27`), as kernl's serve does;
- then the overrides, each applied only when non-empty after trimming, so an exported empty
  variable changes nothing: `HOUSTON_VAULT`, `HOUSTON_DB`, and `HOUSTON_ADDR` parsed with
  `net.SplitHostPort`, with a non-empty host and a port between 1 and 65535, and a value
  containing `://` refused with the hint of provisional decision 1;
- then `~` is expanded in `vault.root` and `db` (`expandHomePath`, copied from kernl's
  `internal/config/config.go:459-493` without its kernl failure prefix), so a value from the file
  and one from an environment variable both expand, and each non-empty one is made absolute with
  `filepath.Abs` (never an empty one, which `Abs` would turn into the working directory). A
  relative root breaks the file routes: `filepath.Rel(root, fullPath)` in `POST /api/vault/file`
  (`internal/api/vault.go:223`) cannot relate a relative root to the absolute path
  `resolveVaultFilePath` returns (`notes.go:206-227`) and answers 500.

`NotesConfig.ValidateForServe()`, called by `houston serve` and `houston preflight` but not by the
client verbs, which only need the address:

- the server's host is loopback (`127.0.0.1`, `::1` or `localhost`) and its port between 1 and
  65535, so `:3301` or `0.0.0.0`, from the file or the environment, can never bind a network
  interface;
- an empty `vault.root` is an error (kernl's handlers fall back to `~/.kernl/vault`, vault.go:85
  and others; the ported ones never do, A3);
- a `db` inside or equal to `vault.root`, resolved with `filepath.Abs` and compared with
  `filepath.Rel` (never a string prefix, so `/vault-db` beside `/vault` is fine), is an error,
  because a live SQLite file with its write-ahead log does not belong in a synced folder.

Proof: `go test ./internal/graph/dbfile/...` covers the lock, a second lock refused with
`GraphLockedError`, the release, a missing parent directory created, and `houston serve` named in
the message. Table tests in `notes/internal/config` for each source and override, a malformed file,
a missing file, an unknown section ignored, `~` expansion from the file and from `HOUSTON_VAULT`, a
relative `HOUSTON_VAULT` stored absolute, an empty `HOUSTON_VAULT` and a blank `HOUSTON_DB` ignored,
a relative `XDG_STATE_HOME` ignored, an invalid `HOUSTON_ADDR`,
`HOUSTON_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:3301` refused with the hint, `HOUSTON_ADDR=:3301` and
`server.host: 0.0.0.0` refused for serving, the empty root, a database inside the vault, a sibling
path that only shares a prefix, and a relative path that resolves inside the vault. Broken on
purpose: dropping the `MkdirAll` turns the missing-directory case red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `go test ./internal/graph/dbfile/...` inside notes/ passes with the lock, a second lock refused with `GraphLockedError`, the release, a missing parent directory created, `houston serve` named in the message, and the ported white-box tests of `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock_test.go`.
- [ ] Table tests in `notes/internal/config/config_test.go` pass for every case listed under Proof in the Specification, from a malformed file to a relative path that resolves inside the vault.
- [ ] Dropping the `MkdirAll` turns the missing-directory case red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] The Go gate of "Rules for this work" passes: go vet, go test and go build of the houston command inside notes/, and the dependency check script.
- [ ] Done when: the notes config loads from its file and the environment with its defaults, refuses an empty vault, a database inside the vault and a non-loopback bind, and the lock creates its directory.

## Tests
- unit: `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock_test.go`, the lock, its release and its contention.
- unit: table tests in `notes/internal/config/config_test.go` for every source, override and refusal.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`, `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock_test.go`, `notes/internal/config/config.go`, `notes/internal/config/config_test.go`
**Reads only:** `notes/internal/vault/config.go`, `notes/internal/graph/internal/sqlite/sqlite.go`, and kernl's `internal/app/lock.go`, `internal/app/lock_test.go` and `internal/config/config.go` in the clone outside the repository, `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`

Four files in two packages of the notes module. Size M.
close_reason: notes/internal/graph/dbfile takes kernl's lock with an explicit path (creates the parent directory, GraphLockedError naming houston serve with its own Fix line, white-box tests ported); notes/internal/config gains NotesConfig, LoadNotes (missing file from zero values, defaults 127.0.0.1:3301 and the state-dir db, trimmed HOUSTON_VAULT/HOUSTON_DB/HOUSTON_ADDR overrides, scheme refused with the hint, ~ expansion and Abs on non-empty paths) and ValidateForServe (loopback only, port range, empty root, db inside the vault by filepath.Rel). Dropping the MkdirAll failed TestAcquireCreatesMissingParentDirectory. Review breaks all red: untrimmed HOUSTON_DB, relative XDG_STATE_HOME accepted, Abs on an empty root, ~ expansion skipped for the vault, port 0 accepted in HOUSTON_ADDR, the serve port check removed, a release that never unlocks. Internal-name sweep passed; go vet, go test, go build, check-notes-deps, lint and build pass.

Today the copied engine has no HTTP routes: in kernl every notes route hangs off the whole application, which the copy does not take. Once this lands the notes service can list, read, write, append to and delete notes, list the note index and the tag tree, search nodes and follow related nodes and edges, answering as kernl answers; a deleted note goes to the vault's own trash folder, where Obsidian keeps its deleted notes, instead of a trash path that does not work on macOS.

## Outcome
`notes/internal/api` registers the ported routes on an `http.ServeMux` from a small dependency struct (`Graph`, `VaultRoot`), refusing an empty root; the link-suggestion block, the companion collapse, the pin routes and the editor routes are left out as the Specification lists; kernl's tests of the ported routes pass against it, and new tests pin each change.

## Context
kernl's handlers take its whole application struct but read from it only the graph and the vault root (plus a link budget inside the suggestion block, which is not ported), so the port is a change of signature plus the removals listed below, each because the code it called is not copied. Critical because these routes write and delete files in the work vault and the CLI and the hub decode their answers: a path check lost in the port, or a delete that silently replaces a file already in the trash, loses notes without an error. Health keeps its three string fields, encoded from a map that the large-vault step can extend with readiness fields.

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or

## Facts verified for this step
Checked while the plan was written, on 2026-11-25.

- Why each package is in or out, from the imports: `internal/vault` imports kernl's
  `internal/config` only for `VaultConfig` (`internal/vault/config.go:20,34,52,57`,
  `service.go:23,35`); `internal/notes/blocks.go:31,67` calls `SplitFrontmatter`, defined in

  `internal/vault/layout` is imported only by `companion`, by kernl's project, task, bookmark and
  ingest handlers, by `internal/inbox`, `internal/bookmarks` and `cmd/kernl`.
- kernl's notes-side handlers take `*app.App` and read from it only `a.Graph` and
  `a.Config.Vault.Root`, plus `a.Config.Planning.LinkBudgetOrDefault()` inside the link-suggestion

## Decisions this step follows

  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.

  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A3. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A11** fixes the engine for large synced vaults, adds readiness to health, an index on revisions, the five-thousand-note measurement and opt-in pagination.
- **A12** ports kernl's notes-side CLI verbs into `houston` and adds `houston search`.

## Specification
A new package, `notes/internal/api`, ports kernl's notes-side handlers, written against the graph
and the vault root instead of `*app.App`: a dependency struct (`Graph *graph.Graph`,
`VaultRoot string`; A11 adds the vault service, for health) and one function that registers every
ported route on a `*http.ServeMux`, refusing an empty `VaultRoot`. kernl's handlers fall back to
`~/.kernl/vault` when the root is empty (vault.go:82-86,146-150,181-185,348-352,436-440); the port
does not.

Ported:

- health, `GET /api/health` (routes.go:62-76);
- node list, `GET /api/nodes` (chat.go:341-372, the only handler taken from `chat.go`);

- note index and tag tree: `GET /api/notes` (notes_index.go:51-75,161-205), `GET /api/notes/tags`
  (notes.go:23-31, through `notes.TagTree`);
- node search, `GET /api/nodes/search` (nodes_search.go:30-110);
- related, `GET /api/nodes/{id}/related` (nodes_related.go:23-60);
- edges, `GET /api/nodes/{id}/edges`, `GET /api/edges` (edges.go:46-219).

With them, the helpers they use: `vaultDisplayPath` (routes.go:80), `noteIDForPath` (vault.go:494),
`parseNoteTags` (vault.go:529), `resolveVaultFilePath` (notes.go:206-227), and a `writeJSON` and

Not ported, and left in kernl: `POST /api/notes/save` and its editor; `POST /api/notes/suggest` and
`POST /api/notes/apply-hunks`; `GET /api/plan/context`; the companion backfill routes; the pin
routes (`PATCH /api/notes/{id}`, `PATCH /api/notes/tags`). So nothing in the service writes pin
state; the copied `pinned` columns keep their defaults, and `GET /api/notes` still reads them.

  `vault_linksuggest_test.go`, `notes_apply_test.go`, and the save and suggest cases of
  `vault_path_traversal_test.go` (`:202-308`);

  `suggestions`, `accepted` and `rejected`; `DELETE /api/vault/file` with a directory and with a path

  sub-path is kept; registering with an empty `VaultRoot` is refused;
