title: Add houston serve and houston health, with the server up before the first index
description:
## What changes for the user
Today there is no command that starts the notes service. Once this lands `houston serve` starts it on the configured vault and address, answers health from the first second while the vault is still being indexed, and stops cleanly on Ctrl-C or a service stop, also in the middle of the first index, leaving no stale lock behind; `houston health` prints what a running service answers.

## Outcome
`notes/cmd/houston` dispatches `serve` and `health` with the global flags of the Specification; `serve` follows its seven-step start order and the shutdown it gives, with kernl's server timeouts and the logging and correlation middleware but no CORS middleware; an integration test proves the order and the shutdown.

## Context
It joins the config loader and the lock of the config step with the routes of the port step. kernl's own serve starts the vault service before the server and returns at once when the first index fails or is cancelled, skipping the shutdown; here the server listens first, so health answers during an index that takes minutes on a large vault, and every exit runs the same shutdown. This bead keeps `serve` in a file of its own, `notes/cmd/houston/serve.go`, beside `main.go`, and that is where the request guard of the next step wraps the handler chain. Health's readiness fields (whether indexing is finished, what was skipped) come with the large-vault step; here it answers its three fields.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead works inside the notes module, so the Go gate applies to it.

## Facts verified for this step
Checked while the plan was written, on 2026-11-25.

- `vault.New` needs `vault.ApplyDefaults` first (`cmd/kernl/serve.go:316`): with `MoveWindowMs`
  zero, the flush ticker (`internal/vault/service.go:185`) is created with a zero duration, which
  panics.

## Decisions this step follows
The user accepted these on 2026-11-25; the Specification cites them by number.

- **Provisional decision 1.** The notes service reads its config from `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/houston/notes.yaml`, beside the hub's `config.json`. Not `os.UserConfigDir`, which on macOS is `~/Library/Application Support`. Environment variables `HOUSTON_VAULT`, `HOUSTON_DB` and `HOUSTON_ADDR` override the file; `HOUSTON_ADDR` is `host:port` (a value with a scheme is refused with a hint to drop it, since `HOUSTON_HUB_URL` takes one), and the CLI prepends `http://`. An `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` that is not absolute is ignored, as the XDG specification says.

## Reading the citations
- A path under `internal/` or `cmd/kernl/` with a line number is kernl at `488fbbe`, the copy's
  source. Paths under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/` and `docs/` are Houston's.
- In the copy, kernl's `internal/<package>/<file>` is `notes/internal/<package>/<file>`, with the
  same name and, until a step edits that file, the same line numbers, since the copy's rewrite of
  import paths keeps every line count. The one exception is `internal/vault/config_test.go` after
  line 84, where the copy removed a kernl-only test.
- kernl's `internal/api/<file>` is ported into `notes/internal/api/<file>`; `cmd/kernl/<file>` into
  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.
- A cited kernl path that the copy does not take (`internal/app`, `internal/planning`,
  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.
- Line numbers are starting points; the search or test named as proof is what decides.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A4. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A1** copies kernl's notes engine into `notes/`, a Go module of Houston's own, and adds the dependency check `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh` and the Go gate.
- **A2** adds the notes config loader (`LoadNotes`, `ValidateForServe`) and the database lock with an explicit path (`notes/internal/graph/dbfile`).
- **A3** ports kernl's notes-side HTTP routes into `notes/internal/api`, written against the graph and the vault root.
- **A5** adds the request guard that refuses non-loopback hosts and requests made by a browser page.
- **A6** adds `houston preflight`, which reports what the first index would change and writes nothing.
- **A11** fixes the engine for large synced vaults, adds readiness to health, an index on revisions, the five-thousand-note measurement and opt-in pagination.
- **A12** ports kernl's notes-side CLI verbs into `houston` and adds `houston search`.
- **A13** adds `houston links`, a client of the hub's links route.

## Specification
`notes/cmd/houston/main.go` gains `serve` and `health`; `preflight` joins in A6, the client verbs in
A12 and `links` in A13. Global flags `--config` (default per provisional decision 1), `--server` for
the client verbs, `health` included (A12 gives its order of precedence), `--json`, and `--help`,
`-h` and `help`; `serve` also takes `--addr`. Logging through `internal/logging`, initialised from
`HOUSTON_LOG_LEVEL` (default `info`), and the request middleware kernl's router uses (timing,
logging and correlation, `internal/api/routes.go:52-54`), not its `corsMiddleware` (`:55`), since
the guard of A5 refuses every request that carries an `Origin`.

`serve`, in this order, following `cmd/kernl/serve.go:272-329`:

1. `config.LoadNotes`, `ValidateForServe`, `vault.ApplyDefaults(&cfg.Vault)`,
   `vault.Validate(cfg.Vault)`;
2. the lock of A2 on the notes database, released on exit;
3. `graph.Open`, closed on exit;
4. `vault.New(g, cfg.Vault)`, before the server, so health has a service to read from the first
   request (A11);
5. `net.Listen` on the configured address, and an `http.Server` with kernl's timeouts
   (`serve.go:257-263`) serving the routes of A3, in a goroutine, so health answers while the vault
   is indexed;
6. `Start(ctx)`. A SIGINT or SIGTERM during the first index ends it with the context's error, which
   is a clean stop, not a failure; any other error also runs the shutdown below before it is
   returned. kernl's serve returns at once instead (`serve.go:326-328`), skipping the server's
   shutdown;
7. on SIGINT or SIGTERM: stop the vault service, shut the server down with a timeout, close the
   graph, release the lock.

Proof: `houston serve` against a temporary vault and a database in a directory that does not exist
yet answers `GET /api/health` while the first index runs, and exits cleanly on SIGTERM, also when
the signal arrives during the first index, leaving no lock file held; `houston health` prints the
answer; A1's gate passes. Broken on purpose: starting the vault service before the server turns the
health-during-index case red, and returning on `Start`'s error without the shutdown turns the
SIGTERM-during-index case red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An integration test in `notes/cmd/houston/serve_test.go` starts `houston serve` against a temporary vault, with its database in a directory that does not exist yet: `GET /api/health` answers while the first index runs, SIGTERM ends it cleanly, also when the signal arrives during the first index, and no lock is held afterwards.
- [ ] `houston health` prints the answer of a running service.
- [ ] Starting the vault service before the server turns the health-during-index case red, and returning on `Start`'s error without the shutdown turns the SIGTERM-during-index case red, both recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] The Go gate of "Rules for this work" passes: go vet, go test and go build of the houston command inside notes/, and the dependency check script.
- [ ] Done when: `houston serve` answers health during the first index and always shuts down through the same path.

## Tests
- integration: `notes/cmd/houston/serve_test.go`, the service started against a temporary vault and stopped by signal, before and during the first index.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `notes/cmd/houston/main.go`, `notes/cmd/houston/serve.go`, `notes/cmd/houston/health.go`, `notes/cmd/houston/serve_test.go`
**Reads only:** `notes/internal/api/`, `notes/internal/config/config.go`, `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`, `notes/internal/vault/service.go`, `notes/internal/logging/`, and kernl's `cmd/kernl/serve.go` in the clone outside the repository, `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`

Four files of one command. Size M.
close_reason: houston serve loads and validates the notes config, takes the database lock, opens the graph, creates the vault service, listens and serves the A3 routes behind kernl's timing, logging and correlation middleware (no CORS), then starts the vault; a SIGINT or SIGTERM during the first index is a clean stop, and every exit runs one shutdown (stop the service, shut the server down, close the graph, release the lock). houston health prints a running service's answer; global --config, --server, --json, help. The integration test answers health during a held first index, stops cleanly on SIGTERM during it, and leaves no lock held. Starting the vault before the server failed TestServeAnswersHealthDuringFirstIndex; returning on Start's error without the shutdown failed TestServeSIGTERMDuringFirstIndexIsCleanStop. Review: a lock never released went red; dropping svc.Stop survives because the context cancellation already ends the service's goroutines; the in-use hint now names lsof, which macOS ships, instead of ss. Internal-name sweep passed; go vet, go test, go build, check-notes-deps, lint and build pass.

title: Refuse browser and non-loopback requests in the notes service
description:
## What changes for the user
Today a web page open in the browser could read the work vault through a host name that resolves to the machine, or write a note with a plain cross-site form post, because the notes service answers anyone who reaches its port. Once this lands it answers only the hub's server side and the command line, and every refused request is logged.

## Outcome
A middleware in `notes/cmd/houston/guard.go`, wrapping the mux inside the logging middleware, answers 403 to a non-loopback or malformed `Host` and to any request carrying an `Origin` or a `Sec-Fetch-Site` header, by the rules of the Specification, with a Go test per case.

## Context
Critical: a mistake either exposes the vault to any page in the browser or refuses the hub. The hub calls the service with Node's `fetch`, which sends `sec-fetch-mode: cors` and neither `Origin` nor `Sec-Fetch-Site` (checked on Node v24.18.0), so the guard refuses on the two headers a browser adds to a page's request and never looks at `Sec-Fetch-Mode`. The write routes never check `Content-Type`, so without this guard a cross-site form post reaches them. The guard is wired where `houston serve` builds its handler chain, `notes/cmd/houston/serve.go`, the file the serve step created (the plan's ordering section names `main.go` for this wiring; the serve step puts the chain in `serve.go`).

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead works inside the notes module, so the Go gate applies to it.

## Facts verified for this step
Checked while the plan was written, on 2026-11-25.

- Node's `fetch`, which the hub's server side uses, sends `sec-fetch-mode: cors` on every request
  and sends neither `Origin` nor `Sec-Fetch-Site` (checked 2026-11-25 with a local HTTP server on
  Node v24.18.0, GET and POST). So the notes service's guard (step A5) refuses on `Origin` and on
  `Sec-Fetch-Site`, which browsers send on requests from a page, and never on `Sec-Fetch-Mode`
  alone, or it would refuse the hub.

## Reading the citations
- A path under `internal/` or `cmd/kernl/` with a line number is kernl at `488fbbe`, the copy's
  source. Paths under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/` and `docs/` are Houston's.
- In the copy, kernl's `internal/<package>/<file>` is `notes/internal/<package>/<file>`, with the
  same name and, until a step edits that file, the same line numbers, since the copy's rewrite of
  import paths keeps every line count. The one exception is `internal/vault/config_test.go` after
  line 84, where the copy removed a kernl-only test.
- kernl's `internal/api/<file>` is ported into `notes/internal/api/<file>`; `cmd/kernl/<file>` into
  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.
- A cited kernl path that the copy does not take (`internal/app`, `internal/planning`,
  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.
- Line numbers are starting points; the search or test named as proof is what decides.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A5. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does.

## Specification
In `notes/cmd/houston`, wrapping the mux from the moment it exists, inside the logging and
correlation middleware so every refusal is logged: a middleware that refuses with 403

- a request whose `Host` is not loopback. `Host` is parsed with `net.SplitHostPort`, and when that
  succeeds the port must be an integer from 1 to 65535 (`SplitHostPort` accepts `127.0.0.1:abc` and
  `127.0.0.1:`); without a port, the bare host is taken as it is, brackets allowed only in `[::1]`.
  The host is compared without regard to case with `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` and `::1`, so
  `localhost.evil.example`, `127.0.0.1.nip.io` and `[127.0.0.1]` are refused, and so are an empty
  `Host` (HTTP/1.0) and a malformed one such as `[::1]evil` or `127.0.0.1:1:2`;
- a request that carries an `Origin` or a `Sec-Fetch-Site` header, checked by the key's presence
  (`len(r.Header.Values(...)) > 0`, never `Get(...) != ""`), so an empty `Origin:`,
  `Origin: null` and an `OPTIONS` preflight are refused too. These are the headers a browser adds
  to a request made by a page.

It does not look at `Sec-Fetch-Mode`, which Node's `fetch` sends (see "Facts verified"). Without
this guard, a page open in the browser could read the vault through a rebound host name, or write
a note with a plain cross-site request, because the write routes never look at `Content-Type`
(vault.go:203,374).

Proof: Go tests: a request shaped like Node's (only `sec-fetch-mode: cors`) passes; `Origin`
refused; `Origin: null` and an empty `Origin:` refused; `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` refused; an
`OPTIONS` preflight refused; `Host: evil.example`, `Host: localhost.evil.example`,
`Host: 127.0.0.1.nip.io:3301`, an empty `Host`, `[::1]evil`, `127.0.0.1:1:2`, `127.0.0.1:abc`,
`127.0.0.1:` and `[127.0.0.1]` refused; `Host: 127.0.0.1:3301`, `Host: localhost:3301`,
`Host: [::1]:3301` and `Host: 127.0.0.1` pass; a refused request leaves a log line. Broken on
purpose: a prefix match on the host turns the `localhost.evil.example` case red, and
`Get(...) != ""` turns the empty-`Origin` case red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Go tests in `notes/cmd/houston/guard_test.go` pass for every accepted and refused request listed under Proof in the Specification, and a refused request leaves a log line.
- [ ] A prefix match on the host turns the localhost.evil.example case red, and `Get(...) != ""` in place of the presence check turns the empty-Origin case red, both recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] A request through the handler chain `houston serve` builds, not only through the bare middleware, is refused for carrying an `Origin`.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] The Go gate of "Rules for this work" passes: go vet, go test and go build of the houston command inside notes/, and the dependency check script.
- [ ] Done when: every route of `houston serve` sits behind the guard and every case of the Specification is a named test.

## Tests
- unit: Go tests of the middleware, one per accepted and refused case.
- integration: one refused request through the full handler chain of `houston serve`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `notes/cmd/houston/guard.go`, `notes/cmd/houston/guard_test.go`, `notes/cmd/houston/serve.go`
**Reads only:** `notes/internal/api/vault.go`, `notes/internal/logging/`, `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`

title: Add houston preflight, which reports what the first index would change and writes nothing
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the first index of a vault rewrites every note that has no id, with no warning of what it will touch or of the notes it cannot handle. Once this lands `houston preflight` lists, without writing a byte, every note that will get an id, every id that is empty, malformed or shared by two files, every frontmatter that cannot be read, every unknown value, and every empty or non-text file a sync client may have left, and exits 0 only when nothing needs fixing.

## Outcome
`houston preflight` walks the vault with the reconciler's own parser and note-file helpers, prints one line per finding and a count per kind, exits 0 or 1 by the rule of the Specification, and with `--json` prints exactly one document; kernl's `exitcode.go` is ported so an already-reported failure prints nothing more.

## Context
It reports exactly what the reconciler would do because it uses the same code: the fence scanner and the top-level `id:` detection of the frontmatter-fixes step, which tells a missing id from an empty one, and the `kind`, `refs` and list parsing of the kind-and-refs step, which is why it runs after both. It is the first thing the setup guide has the user run on the work vault, before anything is written there. The other CLI verbs, ported in a later step, build on the exit-code file this bead ports.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead works inside the notes module, so the Go gate applies to it.

## Reading the citations
- A path under `internal/` or `cmd/kernl/` with a line number is kernl at `488fbbe`, the copy's
  source. Paths under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/` and `docs/` are Houston's.
- In the copy, kernl's `internal/<package>/<file>` is `notes/internal/<package>/<file>`, with the
  same name and, until a step edits that file, the same line numbers, since the copy's rewrite of
  import paths keeps every line count. The one exception is `internal/vault/config_test.go` after
  line 84, where the copy removed a kernl-only test.
- kernl's `internal/api/<file>` is ported into `notes/internal/api/<file>`; `cmd/kernl/<file>` into
  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.
- A cited kernl path that the copy does not take (`internal/app`, `internal/planning`,
  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.
- Line numbers are starting points; the search or test named as proof is what decides.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A6. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A7** fixes id injection, duplicate ids, fences, placeholders and in-place writes, and adds the leaf package `notes/internal/vault/vaultfile` with the atomic writer.
- **A8** adds the `kind` and `refs` frontmatter fields, the `note_refs` table and the refs route, GET /api/notes/refs.
- **A12** ports kernl's notes-side CLI verbs into `houston` and adds `houston search`.

## Specification
`houston preflight` walks the vault (skipping dot-files and dot-directories relative to the vault
root, as the cold start does) with the same frontmatter parser and note-file helper as the
reconciler, so it runs after A7 and A8. It writes nothing. Two kinds of finding:

- notices, which do not fail: no id (the file will get one on the first run); an id that is not a
  UUID (kept as it is by the reconciler, never matched as a UUID by wikilinks); a `kind` string
  that is not one of the four values, which A8 indexes as `nota` (`implementação`, with its
  accent, is one);
- errors: an empty `id:` line; an id shared by two files; frontmatter that cannot be parsed;
  `tags` or `refs` that are neither a scalar nor a list of scalars, or a `kind` that is not a
  scalar; a `permission` value the service does
  not know (known: `ask`, `edit`, reconcile.go:832-835); a file that is not valid UTF-8 text, or
  has zero bytes, which is what a sync client leaves as a placeholder. The reconciler of A7 skips
  both the same way.

The parser answers an empty id both for a missing `id:` key and for an empty one, so the
preflight tells them apart with A7's own detection of a top-level `id:` line, not a second rule.

Output: one line per finding and a count per kind; exit 0 when there is no error, 1 otherwise;
`--json` emits `{ "errors": n, "notices": n, "counts": {...}, "findings": [...] }`. On exit 1 the
verb signals an already-reported failure, so `main` writes nothing after the report, as kernl's
`main` does for `alreadyReported` (`cmd/kernl/main.go:52-58`, `cmd/kernl/exitcode.go:27-38`); an
ordinary error would make it print an error envelope after the report, two JSON documents on
stdout. This step ports `exitcode.go` into `notes/cmd/houston`, and A12 builds the other verbs on it.

Proof: Go tests over a `testdata` vault with one file per finding, asserting the report, the exit
code (a vault where every note only lacks an id exits 0), that `--json` with an error prints
exactly one JSON document, and that no file's bytes or modification time changed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Go tests in `notes/cmd/houston/preflight_test.go` over a fixture vault in `notes/cmd/houston/testdata/` pass with one file per finding of the Specification, asserting the report, the count per kind and the exit code, with a vault where every note only lacks an id exiting 0.
- [ ] With an error present, `--json` prints exactly one JSON document and nothing after it.
- [ ] No fixture file's bytes or modification time change during the test run.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] The Go gate of "Rules for this work" passes: go vet, go test and go build of the houston command inside notes/, and the dependency check script.
- [ ] Done when: preflight reports every finding of the Specification, exits by its rule, and writes nothing.

## Tests
- unit: Go tests over the fixture vault, one file per finding, the exit codes and the single JSON document.
- regression: the bytes and modification time of every fixture file, compared before and after.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `notes/cmd/houston/preflight.go`, `notes/cmd/houston/preflight_test.go`, `notes/cmd/houston/testdata/`, `notes/cmd/houston/exitcode.go`, `notes/cmd/houston/main.go`
**Reads only:** `notes/internal/vault/frontmatter/frontmatter.go`, `notes/internal/vault/vaultfile/`, `notes/internal/vault/reconcile/reconcile.go`, `notes/internal/vault/reconcile/coldstart.go`, `notes/internal/config/config.go`, and kernl's `cmd/kernl/main.go` and `cmd/kernl/exitcode.go` in the clone outside the repository, `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`

One new verb, its fixtures, the ported exit-code file and the verb's registration. Size M.
close_reason: houston preflight reads the configured vault and reports what the first index would change, writing nothing: missing, non-UUID, empty and duplicate ids, unknown and invalid kinds, invalid frontmatter, tags and refs, unknown permissions, empty and non-UTF-8 files, with a count per kind, a human report or exactly one JSON document, and an exit code by its rule (a vault whose notes only lack an id exits 0) through a shared exit-code dictionary. preflight_test.go runs over a fixture vault with one file per finding and checks every fixture's bytes and modification time before and after. Every finding's detection broken was red (13 rows, e.g. empty id read as missing failed TestPreflightReportsEveryFinding). Review: preflight rewriting the files it reads, same bytes or with a byte appended, failed TestPreflightWritesNothing. Internal-name sweep passed; go vet, go test, go build, check-notes-deps, lint and build pass.

title: Fix id injection, duplicate ids, fences, placeholders and in-place writes in the notes engine
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, on a synced vault, an empty `id:` line can make the service rewrite a note over and over, a sync client's conflict copy can steal a note's identity, a note replaced in place by another stays out of the index, a note with an unknown permission disappears and breaks the note list, a fence written with a trailing space gets a second frontmatter block, an empty placeholder left by a sync client gets frontmatter written into it, and every write happens in place, so a crash can leave a half-written note. Once this lands each of those is handled, and nothing the service writes into the vault is ever half-written.

## Outcome
The fixes of the Specification, in the reconciler, the injector, the five frontmatter fence sites and the vault file routes, with a new leaf package `notes/internal/vault/vaultfile` holding the fence scanner and the atomic writer; each fix has a Go test that fails on the copied code and passes now, and the duplicate, unknown-permission, invalid-UTF-8 and empty-file reports are kept by path for health and the preflight.

## Context
Critical because each defect corrupts or hides notes silently, and the first run on the work vault writes into thousands of notes. Each was verified by reading kernl's code at the copied commit, which the copy carries unchanged. The shared helpers go to a new leaf package that imports only the standard library, because the vault package imports the reconciler and the watcher, so a helper placed there would be an import cycle. The preflight verb and health's readiness fields, which read the reports this bead keeps, come in later steps.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead works inside the notes module, so the Go gate applies to it.

## Steps to Reproduce
Against `houston serve` on a temporary vault, with the copied code (line numbers are kernl's, see
"Reading the citations"):
1. Create a note whose frontmatter has an empty `id:` line, and watch the file: it is rewritten
   repeatedly (injector.go:78-83, reconcile.go:790-800).
2. Copy an indexed note to `00-conflict.md`, keeping its id, and restart: the copy takes the note's path
   (coldstart.go:158-162).
3. Replace an indexed note in place with a note carrying another id (`mv other.md note.md`): the upsert
   fails on the unique path and the file stays unindexed (reconcile.go:98-113).
4. Give a note `permission: readonly`: it is skipped with a log line and never indexed
   (reconcile.go:864-865, 898-900); and once one unknown value is stored, `GET /api/notes` answers 500
   for the whole index (notes_index.go:192-195).
5. Create a note without an id whose frontmatter opens with `--- ` (a trailing space): the injector
   prepends a second block instead of adding the id to the first (injector.go:56-58).
6. Truncate an indexed note to zero bytes: the service writes a frontmatter block into it
   (frontmatter.go:57-59, reconcile.go:796).

## Facts verified for this step
Checked while the plan was written, on 2026-11-25.

- `internal/vault/service.go:14-15` imports `internal/vault/reconcile` and
  `internal/vault/watcher`. So a helper those packages need cannot live in package `internal/vault`:
  it would be an import cycle. Shared helpers go to a leaf package, `internal/vault/vaultfile`.

## Reading the citations
- A path under `internal/` or `cmd/kernl/` with a line number is kernl at `488fbbe`, the copy's
  source. Paths under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/` and `docs/` are Houston's.
- In the copy, kernl's `internal/<package>/<file>` is `notes/internal/<package>/<file>`, with the
  same name and, until a step edits that file, the same line numbers, since the copy's rewrite of
  import paths keeps every line count. The one exception is `internal/vault/config_test.go` after
  line 84, where the copy removed a kernl-only test.
- kernl's `internal/api/<file>` is ported into `notes/internal/api/<file>`; `cmd/kernl/<file>` into
  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.
- A cited kernl path that the copy does not take (`internal/app`, `internal/planning`,
  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.
- Line numbers are starting points; the search or test named as proof is what decides.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A7. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A11** fixes the engine for large synced vaults, adds readiness to health, an index on revisions, the five-thousand-note measurement and opt-in pagination.

## Specification
A leaf package, `notes/internal/vault/vaultfile`, importing only the standard library, holds the
helpers the vault packages share: never package `internal/vault`, which imports `reconcile` and
`watcher` (an import cycle).

Each fix is a defect in kernl's code at `488fbbe`, and so in the copy, verified in the code:

- **Empty `id:` line.** `InjectID` returns the bytes unchanged (injector.go:78-83) while the
  reconciler records a new id and rewrites the file, which likely loops through the watcher. And
  its check, `strings.Contains(block, "\nid:")`, also matches an indented key or a comment. Fix:
  when the parsed id is empty and the block has a top-level `id:` line, at column 0, that line is
  replaced in place with `id: <uuid>`, keeping its line ending. Any value on that line is one the
  YAML parser read as empty: besides empty, `""`, `''`, `null` and `~`, also `NULL`, `Null`, and an
  inline `# comment`, all of which `yaml.v3` decodes to an empty string; and a second `id:` key
  prepended beside it would make the block fail to parse (`mapping key "id" already defined`),
  checked with yaml.v3 v3.0.1.
- **Two files with one id.** Nothing detects it; the last file processed wins and the other is
  silently unindexed (reconcile.go:698, coldstart.go:158-162,241-246). The walk is in lexical
  order, so a conflict copy that sorts first (`00-conflict.md` before `note.md`) takes the note's
  path today. Fix: in `ColdStart` (coldstart.go:158-162), in the live adopt (reconcile.go:562-567),
  and in `OnChange` (reconcile.go:722-777), which is where a live copy arrives, since the watcher
  emits a change and never a create (watcher.go:368-391) and `OnChange` today updates the node and
  points `note_paths` at the copy, a different path counts as a move only when the cached path no
  longer exists on disk; otherwise the existing path keeps the node and the newcomer is left out and
  reported as a duplicate, whatever the walk order. In `ColdStart`, a move also updates the walk's
  in-memory `byUUID` entry (coldstart.go:42-50), or a second copy later in the same walk would find
  the old path gone and take the node again. This holds in normal running, not only at the first
  index, because sync clients make conflict copies and templates get duplicated at any time.
- **A path taken over by another id.** `note_paths.path` is `UNIQUE` (0003_notes.up.sql:5) and
  `upsertInTx` resolves a conflict on `uuid` only (reconcile.go:98-113), so a file replaced in place
  by a note carrying another id (a `mv other.md note.md`, or a sync client's replacement) fails the
  upsert and stays unindexed for the run. Fix: before the upsert, a row at that path held by
  another id is removed and that id goes through the delete path, inside the move window, so it
  keeps its identity if its file shows up elsewhere.
- **Unknown `permission`.** Today the note is skipped with a log line (reconcile.go:864-865,
  898-900), and `GET /api/notes` answers 500 for the whole index when one stored value is unknown
  (notes_index.go:192-195). Fix: `noteFromFile` (reconcile.go:891), which today refuses the value
  through `ResolvePermission`, turns an unknown value into `ask`, the most restrictive known one,
  before it is stored, and reports it. `ResolvePermission` itself keeps refusing it, and so does
  `POST /api/vault/file` (vault.go:276), which calls it, since a writer can be told
  (`vault_write_status_test.go:91` pins the 400).
- **A fence followed by spaces.** Today an opening `--- ` makes the injector prepend a second
  block (injector.go:56-58, and in `InjectTags`, :137-161), a closing `--- ` is not a fence
  (frontmatter.go:105-110), and the closing loops of the injector (:69-75, :167-173) never look at
  what follows `---`, so a `----` line ends the block. Fix: one fence scanner in `vaultfile`: a
  fence line is `---` followed only by spaces or tabs before the line end (or the end of the file,
  for a closing fence), keeping a BOM and CRLF; used at the opening and the closing in
  `frontmatter.go:49-116`, `InjectID` (`injector.go:45-76`), `InjectTags` (`injector.go:137-178`),
  `reconcile.go:1080-1117` and `notes/suggest.go:51-67` (`SplitFrontmatter`, which the append
  route reaches through `blocks.go`), which today also breaks on CRLF and a BOM.
  It answers one of three states, no block, a closed block with its spans, or an opening fence never
  closed, because the sites treat the last differently and keep doing so: `frontmatter.go:80-84`
  refuses it (pinned by `testdata/malformed_unterminated.md`), while `reconcile.go:1080-1117` and
  `notes/suggest.go:56-58` read the whole file as body.
- **Empty file, and invalid UTF-8.** Today a zero-byte file gets a frontmatter block written into
  it (frontmatter.go:57-59, injector.go:45-47, reconcile.go:796), and `POST /api/vault/file` does the
  same to an empty body. Fix: the guard goes in the reconciler (`reconcileFile`, `OnCreate`,
  `OnChange`, before `parseAndInject`), not in `frontmatter.InjectID`, whose golden test
  (`internal/vault/frontmatter/testdata/empty_file.md`, `frontmatter_test.go:104-162`) pins injecting
  into empty bytes: a zero-byte file, or one that is not valid UTF-8, is not indexed and not written,
  and is reported. `POST /api/vault/file` creates directories (vault.go:198) before it reads the
  body (:203), injects the id (:262) and checks the permission (:276); the `MkdirAll` moves after
  every check, so a refused request leaves no directory behind. It refuses with 400, through
  `vaultFileWriteError` (`vault.go:74-78`, pinned by `vault_write_status_test.go:35-38`), a
  zero-byte body and a `.md` body that is not valid UTF-8, which the reconciler would never index,
  the orphan the permission check's comment warns against (vault.go:269-273). In `ColdStart`, a
  path skipped because it is empty, unreadable or malformed still marks its cached id as seen,
  looked up by path in a third map built from `note_paths` beside `byUUID` and `byHash`
  (coldstart.go:37-50), so the tombstone sweep (coldstart.go:90-106) does not delete a note whose
  file became a placeholder.
- **Writes in place.** Id injection (reconcile.go:796) and the two routes the CLI writes through
  (`POST /api/vault/file`, vault.go:283; `POST /api/vault/append`, vault.go:414) all use
  `os.WriteFile`. Fix: `vaultfile.WriteFileAtomic(path, data, defaultMode)`: a temporary file in
  the same directory, named `.houston-tmp-*` (a dot-file that does not end in `.md`, so no watcher,
  index, Obsidian or sync client takes it for a note), given the existing file's mode or
  `defaultMode` with an explicit `Chmod` (`os.CreateTemp` creates it `0600`), written, synced and
  closed, with the close's error checked, then renamed into place; removed on any failure. Every
  path of the service that writes into the vault uses it.

Health and the preflight keep the duplicate, unknown-permission, invalid-UTF-8 and empty-file
reports by path, so fixing or deleting a file clears its count. A skipped file has no `note_paths`
row, and `OnDelete` returns early for a path it does not know (reconcile.go:326-328), so the report
is cleared before that return; `OnDirDelete` (A11) clears the reports under its prefix, and
`ColdStart` drops the reports of paths it no longer finds.

Proof: Go tests for each, through the reconciler and through the routes, including: an empty `id:`,
`id: null`, `id: NULL`, `id: ~` and `id: # comment` get the id and a second event writes nothing; an
indented `  id:` is not mistaken for one; the duplicate stays out across a cold start and a live
change, a conflict copy that sorts first does not take the path, and neither does a second copy
after a genuine move in the same cold start; a file replaced in place by a note with another id is
indexed under the new id, and the displaced note is deleted after the window unless its file
appears elsewhere; an unknown permission indexes as `ask`, `GET /api/notes` still answers 200, and
`POST /api/vault/file` still refuses it; `--- ` fences on both sides, a `----` line inside the
block, CRLF and a BOM parse in all five sites, and an unterminated block keeps each site's present
answer; an empty file is untouched and an indexed note emptied by a placeholder survives a cold
start; a write refused for its permission, its id or its encoding leaves no new directory; deleting
a skipped file clears its count; the atomic writer keeps the mode, gives a new file `defaultMode`
and not `0600`, replaces the inode (`os.SameFile` is false afterwards), leaves no temporary file,
and leaves the original bytes untouched when a write or rename failure is injected. Broken on
purpose: writing in place again turns the inode and injected-failure cases red, and dropping the
`OnChange` check turns the live-copy case red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Go tests pass for every case listed under Proof in the Specification, through the reconciler in `notes/internal/vault/reconcile/` and through the routes in `notes/internal/api/`.
- [ ] Writing in place again turns the inode and injected-failure cases red, and dropping the `OnChange` check turns the live-copy case red, both recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `grep -rn os.WriteFile` over the non-test Go files of the notes module finds no call that writes into the vault: every such write goes through `vaultfile.WriteFileAtomic`.
- [ ] The goldens `notes/internal/vault/frontmatter/testdata/empty_file.md` and `notes/internal/vault/frontmatter/testdata/malformed_unterminated.md` keep their present answers.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] The Go gate of "Rules for this work" passes: go vet, go test and go build of the houston command inside notes/, and the dependency check script.

title: Store a note's kind and refs, and answer which notes cite an identifier
description:
## What changes for the user
Today a note cannot say what it is or which beads and tickets it is about, so nothing can list the planning, implementation and evidence notes of an epic. Once this lands a note's frontmatter can carry a kind and a list of references, and one request answers which notes cite any of a list of identifiers, matched without regard to case, with the notes one link away from them.

## Outcome
`kind` (one of four values, `nota` by default) and `refs` (a list) are parsed, kept with the note's attributes in all three places that list them, and `refs` gets the `note_refs` table of migration 0009 with its down file; `GET /api/notes/refs` answers the exact shape of the Specification, which the hub is built against.

## Context
The hub's chain asks, in one call, for the notes that cite an epic and all its descendants, and groups the answer by kind. The answer's shape is pinned here because the hub's side is built against it, with a stub service, possibly before this lands, so any change to it breaks the hub silently. Refs are compared without regard to case (`hou-4kz` and `HOU-4KZ` are one row) because identifiers are typed both ways. Tag rows and refs rows both survive a soft delete, so a revived note comes back whole, and every read joins live nodes only.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead works inside the notes module, so the Go gate applies to it.

## Facts verified for this step
Checked while the plan was written, on 2026-11-25.

- `internal/vault/service.go:14-15` imports `internal/vault/reconcile` and
  `internal/vault/watcher`. So a helper those packages need cannot live in package `internal/vault`:
  it would be an import cycle. Shared helpers go to a leaf package, `internal/vault/vaultfile`.
- Every `NNNN_*.up.sql` migration needs its `.down.sql`, or `graph.Open` fails
  (`internal/graph/internal/migrate/migrate.go:108`); 0005 is skipped on purpose, the next free
  number is 0009.

## Reading the citations
- A path under `internal/` or `cmd/kernl/` with a line number is kernl at `488fbbe`, the copy's
  source. Paths under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/` and `docs/` are Houston's.
- In the copy, kernl's `internal/<package>/<file>` is `notes/internal/<package>/<file>`, with the
  same name and, until a step edits that file, the same line numbers, since the copy's rewrite of
  import paths keeps every line count. The one exception is `internal/vault/config_test.go` after
  line 84, where the copy removed a kernl-only test.
- kernl's `internal/api/<file>` is ported into `notes/internal/api/<file>`; `cmd/kernl/<file>` into
  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.
- A cited kernl path that the copy does not take (`internal/app`, `internal/planning`,
  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.
- Line numbers are starting points; the search or test named as proof is what decides.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A8. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A6** adds `houston preflight`, which reports what the first index would change and writes nothing.
- **A7** fixes id injection, duplicate ids, fences, placeholders and in-place writes, and adds the leaf package `notes/internal/vault/vaultfile` with the atomic writer.

## Specification
- `kind` (one of `plano`, `implementacao`, `evidencia`, `nota`, matched after trimming and
  lower-casing; anything else, or nothing, counts as `nota`) and `refs` join `Frontmatter`
  (frontmatter.go:18-25). `tags` and `refs` use one YAML list type, in `internal/vault/frontmatter`,
  which already imports `gopkg.in/yaml.v3`, and not in `vaultfile`, which stays standard library
  only (A7): null or empty is an empty list; a single scalar, string or number, becomes a one-item
  list of its trimmed text; a sequence of scalars is the list, blank items dropped after trimming;
  a mapping or a nested sequence is a parse error, which A6 reports.
- `kind` travels with the note's other attributes, which are written out as an explicit list in
  three places: the serialiser `Note.NodeAttrs` (note.go:112-130) and the readers `GetNote`
  (note.go:170-203) and `ListNotes` (note.go:306-339). A key missing from one of them is dropped on
  the note's next update. `reconcile.NoteFromFile` (reconcile.go:873-883) fills `Kind` and `Refs`.
  `GET /api/notes` and `GET /api/vault/notes` keep their present answers.
- `refs` gets a table of its own, migration `0009_note_refs`, with its `.down.sql`:
  `note_refs(node_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES nodes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, ref TEXT NOT NULL
  COLLATE NOCASE, PRIMARY KEY (node_id, ref))` and an index on `ref COLLATE NOCASE`, so a
  case-insensitive lookup uses it and `hou-4kz` and `HOU-4KZ` are one row. An optional interface,
  `NodeRefs() []string`, implemented by `Note` beside `NodeTags()` (`internal/graph/nodes/node.go:8-13`),
  is reconciled where tag rows are, on create (through `finishNodeCreate`, `chokepoint.go:159`,
  which both `createNode` and `createNodeIfAbsent` call, and `:189-207`) and update (`:300-335`),
  and loaded by `GetNote` and `ListNotes`. Refs are de-duplicated and diffed by their case-folded
  text, not as tags are (`dedupStrings`, `:190`, is exact): under `COLLATE NOCASE`,
  `refs: [hou-4kz, HOU-4KZ]` would otherwise fail the primary key. Like tag rows, refs rows survive a
  soft delete, which is what lets a revived note come back whole; every query against the table
  joins `nodes` with `deleted_at IS NULL`.
- A note indexed before this step has no `kind` in its attributes until its file changes, so every
  read and filter takes a missing or empty `kind` as `nota`
  (`COALESCE(NULLIF(json_extract(n.attrs, '$.kind'), ''), 'nota')`), and the answers below never
  carry an empty `kind`.
- A new route, `GET /api/notes/refs?ids=<a>,<b>&kind=<k>&hop=0|1`, `hop` 0 by default:
  - the `ids` items are trimmed, blanks dropped, and de-duplicated without regard to case before
    they are counted; 400 when none is left or more than 200 are, or when `kind` (if given) or
    `hop` is not one of its values;
  - answer `{ "notes": [ { "id", "title", "path", "kind", "tags", "matchedRefs" } ],
    "linked": [ { "id", "title", "path", "kind", "tags" } ], "linkedOmitted": 0 }`, every list `[]`
    when empty and never `null`, `tags` and `matchedRefs` sorted;
  - `notes`: live note nodes (`type = 'note'`) with a `note_paths` row whose refs contain any of
    the identifiers, of one kind when `kind` is given, ordered by path;
  - with `hop=1`, `linked`: live notes of any kind with a path joined to those by a `links_to`
    edge in either direction (never `describes`), not already in `notes`, each note once however
    many direct notes link to it, ordered by path, the first 20, and `linkedOmitted` the rest.

Proof: Go tests: the refs rows through create, update, soft delete, revive and hard delete; a
deleted note never returned; `kind` survives an update that does not mention it (the three lists);
`kind: Plano` reads as `plano`; `refs: [12345]` reads as `"12345"`; `refs: [hou-4kz, HOU-4KZ]` stores
one row and a case-only edit keeps one row; `tags: foo` and `tags:` parse; `tags: {a: 1}` fails; a
note stored without `kind` answers `nota` and matches `kind=nota`; the route's matching without
regard to case, `ids` that differ only in case counted once, the `kind` filter applied to `notes`
and not to `linked`, the hop and its edge label, a neighbour linked from two direct notes listed
once, the cap and the count, the ordering, empty lists as `[]`, and each 400.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Go tests pass for every case listed under Proof in the Specification.
- [ ] `graph.Open` applies migration 0009 on a fresh database and on one at 0008, and `notes/internal/graph/schema/0009_note_refs.down.sql` exists beside its up file.
- [ ] The refs route answers every list as `[]` when empty, never `null`, and refuses each invalid `ids`, `kind` and `hop` with 400.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] The Go gate of "Rules for this work" passes: go vet, go test and go build of the houston command inside notes/, and the dependency check script.
- [ ] Done when: the refs route answers the pinned shape for an epic and its descendants, one-hop notes included.

## Tests
- unit: Go tests of the frontmatter list type, `kind` normalisation, the three attribute lists, and the refs rows through create, update, soft delete, revive and hard delete.
- integration: the refs route through the ported mux, the hop and every 400.

## Recovery path
Migration 0009 only adds a table and its index; `0009_note_refs.down.sql` drops them. Reverting the merge commit restores the code; a database already migrated keeps an unused table until the down file is applied. The database holds nothing a fresh index of the vault would not rebuild, except the revision history.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `notes/internal/vault/frontmatter/frontmatter.go`, `notes/internal/vault/frontmatter/*_test.go`, `notes/internal/graph/nodes/note.go`, `notes/internal/graph/nodes/node.go`, `notes/internal/graph/nodes/chokepoint.go`, `notes/internal/graph/nodes/*_test.go`, `notes/internal/graph/schema/0009_note_refs.up.sql`, `notes/internal/graph/schema/0009_note_refs.down.sql`, `notes/internal/vault/reconcile/reconcile.go`, `notes/internal/vault/reconcile/reconcile_test.go`, `notes/internal/api/notes_refs.go`, `notes/internal/api/notes_refs_test.go`, `notes/internal/api/routes.go`
**Reads only:** `notes/internal/graph/internal/migrate/migrate.go`, `notes/internal/vault/vaultfile/`, `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`

The frontmatter, the node layer, one migration, the reconciler and one route. Size L: a schema change across four packages.

Every case listed is a named test (e.g. a nil response failed TestHouOc517RefsEmptyListsAsEmpty, kind dropped from NodeAttrs failed TestHouOc517NoteKindSurvivesUpdate). Review breaks: describes edges in the hop, a cap of 21, 201 ids accepted, all red; the direct query's own deleted_at filter is an equivalent mutant behind the joined filter, and removing both fails TestHouOc517RefsDeletedNeverReturned. The lane ended without its done sentinel after finishing; its window was closed by the orchestrator. Internal-name sweep passed; go vet, go test, go build, check-notes-deps, lint and build pass.

title: Add a ranked search route with snippets, filters, paging and exact identifiers
description:
## What changes for the user
Today searching the notes matches the whole query as one phrase, ranks results poorly, shows no snippet, cannot page, and cannot find an identifier that a note declares only in its frontmatter. Once this lands several words match on their own in any order, the best hits come first with the matching words highlighted in a snippet, results filter by tag, folder and kind and page through, and an identifier like a bead id is found exactly, never as two loose words.

## Outcome
`GET /api/search` answers `{ hits, total, limit, offset }` over live notes only, by the term, ranking, snippet, filter, paging and identifier rules of the Specification; the match markers STX and ETX are stripped from everything written into the full-text index; the present node search keeps its answer.

## Context
The answer's shape and the snippet markers are pinned here because the hub's search page and the CLI render them; the markers are control characters so they cannot collide with Markdown. The tokenizer is not changed, which the review of the work hub's overall plan settled: identifiers holding `-`, `_`, `/` or `.` are queried as phrases and then checked as exact substrings, and the `note_refs` table of the kind-and-refs step answers identifiers declared only in frontmatter. - Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or

  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.

  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside

## Names used below

- **A8** adds the `kind` and `refs` frontmatter fields, the `note_refs` table and the refs route, GET /api/notes/refs.

## Specification
`GET /api/search?q=<terms>&tag=<t>&folder=<f>&kind=<k>&limit=<n>&offset=<n>`, beside the present
`GET /api/nodes/search`, which keeps its answer.

- Answer: `{ "hits": [ { "id", "title", "path", "kind", "tags", "snippet" } ], "total", "limit",
  "offset" }`. Only live notes with a path (`type = 'note'`, `deleted_at IS NULL`, joined with
  `note_paths`): the copied `nodes` package still defines tasks, projects, bookmarks and captures,
  which the schema can hold.
- Terms: each matched on its own (all must match), instead of the whole query as one phrase
  (search.go:224). Each token is stripped of `"` and quoted on its own, so FTS5 operators (`AND`,
  `OR`, `NOT`, `NEAR`, `:`, braces) cannot be injected. A token with no letter or digit (a lone `-`
  in `phase 3 - notes`) is left out of the FTS expression, where a quoted token with nothing to index
  is a syntax error, and is used only for the refs lookup. Control characters, NUL included, are
  removed from `q` first, and the refs lookup uses the same stripped, trimmed tokens as FTS. An
  empty or whitespace-only `q` answers 400; a `q` that leaves no FTS token at all looks in
  `note_refs` only, and never answers 500.
  Each token is satisfied by FTS (with the substring check for identifier-shaped ones) or by
  `note_refs`, so `STRY00000001 rollout` finds a note that names the story only in `refs` and says
  "rollout" in its body.
- Ranking: `bm25(nodes_fts, 10.0, 1.0)` ascending (more negative is better), the title weighted
  above the body; `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` checked to use the index the existing query-plan test pins
  (`query_plan_test.go:15-49`).
- Snippet: `snippet(nodes_fts, -1, "\u0002", "\u0003", "…", 24)`, best column, with STX and ETX as
  the match markers, so the hub can turn them into `<mark>` without colliding with Markdown.
  `snippet()` reads the indexed text and cannot strip anything, so STX and ETX are removed, by one
  helper, from the title, the body and the tags at every place they are written into `nodes_fts`:
  create and update (`internal/graph/nodes/chokepoint.go:161-172, 274-285`) and the revival of a
  note (`reviveNote`, `:684-710`); and from the 160-character body excerpt a hit found only through
  `refs` gets. The indexed body column also carries the note's tags, appended after a space
  (`:161-167`), so a snippet can end in tag words; accepted, since changing it means changing the
  FTS schema. `nodes_fts` keeps its alias in the query: `bm25(nodes_fts, ...)` and
  `snippet(nodes_fts, ...)` over `FROM nodes_fts(?) ft`, the shape of `search.go:153`, work on the
  SQLite that `modernc.org/sqlite` v1.60.1 bundles (3.53.4; checked), while naming the alias
  (`bm25(ft)`) fails.
- Filters: tag, folder and kind, each an `EXISTS` sub-query, because the present tag filter's
  `GROUP BY ... HAVING` (search.go:197-200) is the shape in which FTS5's auxiliary functions are
  unavailable. The folder is a path prefix with a `/` boundary and its `LIKE` wildcards (`%`, `_`,
  `\`) escaped, after leading and trailing `/` are trimmed (an empty result is no filter), so `ops`
  and `ops/` match `ops/...` and never `ops-old/`, and `2026_q4` is literal. `kind` reads a missing
  value as `nota`, as in A8.
- `limit` (default 20, at most 100), `offset` (default 0), and `total`. A `limit` below 1, a
  negative `offset`, a value that is not an integer, or a `kind` that is not one of the four
  answers 400.
- Identifiers, without changing the tokenizer (`unicode61`, which also makes plain words match
  without regard to diacritics, so `implementacao` finds `implementação`): a token containing `-`,
  `_`, `/` or `.` is queried as a phrase and then kept only if it appears as an exact substring,
  without regard to case, in the title or body; plain words keep FTS5's matching. Notes whose
  `note_refs` match a token, and that satisfy the other tokens and the filters, are joined with the
  FTS hits, de-duplicated by node, refs matches first, before `total` is counted and `offset` and
  `limit` are applied. Since the substring check and the merge run in Go, the SQL carries no
  `LIMIT` or `OFFSET` whenever either applies, or pages would come back short and `total` wrong.
  A hit that matched some tokens through `refs` gets its snippet from the other tokens, and the
  excerpt only when every token matched through `refs`. So a note that declares an identifier only
  in its frontmatter is found, and `hou-4kz` does not match a note that says `hou 4kz`.

Proof: Go tests: several terms in any order; ranking puts the title match first; the snippet carries
the markers around the term; each filter, a folder prefix that must not match a sibling, a trailing
`/` on the folder, an underscore in a folder name; a note stored without `kind` found by
`kind=nota`; `total` with `limit` and `offset`, also when identifier tokens filter out FTS rows
(every page full, `total` exact); an identifier in `refs` only; an identifier in a body only; the
near miss that must not match; `implementacao` finds `implementação`; an injected `OR` and a
`title:` prefix are treated as words; `q=---`, `q=phase 3 - notes` and a `q` holding a NUL answer
without error; a query with one token only in `refs` and one only in the body, with a snippet of the
second; a body holding STX keeps it out of the snippet, also after the note is deleted and revived;
