title: Resolve wikilinks the way Obsidian does, in the resolver, the dangling keys and the delete path
description:
## What changes for the user
Today a link to a note two folders down, a link to a heading, or an embedded image resolves wrong or not at all, links to a note the service creates itself never heal, and a link to a deleted note can reattach to an unrelated note of the same name. Once this lands links resolve the way Obsidian resolves them, and stay right when a note is created, changed, deleted and brought back.

## Outcome
The parser, the resolver, the dangling-link keys, the promotion of dangling links and the soft-delete path follow one rule set, through one helper, `wikilink.NormalizeTarget`, by the Specification, with Go tests per rule and per place; the existing resolver and promotion tests keep passing, and the tests that read stored keys back move to the normalised lower-case key.

## Context
Critical because a wrong resolution silently attaches a link to the wrong note, and the chain's one-hop notes are read from these links. Three places decide what a link points at and they disagree today; fixing one alone would make a link resolve on write and reattach elsewhere on delete. It runs after the frontmatter-fixes step because both rewrite the reconciler's change handler and the cold start's walk. The large-vault step later moves the `.md` handling of `NormalizeTarget` onto a shared helper.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead works inside the notes module, so the Go gate applies to it.

## Reading the citations
- A path under `internal/` or `cmd/kernl/` with a line number is kernl at `488fbbe`, the copy's
  source. Paths under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/` and `docs/` are Houston's.
- In the copy, kernl's `internal/<package>/<file>` is `notes/internal/<package>/<file>`, with the
  same name and, until a step edits that file, the same line numbers, since the copy's rewrite of
  import paths keeps every line count. The one exception is `internal/vault/config_test.go` after
  line 84, where the copy removed a kernl-only test.
- kernl's `internal/api/<file>` is ported into `notes/internal/api/<file>`; `cmd/kernl/<file>` into
  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.
- A cited kernl path that the copy does not take (`internal/app`, `internal/planning`,
  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.
- Line numbers are starting points; the search or test named as proof is what decides.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A10. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A3** ports kernl's notes-side HTTP routes into `notes/internal/api`, written against the graph and the vault root.

## Specification
- Embeds (`![[...]]`) are not note links: Go's regexp has no lookbehind, so `wikilink.Parse`
  checks the byte before the match (wikilink.go:13). Links whose target ends in a known non-note
  extension (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.svg`, `.webp`, `.pdf`, `.mp3`, `.mp4`, `.wav`,
  `.csv`, `.xlsx`, `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.zip`, `.tar`, `.gz`) are ignored too. A dot alone never
  disqualifies a target, so `[[2026.11.25]]` and `[[v1.2]]` resolve.
- Heading and block anchors are stripped from the first `#` before lookup and before a link is
  stored as dangling (today they stay in the target); a block reference to another note is
  `[[Note#^block]]`, so that covers it, and a `^` elsewhere is part of the name (`[[2^n]]`). An
  anchor-only link, a target starting with `#` or `^` (`[[#Heading]]`, `[[^block]]`), points inside
  its own note and is skipped. One helper, `wikilink.NormalizeTarget`, does this for the resolver
  and for the dangling keys below. Resolved targets and dangling keys are de-duplicated per source
  note, so `[[Note#A]]` and `[[Note#B]]` make one edge.
- `.md` is no longer appended to a target that already ends in it (resolver.go:86-88 looks for
  `b.md.md`).
- Order, without regard to case: a node id first, as today, checked as a live node of any type,
  which keeps `TestResolveUUIDTargetToNonNoteNode` (resolver_test.go:651-687) passing; then the
  exact relative path, with or without `.md`, of a live note; then a file with that name anywhere
  in the vault, the shortest path winning and ties broken alphabetically; then the title, ties by
  id as `TestStemCollisionTiebreak` (resolver_test.go:612) pins.
- The same rule in the three places that decide what a link points at:
  - the resolver (`resolveInTx`, resolver.go:72-113), keeping `target_kind` within the
    `stem|title|uuid` the schema allows (0003_notes.up.sql:14);
  - the keys under which a dangling link waits for its target, normalised (anchors and a trailing
    `.md` stripped, `/` separators, lower case): `danglingKeysFor` (reconcile.go:1131-1149), which
    already offers the stem, the title and the relative path without its extension (`:1146-1147`),
    normalises all three and adds the note id, a new parameter at its four call sites
    (`:501,586,641,693`) and at the promotion `OnChange` gains below; `promoteDanglingInTx`
    (resolver.go:209-270) normalises each incoming key, so its `WHERE target_key = ?` still uses
    `idx_dangling_links_target_key` and `resolver_test.go:420,450,484,510,515`, which promote
    with keys such as `"Target"` against rows the resolver wrote, keep passing; and it checks `edges.Exists`
    (`internal/graph/edges/edge.go:136`) before creating an edge, because `edges` has no unique
    constraint and a revival would otherwise duplicate edges, deleting the dangling row whether or
    not it created one, so a source holding `[[Note]]` and `[[sub/note]]` leaves no row behind;
  - the keys used when a note is deleted (`internal/graph/nodes/chokepoint.go:493,568-613`):
    `softDeleteNote` selects the edges' `attrs` too (today `id, src` only, `:569`) and gives each
    degraded edge one normalised dangling row from the link text it stored (`attrs.target_text`,
    resolver.go:275), falling back to the note's normalised relative path, instead of a stem row and
    a title row; today `[[a/foo]]` degrades to `foo`, which an unrelated `b/foo.md` can take. The
    reconciler forgets the `note_paths` row before it calls `SoftDeleteNoteTx` (reconcile.go:364,
    coldstart.go:304), so `SoftDeleteNoteTx` receives that relative path (already held as
    `pendingDelete.relPath`, and as the walked path in `coldstart.go`) in place of the stem, and its
    callers and tests change with it (`coldstart.go:307`, `reconcile.go:413`, `note_test.go:310,417`,
    `coldstart_test.go:363`, and the ported `vault_write_identity_test.go:131`, A3).
  - Stored keys are now lower case, so the tests that read `dangling_links.target_key` back with
    its written case change to the normalised key: `internal/vault/e2e_test.go:504,520,540,556`
    (`"Roadmap"`, through `countDanglingByTarget`, `:200-208`); and
    `TestPromoteDangling_SelfLinkCleanedUp` (`resolver_test.go:531-560`), which inserts a row keyed
    `"Self"` by hand (`:542-543`) that a normalised `"self"` lookup would no longer find, stores the
    normalised key.
- Dangling links are also promoted when a note arrives through a change event, not only a create:
  notes the service creates itself get their node first and their file event as a change, so today
  links to them never heal (OnChange, reconcile.go:744-763).

Proof: Go tests per rule and per place: a name found two folders deep; two candidates, the shorter
wins, then the alphabetical; `[[Note#Heading]]` resolves to `Note`; `[[#Heading]]` makes nothing;
`![[image.png]]` and `[[report.pdf]]` make no edge; `[[v1.2]]` and `[[2^n]]` resolve; `[[a/b.md]]`
resolves; `[[Note#A]]` and `[[Note#B]]` make one edge; a UUID-shaped target with no node falls
through to the other rules; the two existing resolver tests pass, and so do the promotion tests
that pass a mixed-case key; a dangling link heals when its target is created by
`POST /api/vault/file`; `[[Note]]` and `[[sub/note]]` from one source, both dangling, leave one edge
and no dangling row once `sub/note.md` appears; deleting a target leaves one dangling row, and its
return makes one edge, not two; `[[a/foo]]` does not attach to `b/foo.md` after `a/foo.md` is
deleted.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Go tests in `notes/internal/vault/wikilink/` and `notes/internal/vault/reconcile/` pass for every case listed under Proof in the Specification.
- [ ] `TestResolveUUIDTargetToNonNoteNode` and `TestStemCollisionTiebreak` pass unchanged, and so do the promotion tests that pass a mixed-case key.
- [ ] The tests that read `dangling_links.target_key` back, in `notes/internal/vault/e2e_test.go` and `TestPromoteDangling_SelfLinkCleanedUp`, expect the normalised key.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] The Go gate of "Rules for this work" passes: go vet, go test and go build of the houston command inside notes/, and the dependency check script.
- [ ] Done when: every resolution rule holds in the resolver, the dangling keys and the delete path, each proven per place.

## Tests
- unit: Go tests of the parser, the resolver order, normalisation, promotion with `edges.Exists`, and the soft-delete rows.
- integration: a dangling link healed by a note created through the file route, and a deleted target's return making one edge, not two.

## Recovery path
No migration: dangling-link keys are written normalised from this step on. No work database exists before it lands, since the first run on the work machine waits for it; a database indexed earlier is rebuilt by deleting it and letting the service reindex, losing only revision history. Reverting the merge commit restores the previous resolution.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `notes/internal/vault/wikilink/`, `notes/internal/vault/reconcile/`, `notes/internal/graph/nodes/chokepoint.go`, `notes/internal/graph/nodes/note_test.go`, `notes/internal/vault/e2e_test.go`, `notes/internal/api/vault_write_identity_test.go`
**Reads only:** `notes/internal/graph/edges/edge.go`, `notes/internal/graph/schema/0003_notes.up.sql`, `notes/internal/vault/vaultfile/`, `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`

Three packages that decide a link's target, plus two tests elsewhere that change with the delete path's signature. Size L.

title: Add the notes service settings and the hub's client for it
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the hub has no way to reach a notes service. Once this lands its address and the Obsidian vault's name are settings the hub validates, pages learn whether notes are configured, and every call to the service goes through one client that answers "unavailable" within a couple of seconds instead of failing or hanging a page.

## Outcome
`notesServiceUrl` (a second, stricter mode of the loopback validator) and `obsidianVault` are config keys through the existing config machinery; `GET /api/capabilities` adds `notes` and `obsidianVault`; `lib/notes-service.ts`, server only, calls the refs and search routes with the timeout, abort, shape checks and failure rule of the Specification; pure tests cover each.

## Context
It extends, and does not replace, the hub's config machinery from phase 1 (validated keys written atomically and owner-only through PUT /api/config, a loopback URL validator, and a capabilities route that tells pages which optional features exist) and the pure value validators of `lib/config-values.ts` from phase 2. The address is restricted to the hosts the notes service binds and its guard lets through, and to the root path, because the client builds every address with `new URL(path, base)`. The client checks the shape of the refs and search answers, which the notes service pins, so a service that answers something else reads as unavailable instead of breaking a page.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead wires notes into the hub. It builds against the answers the notes service pins, with stub services or fixtures, and does not wait for the engine's own steps.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is B2. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A2** adds the notes config loader (`LoadNotes`, `ValidateForServe`) and the database lock with an explicit path (`notes/internal/graph/dbfile`).
- **A5** adds the request guard that refuses non-loopback hosts and requests made by a browser page.
- **A8** adds the `kind` and `refs` frontmatter fields, the `note_refs` table and the refs route, GET /api/notes/refs.
- **A9** adds the ranked search route, GET /api/search, with snippets, filters, paging and exact identifiers.
- **phase 1** frames the work dashboard: the loopback URL validator (`lib/loopback-url.ts`), the config machinery with atomic owner-only writes through PUT /api/config, the capabilities route that tells pages which optional features exist, a server-side reachability probe, the /work page with its minimal shell (its step 5), the sidebar's link group and the launcher's work card, and the doc checker `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`.
- **phase 2** ties each bead to its tracker story and pipeline: `external_ref` on beads, the value validators of `lib/config-values.ts`, the chain resolver `lib/chain.ts` (its step 7), the chain routes by project and by identifier, GET /api/links/[id] among them, with `docs/chain.md` (its step 8), and the "Relacionados" panel in the bead drawer and the expanded epic.

## Specification
- `notesServiceUrl`: through a second mode of phase 1's validator, `checkLoopbackServiceUrl` in
  `lib/loopback-url.ts`, which keeps every rule of the first (a primitive string, trimmed, no
  control character, `http:` or `https:`, no user information, no query and no fragment, a bare `?`
  or `#` included, a port from 1 to 65535 or the default, the parser's normalised `href`) and
  differs in two: the host is `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `[::1]`, the set A2 lets the service bind
  and A5 lets through (`127.0.0.2` would be answered 403), never `0.0.0.0` or an IPv4-mapped IPv6;
  and the path is empty or `/`, since the service answers at its root and `new URL("/api/...",
  base)` would drop any other path.
- `obsidianVault`: a string, trimmed, non-empty, with no control character, validated in
  `lib/config-values.ts`.
- Both through phase 1's config machinery, cleared by `""` or `null`; `GET /api/capabilities` adds
  `notes: boolean` and `obsidianVault: string | null`; `hooks/use-capabilities.ts` exposes `notes`
  as `data?.notes === true` and `obsidianVault` as a non-empty string or `null`, as phase 2 does for
  `chain`, so fixtures that answer `{}` keep working; and `scripts/test-work-config.mjs`'s
  deep-equal of the whole answer is updated with them.
- `lib/notes-service.ts`, server only: takes the incoming `Request` from every caller, to refuse
  Houston's own origin as phase 1's probe does (its `url`, its `Host`, the loopback aliases) and to
  abort with it (`AbortSignal.any([request.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(2000)])`); calls with
  `cache: "no-store"`, building every address with `new URL(path, base)` (the configured URL is
  the root, ending with `/`); checks the shape of each answer (the lists and fields A8 and A9 pin);
  and answers `{ ok: false, status: "unavailable", reason }` when the URL is Houston's own, the
  service does not answer, times out, answers non-2xx, or answers something that is not JSON or not
  of that shape. Every call goes through the hub's server side; the page never calls the service.

Proof: `scripts/test-loopback-url.mjs` gains the second mode's table; `scripts/test-config-values.mjs`
gains `obsidianVault`; `scripts/test-work-config.mjs` covers both keys and the extended capabilities
answer; a new pure script, `scripts/test-notes-service.mjs` (the transpile-then-`vm` loader with
`server-only` stubbed), tests `lib/notes-service.ts` against a stub server on `127.0.0.1:0`, closed
with `closeAllConnections()`: a refs call, a search call, Houston's own address refused before any
request reaches the stub, a 200 answer of the wrong shape (`{}`), invalid JSON, a 500, a stopped
stub and a hanging one, each unavailable within three seconds, and a call aborted with its incoming
request. `scripts/test-loopback-url.mjs`'s second-mode table includes `http://127.0.0.2:3301/` and
`http://127.0.0.1:3301/prefix/` refused, and `scripts/test-config-values.mjs` refuses a blank
`obsidianVault`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `node scripts/test-loopback-url.mjs` and `node scripts/test-config-values.mjs` exit 0 with the new cases, including http://127.0.0.2:3301/ and http://127.0.0.1:3301/prefix/ refused and a blank `obsidianVault` refused.
- [ ] Both halves of `scripts/test-work-config.mjs` exit 0 with both keys and the extended capabilities answer.
- [ ] `node scripts/test-notes-service.mjs` exits 0 with every case of the Specification, each unavailable case answered within 3 s (the client's timeout is 2 s).
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: the hub reaches a notes service through one client and degrades to unavailable without an error on any page.

## Tests
- unit: `scripts/test-notes-service.mjs`, pure, against a stub server on an ephemeral port.
- unit: the validator tables in `scripts/test-loopback-url.mjs` and `scripts/test-config-values.mjs`.
- integration: the server half of `scripts/test-work-config.mjs`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `lib/loopback-url.ts`, `lib/config-values.ts`, `lib/config.ts`, `app/api/config/route.ts`, `app/api/capabilities/route.ts`, `hooks/use-capabilities.ts`, `lib/notes-service.ts`, `scripts/test-loopback-url.mjs`, `scripts/test-config-values.mjs`, `scripts/test-work-config.mjs`, `scripts/test-notes-service.mjs`
**Reads only:** `scripts/with-server.sh`

Eleven files of the hub's config layer and one new client. Size L by the file count.
close_reason: notesServiceUrl (a stricter service mode of the loopback validator: 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1], root path only) and obsidianVault (a trimmed, non-blank vault name without control characters) are config keys through the existing machinery; GET /api/capabilities adds notes (a boolean, the address stays on the server) and obsidianVault; lib/notes-service.ts, server only, calls the refs and search routes with the timeout, abort, answer-shape checks and failure rule of the Specification. 57 pure and every server break red, e.g. the service mode accepting 127.0.0.2 failed 'service: 127.0.0.2 should be refused', a blank vault accepted failed 'blank vault name is refused'. Merged with main (pipelineRepo in lib/config.ts) without conflict. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build, test-notes-service, test-loopback-url, test-config-values, test-pipeline-repo, test-actor-default, test-work-config both halves and read-only, test-work-page and test-all-sidebar pass.

title: Make the notes engine safe and ready on a large synced vault
description:
## What changes for the user
Today an edit to a long note costs hundreds of megabytes, a folder moved or deleted is missed, a note deleted and recreated can stay hidden for good, a save that changes nothing corrupts the note's history, a note moved to the trash stays in search until the next restart, events during the first index are lost, and stopping the service mid-index can drop notes from the index. Once this lands each is fixed, health says whether indexing is finished and what was skipped, the bulk listings can page, and a measurement on five thousand notes decides two further speed-ups.

## Outcome
The fixes, the readiness rules and the opt-in pagination of the Specification, with Go tests; migration 0010 adds the index on revisions; `BenchmarkVault5000` measures cold start, warm start and search on a synthetic vault of five thousand notes, and its numbers and the decision on both candidates go to the close reason and to the user.

## Context
Critical because several of these defects lose or hide notes on a synced vault, where sync clients move, replace and recreate files all the time and the first run writes an id into thousands of notes at once. Two of them, the note deleted and recreated and the unchanged save, were not in the work hub's overall plan; the user accepted fixing them here because the service runs that code. The spec is open on one point: batching the first index's writes is adopted if the first index takes more than 10 s, and skipping unchanged files by modification time and size is adopted if a warm start takes more than 2 s (that one needs a further migration).   module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead works inside the notes module, so the Go gate applies to it.

## Facts verified for this step
Checked while the plan was written, on 2026-11-25.

- `internal/vault/service.go:14-15` imports `internal/vault/reconcile` and
  `internal/vault/watcher`. So a helper those packages need cannot live in package `internal/vault`:
  it would be an import cycle. Shared helpers go to a leaf package, `internal/vault/vaultfile`.
- Every `NNNN_*.up.sql` migration needs its `.down.sql`, or `graph.Open` fails
  (`internal/graph/internal/migrate/migrate.go:108`); 0005 is skipped on purpose, the next free
  number is 0009.
- On macOS, fsnotify's kqueue backend opens one descriptor per file, not per directory
  (`backend_kqueue.go:252-254` in fsnotify v1.10.1).

## Decisions this step follows
The user accepted these on 2026-11-25; the Specification cites them by number.

- **Provisional decision 7.** Two defects the direction plan did not list are fixed here because the service runs their code on a synced vault: a note deleted and recreated can stay hidden for good, and an update with an unchanged body stores a revision later read as an empty body.
- **Provisional decision 9.** The measurement of step A11 decides batching the first index if it takes more than 10 s on the synthetic vault, and the modification-time-and-size skip if a warm start takes more than 2 s. The numbers and the decision are reported to the user.

## Reading the citations
- A path under `internal/` or `cmd/kernl/` with a line number is kernl at `488fbbe`, the copy's
  source. Paths under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/` and `docs/` are Houston's.
- In the copy, kernl's `internal/<package>/<file>` is `notes/internal/<package>/<file>`, with the
  same name and, until a step edits that file, the same line numbers, since the copy's rewrite of
  import paths keeps every line count. The one exception is `internal/vault/config_test.go` after
  line 84, where the copy removed a kernl-only test.
- kernl's `internal/api/<file>` is ported into `notes/internal/api/<file>`; `cmd/kernl/<file>` into
  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.
- A cited kernl path that the copy does not take (`internal/app`, `internal/planning`,
  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.
- Line numbers are starting points; the search or test named as proof is what decides.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A11. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A3** ports kernl's notes-side HTTP routes into `notes/internal/api`, written against the graph and the vault root.
- **A4** adds `houston serve`, which starts the server before the first index, and `houston health`.
- **A7** fixes id injection, duplicate ids, fences, placeholders and in-place writes, and adds the leaf package `notes/internal/vault/vaultfile` with the atomic writer.
- **A10** makes wikilinks resolve the way Obsidian does, in the resolver, the dangling keys and the delete path.
- **the direction plan**: the work hub's overall plan, whose review settled what each phase does and does not do.

## Specification
Fixed regardless of measurement:

- **Line diff.** `lineDiff` builds a full table of lines by lines (note.go:430-470), about 8·m·n
  bytes; a note of five thousand short lines costs about 200 MB per edit. It gets a cap on m·n (four
  million cells, about 32 MB) above which the revision is stored as a snapshot.
- **Unchanged body.** Today an update whose body did not change stores `{"ops":null}`
  (`internal/graph/nodes/note.go:380-383`), which reconstruction
  (`internal/graph/revisions/reconstruct.go:96-104,123-125`) reads as a snapshot of an empty body,
  and every `POST /api/vault/file` does it twice. Fix: after reconciling the tags and the refs,
  `updateNode` inserts no revision when title, attributes, tags and refs are all unchanged; when any
  of them changed and the body did not, it stores a full snapshot, never `{"ops":null}`, so a
  metadata change, a refs-only edit included, keeps its history. A tag or ref change is read from
  the reconciliation's own lists to add and remove, never by comparing slices, since `selectTags`
  has no `ORDER BY` (chokepoint.go:771-775); and `Note.DiffBody` answers a snapshot when the diff has
  no operation, so no other caller can store `{"ops":null}` either. The rule holds for every node
  type, so the model test `internal/graph/property_test.go`, which draws identical updates and
  counts one revision per update (`:100-101`, checked at `:183-196,291-294`), counts one only when
  title, body or tags changed.
- **Index.** `revisions(node_id)` is queried on every update with no index
  (chokepoint.go:339-345); migration `0010_revisions_node_id_index`, with its `.down.sql`, adds one.
- **Listing and dot-paths.** `GET /api/vault/list` (vault.go:89-98, moved to `filepath.WalkDir`),
  `locateNoteFile` (reconcile.go:1058) and the watcher's live events skip dot-files and
  dot-directories by the path relative to the vault root, never by components above it, so a vault
  under a dot-named directory such as `/tmp/.test/` is not skipped whole. A path outside the root,
  whose relative form starts with `..`, is refused as such, not taken for a dot-file; and
  `watcher_deterministic_test.go`, whose watcher's root is `t.TempDir()` (`:78`) while it injects
  `/vault/...` paths (`:111,153,179-180` and others), injects paths under its root instead.
- **Watcher.** `*fsnotify.Watcher` goes behind a small interface (`Add`, `Remove`, `Close`), so a
  test can drive directory moves with a fake backend (today `newWithSources` leaves `w.fsw` nil,
  watcher.go:134, and `addDirRecursive` would panic, :234,288). A directory created or renamed into
  the vault (today `Rename` is not watched and `Create` emits nothing, :285-291) is watched
  recursively, skipping dot-directories, and emits a change for each note inside. The watcher has no
  access to the graph, so a tracked directory removed or renamed away (dropped today: its `os.Stat`
  fails, so it is not seen as a directory, and its name does not end in `.md`, :270-281) is
  recognised by its entry in the watcher's directory set, checked before the extension filter,
  pruned with its subdirectories from that set and emits a directory-delete event; the
  reconciler's `OnDirDelete` queries `note_paths` under that prefix, escaped, and hands each path to
  `OnDelete`, inside the move window, never tombstoning at once, so a folder renamed inside the vault
  keeps every note's identity when its notes arrive at the new path.
- **Extension.** One helper, `vaultfile.IsNoteFile`, matches `.md` without regard to case, and every
  site that asks whether a path is a note uses it: api/vault.go:93,222,274,297;
  reconcile/coldstart.go:74; reconcile.go:1059; watcher.go:279; and wikilink/resolver.go:87, where
  A10's check of a target already ending in `.md` is that question. Its companion,
  `vaultfile.TrimNoteExt`, strips a trailing `.md` without regard to case where a site removes it:
  A10's `wikilink.NormalizeTarget`. Fixing the watcher alone would index a `.MD` note and delete it
  at the next start.
- **Delete then recreate.** The watcher never emits a create (create becomes change,
  watcher.go:368-391), so the pending-delete path is reached only through a fallback
  (service.go:162-166). A note whose file is deleted and recreated within the move window is
  tombstoned with its file on disk; after the window it is updated as a tombstone, because
  `updateNode` reads the row without `deleted_at IS NULL` (chokepoint.go:244-247), and stays hidden.
  Fix: `OnChange` cancels a pending delete only by the note's id or its content hash, never just by
  path (a new note written under a deleted note's name must not cancel the old note's delete), and
  hands a tombstoned id to `OnCreate`, which revives it.
- **A note moved out of reach.** fsnotify reports a rename on the old path, which the watcher
  turns into a move candidate (watcher.go:394-399); the router then finds the file gone and does
  nothing (service.go:147-159), counting on the event at the new path. A note moved into `.trash/`,
  which is a dot-directory and not watched, or out of the vault never has that event, so it stays
  live in search and refs until the next start; that is exactly what the service's own
  `DELETE /api/vault/file` does (A3), and Obsidian's move to its trash. Fix: a move candidate whose
  file is gone goes to `OnDelete`, inside the move window, so a move within the vault still keeps
  its identity through the new path's event, and the others are tombstoned when the window ends.

Readiness:

- The server answers before the first index completes (A4). Health adds `indexing: true|false` and
  the current counts of A7's reports beside its three fields, read from the vault service, which A4
  hands to the routes through the dependency struct of A3. The service's status is safe to read
  from any goroutine from `vault.New` on, `indexing: true` until `ColdStart` returns; today `Start`
  assigns its reconciler unguarded (`internal/vault/service.go:66`), which a health read during the
  first index would race.
- The watcher's OS watches are armed before `ColdStart` (today they start after it,
  service.go:69-94, and events in between are lost) and stopped if `ColdStart` fails or is cancelled.
  The event router starts draining only after `ColdStart` finishes, so live events never run against
  the cold start's snapshot and its tombstone sweep.
- The watcher's emit (watcher.go:356-361), a blocking send into a 256-slot channel today, becomes
  non-blocking with a `dropped` flag (also set when the raw error channel delivers
  `fsnotify.ErrEventOverflow`, the kernel queue's overflow, which today is only logged,
  watcher.go:260-264): on a first run that injects ids into five thousand notes, each write raises
  an event, and a blocking send would pile up thousands of waiting timer goroutines. The flag is
  checked once `ColdStart` finishes and then on every tick of the flush ticker, so an overflow during
  live running is recovered too (the periodic rescan is off by default); when set, it is cleared and
  one rescan follows.
- `OnChange` (reconcile.go:722-777) is a no-op when `note_paths` already records the same id, path
  and content hash for a live note (after the pending-delete and tombstone checks), so the cold
  start's own id-injection writes do not cause a second full write of every note. That makes
  `applyMove` wrong as it stands: for a note moved and edited while the service was stopped, it
  writes the new path with the new hash (coldstart.go:245) before calling `OnChange` (:259), which
  would then skip the edit, and `TestColdStart_MoveAndEditWhileOff` (coldstart_test.go:642) would
  fail. When the hash differs, `applyMove` keeps the old hash in the row and leaves the new one to
  `OnChange`.
- The walk checks its context on every entry and returns the error at once, skipping the tombstone
  sweep, so a cancelled walk never tombstones the notes it had not reached (coldstart.go:59-106).

Measured, then decided: cold start, warm start and search on a synthetic vault of five thousand
notes, as three sub-benchmarks (`BenchmarkVault5000/ColdStart`, `/WarmStart`, `/Search`) whose
fixture is built outside the timer, with a fresh database for each cold start, run by the
implementer inside `notes/` with `go test -run=^$ -bench=BenchmarkVault5000 -benchtime=1x -count=3
./internal/vault/...` on a quiet machine. Two candidates wait for that number (provisional
decision 9): batching the writes of the
first index, adopted if the first index takes more than 10 s; and skipping unchanged files by
modification time and size instead of reading and hashing each one, adopted if a warm start takes
more than 2 s, which needs `mtime_ns` and `size` columns on `note_paths` in a further migration. The
second matters most if the sync client keeps files in the cloud until read. The numbers and the
decision go into the bead's close reason and to the user.

Pagination, opt-in: `limit` and `offset` on `GET /api/nodes`, `GET /api/vault/notes`,
`GET /api/vault/list` and `GET /api/edges`, which return everything today. Without either, the
answer is unchanged. With either, `limit` is an integer from 1 to 500, 500 when only `offset` is
given (SQLite takes no `OFFSET` without a `LIMIT`), and `offset` a non-negative integer, 400
otherwise; and the order is fixed (`n.id`, `np.path`, the path, `e.id`, ascending), since none of
them has an `ORDER BY` today (chat.go:346, vault.go:117, edges.go:194). `GET /api/notes`
(notes_index.go:51-75) stays unpaginated; the hub never calls it.

Proof: Go tests: the diff cap stores a snapshot for a 5,000-line note and a diff for a small one; an
unchanged update adds no revision, a tags-only change adds a snapshot that reconstructs to the
body, and the same tags in another order add nothing; `TestSubstrateProperties` passes with its
mirror updated; the listing skips `.obsidian` and still lists a vault under a dot-named parent; the
deterministic watcher tests pass with paths under their root; a directory moved in and one moved
out, with a fake watcher backend; `Note.MD` indexed and kept across a cold start; delete then
recreate within and after the window leaves the note live; a folder renamed inside the vault keeps
its notes' ids; a note moved into `.trash/` or out of the vault leaves search after the window, and
one moved inside it keeps its id; a note moved and edited while stopped keeps the edit after a cold
start; a first run over a few hundred id-less notes leaves no blocked goroutine and writes each note
once; an overflow injected during live running is followed by one rescan; a refs-only edit adds a
snapshot revision; a new note written under a deleted note's name leaves the old note deleted;
health reports `indexing` and the counts, and is read concurrently with the first index under
`go test -race`; an event during the first index is not lost; a cancelled context stops the walk and
tombstones nothing; each paginated route with and without parameters, with `offset` alone, and with
invalid ones (`limit=0`, `limit=501`, `offset=-1`). Broken on purpose: the move candidate's old
no-op turns the `.trash/` case red, and `applyMove` writing the new hash turns the moved-and-edited
case red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Go tests pass for every case listed under Proof in the Specification, and the health read during the first index passes under `go test -race`.
- [ ] An edit of a 5,000-line note stores a snapshot, the diff table being capped at four million cells (about 32 MB), while a small note still stores a diff.
- [ ] The move candidate's old no-op turns the trash case red, and `applyMove` writing the new hash turns the moved-and-edited case red, both recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `graph.Open` applies migration 0010 after 0009, and `notes/internal/graph/schema/0010_revisions_node_id_index.down.sql` exists beside its up file.
- [ ] `BenchmarkVault5000` runs its three sub-benchmarks once in the lane; the review then times three runs on a quiet machine and records cold start, warm start and search in the close reason, with the decision on batching (adopted above 10 s for the first index) and on the modification-time skip (adopted above 2 s for a warm start).
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] The Go gate of "Rules for this work" passes: go vet, go test and go build of the houston command inside notes/, and the dependency check script.
- [ ] Done when: every fix of the Specification has a test, health reports readiness, and the measurement's decision is recorded and reported to the user.

## Tests
- unit: Go tests of the diff cap, revisions, listing, the watcher with a fake backend, the reconciler and the cold start.
- property: `TestSubstrateProperties` with its mirror updated to count a revision only when title, body or tags changed.
- integration: health read concurrently with the first index under `go test -race`, and each paginated route with and without parameters.
- load: `BenchmarkVault5000` (cold start, warm start, search) over five thousand synthetic notes, three timed runs by the review.

## Recovery path
Migration 0010 only adds an index; its down file drops it. Reverting the merge commit restores the previous behaviour; this bead writes nothing into the vault beyond what the service already writes.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `notes/internal/graph/nodes/`, `notes/internal/graph/property_test.go`, `notes/internal/graph/schema/0010_revisions_node_id_index.up.sql`, `notes/internal/graph/schema/0010_revisions_node_id_index.down.sql`, `notes/internal/vault/service.go`, `notes/internal/vault/service_test.go`, `notes/internal/vault/bench_test.go`, `notes/internal/vault/watcher/`, `notes/internal/vault/reconcile/`, `notes/internal/vault/vaultfile/`, `notes/internal/vault/wikilink/`, `notes/internal/api/`
**Reads only:** `notes/internal/graph/revisions/reconstruct.go`, `notes/internal/graph/internal/migrate/migrate.go`, `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`

The node layer, one migration, the watcher, the service, the reconciler, the shared helpers and the routes. Size L; the readiness rules and the watcher fixes share the service's start order, so they do not split along a seam that shares no file.

title: Give houston its CLI: the note and graph verbs, health and search
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the notes service can only be reached with raw HTTP requests. Once this lands an agent or the user can list, read, write, append to, delete and tag notes, walk the graph, check the service's health and readiness, and search with filters from the `houston` command, against its own service, with messages that name `houston` and its own settings, never the application the engine came from.

## Outcome
`notes/cmd/houston` carries kernl's notes-side client verbs and their plumbing, ported and renamed as the Specification lists, plus `search`, a client of the search route that strips the snippet markers in text; the address comes from `--server`, then `HOUSTON_ADDR`, then `notes.yaml`, then `127.0.0.1:3301`; kernl's CLI tests of the ported verbs pass against `httptest` fakes.

## Context
The verbs are copied from kernl's command, not shared with it: kernl's binary stays as it is, and every message that said `kernl` now says `houston`, including two hints that named verbs only kernl has. Health also prints the readiness fields and skipped-file counts that the large-vault step adds, which is why this runs after it, and after the preflight verb, whose exit-code file the other verbs build on, and after the search route. The `links` verb, the only one that needs the hub, is a step of its own after this one.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead works inside the notes module, so the Go gate applies to it.

## Reading the citations
- A path under `internal/` or `cmd/kernl/` with a line number is kernl at `488fbbe`, the copy's
  source. Paths under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/` and `docs/` are Houston's.
- In the copy, kernl's `internal/<package>/<file>` is `notes/internal/<package>/<file>`, with the
  same name and, until a step edits that file, the same line numbers, since the copy's rewrite of
  import paths keeps every line count. The one exception is `internal/vault/config_test.go` after
  line 84, where the copy removed a kernl-only test.
- kernl's `internal/api/<file>` is ported into `notes/internal/api/<file>`; `cmd/kernl/<file>` into
  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.
- A cited kernl path that the copy does not take (`internal/app`, `internal/planning`,
  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.
- Line numbers are starting points; the search or test named as proof is what decides.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A12. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A1** copies kernl's notes engine into `notes/`, a Go module of Houston's own, and adds the dependency check `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh` and the Go gate.
- **A6** adds `houston preflight`, which reports what the first index would change and writes nothing.
- **A7** fixes id injection, duplicate ids, fences, placeholders and in-place writes, and adds the leaf package `notes/internal/vault/vaultfile` with the atomic writer.
- **A9** adds the ranked search route, GET /api/search, with snippets, filters, paging and exact identifiers.
- **A13** adds `houston links`, a client of the hub's links route.

## Specification
`notes/cmd/houston` takes kernl's notes-side client verbs, ported from `cmd/kernl` and shared with
nothing: `note list|read|write|append|delete|tags` (note.go:204-237),
`graph nodes|search|related|edges` (graph.go:140-158), the status part of `health.go:70-95`, and the plumbing they use: `verbio.go`,
`apiclient.go`, `postRaw`, `postRawWithClient` and `sortedKeys` (note.go:780-830), `parseBoolFlag`
(main.go:163), all of `suggest.go` (`didYouMean`, `:66`, calls `suggest`, `:47`, and
`damerauDistance`, `:8`), the JSON error envelope (`wantsJSONOutput`, `errorEnvelope`,
main.go:77-104), and the `commandMeta` and `commandFlag` types (help.go:11-45) with a command table
of `houston`'s own verbs; `exitcode.go` came with A6. These files import only the standard library,
and `main.go` also `internal/logging`.

- Every message that says `kernl` says `houston`: the usage errors of `takeFlag`,
  `rejectUnknownFlags` and `requireSub` (verbio.go:83,102,111,119), the `--server` errors and the
  unreachable-server hint (apiclient.go:90,97,200). Two hints name verbs only kernl has, the empty
  graph's `kernl capture` (graph.go:172) and the unconfigured vault's `kernl settings set vault`
  (health.go:138); `houston` names its own fix in both (the vault setting in `notes.yaml` or
  `HOUSTON_VAULT`).
- The default address: `houston` joins its configured host and port with `net.JoinHostPort`, so
  `server.host: ::1` is dialled as `[::1]`, where kernl writes `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`
  (apiclient.go:81).
- `stdinIsTerminal` (verbio.go:12-18), the seam `stdin_guard_test.go:16-18` overrides, comes along
  for `note write`, with that test's `note write` case.
- `houston`'s verbs: `serve`, `preflight`, `health` (also printing `indexing` and A7's counts);
  `note list|read|write|append|delete|tags`, where `note write` has no `--no-links-reason`
  (note.go:56,85,412), since the service suggests no links; `graph nodes|search|related|edges`;
  `search <query...> [--tag] [--folder] [--kind] [--limit] [--offset] [--json]`, a client of A9's
  route, its positional words joined with spaces as `graph search` does, printing in text one block
  per hit (title, path, kind, tags, and the snippet with the STX and ETX markers stripped) and a
  last line with `total`. `links` comes in A13. Its own address: `--server`, then `HOUSTON_ADDR`,
  then `notes.yaml`, then `127.0.0.1:3301`. Exit codes 0, 1 and 2 and the `--json` error envelope as
  kernl's. Not ported: `note suggest`, `note apply-hunks`, `note backfill-companions`,
  `graph briefing` and `health update-check`, whose routes or services the copy does not have.

Proof: kernl's CLI tests of the ported verbs, ported with them (the cases of `note_test.go`,
`graph_test.go`, `health_test.go`, `apiclient_test.go` and `suggest_test.go` that cover a ported
verb, and the `note write` case of `stdin_guard_test.go`), pass against `httptest` fakes, the
pattern of `cmd/kernl/note_test.go:32`; new tests, one per verb, include `search` with several words
and markers stripped, `note write --no-links-reason` refused as an unknown flag, and no `houston`
message naming `kernl` (an unknown flag, a missing subcommand, an unreachable server, an empty
graph, an unconfigured vault); A1's gate passes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] kernl's CLI tests of the ported verbs, ported into `notes/cmd/houston/`, pass against `httptest` fakes.

title: Add houston links, the CLI client of the hub's links route
description:
## What changes for the user
Today an agent working in a repository has no command to ask what holds an identifier across every project. Once this lands `houston links <id>` prints the tracker state of the identifier, every bead that carries it with its chain, the notes that cite it, and the projects the hub could not read.

## Outcome
`houston links <id> [--json]` calls the hub's links route with the identifier path-escaped, at the address in `HOUSTON_HUB_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:3300`, a trailing `/` dropped), prints the answer as text or as JSON, and fails with an error naming `HOUSTON_HUB_URL` when the hub does not answer.

## Context
The links route belongs to the hub, not to the notes service. Given an identifier it answers `{ id, snapshot, ticket, beads, unreadable }`: `beads` lists every bead in every project whose id or external reference matches, each with its project and its chain; `ticket` is the identifier as a tracker item; `snapshot` says whether the work snapshot was readable; `unreadable` lists the projects that failed to read. `docs/chain.md` describes that answer field by field. The hub's chain-routes step adds the route and that document, so this bead depends on it in the tracker; no other engine step does. The hub's notes-in-the-chain step adds a top-level `notes` list to the same answer; this verb prints it when present and prints nothing for it when absent, so it does not wait for that step.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead works inside the notes module, so the Go gate applies to it.

## Reading the citations
- A path under `internal/` or `cmd/kernl/` with a line number is kernl at `488fbbe`, the copy's
  source. Paths under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/` and `docs/` are Houston's.
- In the copy, kernl's `internal/<package>/<file>` is `notes/internal/<package>/<file>`, with the
  same name and, until a step edits that file, the same line numbers, since the copy's rewrite of
  import paths keeps every line count. The one exception is `internal/vault/config_test.go` after
  line 84, where the copy removed a kernl-only test.
- kernl's `internal/api/<file>` is ported into `notes/internal/api/<file>`; `cmd/kernl/<file>` into
  `notes/cmd/houston/<file>`; `internal/app/lock.go` into `notes/internal/graph/dbfile/lock.go`; and
  kernl's `internal/config/config.go` gives `ServerConfig`, `VaultConfig` and `expandHomePath` to
  `notes/internal/config/config.go`.
- A cited kernl path that the copy does not take (`internal/app`, `internal/planning`,
  `internal/vault/companion`, `internal/inbox` and the rest) is cited only as the source of what is
  left out. kernl's code at that commit is read from a clone of kernl's repository, kept outside
  this one, and is never written.
- Line numbers are starting points; the search or test named as proof is what decides.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is A13. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A1** copies kernl's notes engine into `notes/`, a Go module of Houston's own, and adds the dependency check `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh` and the Go gate.
- **A12** ports kernl's notes-side CLI verbs into `houston` and adds `houston search`.
- **phase 2** ties each bead to its tracker story and pipeline: `external_ref` on beads, the value validators of `lib/config-values.ts`, the chain resolver `lib/chain.ts` (its step 7), the chain routes by project and by identifier, GET /api/links/[id] among them, with `docs/chain.md` (its step 8), and the "Relacionados" panel in the bead drawer and the expanded epic.

- [ ] A fake answer with and without the top-level `notes` list prints without error.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] The Go gate of "Rules for this work" passes: go vet, go test and go build of the houston command inside notes/, and the dependency check script.
- [ ] Done when: `houston links <id>` prints what the hub's links route answers.

## Tests
- unit: CLI tests against an `httptest` fake hub, a missing hub and an escaped id.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `notes/cmd/houston/links.go`, `notes/cmd/houston/links_test.go`, `notes/cmd/houston/main.go`, `notes/cmd/houston/help.go`
**Reads only:** `notes/cmd/houston/apiclient.go`, `docs/chain.md`, `app/api/links/[id]/route.ts`, `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`

One verb, its test, and its entries in the dispatch and the command table. Size M by the four files, though the work is mechanical.

title: Back up the notes database once a day to a synced folder
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the notes database lives only on the work machine, and the revision history of every note, which a fresh index cannot rebuild, would be lost with it. Once this lands a login agent copies the database once a day, at noon or at the next wake or login, into a synced folder the user chooses, keeps the seven most recent copies, and the setup guide says how to restore one.

## Outcome
`scripts/notes-backup.sh <db> <dir>` writes a consistent copy with `VACUUM INTO` under a temporary name, renames it to `notes-YYYY-MM-DD.db`, and keeps the seven newest; `scripts/install-services.sh` installs it as a third agent, `houston.notes-backup`, with `--notes-backup-dir` and `--print-notes-backup`, by the rules of the Specification; `docs/work-side-setup.md` documents the option and the restore; a new pure test and the install test cover both.

## Context
The user decided on 2026-11-25 that the notes database is backed up once a day to a synced folder, seven copies kept. The database sits outside the vault so its live file and write-ahead log never ride the sync; a copy made with `VACUUM INTO` is one closed file that is safe to sync. A fresh index of the vault rebuilds everything in the database except the revision history, since the service writes no pin or link-suggestion state. The temporary name keeps the sync client from uploading half a copy under the final name, and lets a second run on the same day replace that day's copy, which `VACUUM INTO` alone refuses. The notes service's own login agent, which this one sits beside, comes from the install step.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead wires notes into the hub. It builds against the answers the notes service pins, with stub services or fixtures, and does not wait for the engine's own steps.

## Facts verified for this step
Checked while the plan was written, on 2026-11-25.

- Pin state is written only by `PATCH /api/notes/{id}` and `PATCH /api/notes/tags`
  (`internal/api/notes_index.go:98,134`), and link-suggestion state only by `POST /api/vault/file`'s
  suggestion block (`vault.go:322`). The copy ports neither (A3), so in it the database holds
  nothing that a fresh index of the vault would not rebuild except the revision history (B7).
- `sqlite3 <db> "VACUUM INTO '<path>'"` (sqlite3 3.53.4, checked 2026-11-25) copies a database in
  WAL mode into a single file in `delete` journal mode that passes `PRAGMA integrity_check`, takes a
  `'` in the path doubled, and refuses a target that already exists ("output file already exists").

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is B7. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A3** ports kernl's notes-side HTTP routes into `notes/internal/api`, written against the graph and the vault root.

## Specification
- `scripts/notes-backup.sh <db> <dir>` makes `<dir>/houston-backup` when it is missing, removes a
  `.notes-YYYY-MM-DD.db.partial` a failed run left there, and runs
  `sqlite3 <db> "VACUUM INTO '<dir>/houston-backup/.notes-YYYY-MM-DD.db.partial'"`, the date from
  `date +%F` and every `'` in the path doubled inside the SQL literal, since a synced folder's name
  can hold one. It then renames that file to `notes-YYYY-MM-DD.db`. `VACUUM INTO` writes a
  consistent, closed copy, one file in `delete` journal mode, while the service keeps running and
  writing; the live file and its write-ahead log are not safe to sync. The temporary name means the
  sync client never uploads half a copy under the final name, and it lets a second run on the same
  day (`RunAtLoad` after a restart) replace that day's copy, where `VACUUM INTO` refuses a target
  that exists. Last, it keeps the 7 most recent `notes-YYYY-MM-DD.db` by name (ISO dates sort in time
  order) and deletes the older ones, touching no other file in the folder. A missing database or a
  failing `sqlite3` exits non-zero with a message, and the copies already there stay.
- `scripts/install-services.sh` learns a third definition, `houston.notes-backup`, enabled by
  `--notes-backup-dir <absolute path>`: refused when relative, without `--notes-vault`, or when,
  normalised, it equals or lies inside the vault (the component comparison of `--notes-db`), checked
  with `validate_xml_safe`; whether it is a directory is checked only after `--print-notes-backup`
  has had its chance to exit. The path is given on the command line and written only into the plist
  under `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, never into the repository. The definition runs
  `/bin/bash <checkout>/scripts/notes-backup.sh <notes-db> <dir>` with a `PATH` of the system
  directories (macOS ships `/usr/bin/sqlite3`), `StartCalendarInterval` `{ Hour: 12, Minute: 0 }`
  and `RunAtLoad`, no `KeepAlive`, and logs to `$HOME/Library/Logs/houston/notes-backup.log`. launchd
  runs a slot missed during sleep when the machine wakes, and `RunAtLoad` covers a machine that was
  off at that hour. `--print-notes-backup` prints it (refused with `--print` or `--print-notes`, and
  without `--notes-vault` and `--notes-backup-dir`); the install checks `sqlite3` in the
  definition's `PATH`, writes the document through a temporary file the `EXIT` trap removes, and runs
  `bootout` and `bootstrap` for it like the others. Without `--notes-backup-dir` nothing about it
  changes. `scripts/update.sh` needs nothing for it: the agent runs the script from the checkout at
  every run.
- `docs/work-side-setup.md`, in the section "Notes service": the option, where the copies go, that
  seven are kept, and why. A fresh index of the vault rebuilds the database except its revision
  history, which exists only there (the service writes no pin or link-suggestion state, A3). How to
  restore: stop `houston.notes`, copy a backup over the database path after removing the `-wal` and
  `-shm` files beside it, and start it again.

Proof: `scripts/test-install-services.mjs`: the third document parses with `plistlib` and carries
the label, `ProgramArguments` (`/bin/bash`, the script in the checkout, the database path and the
backup directory, for a directory with a space in its name), `StartCalendarInterval` with `Hour` 12
and `Minute` 0, `RunAtLoad` true and no `KeepAlive`, and the log path; each refused option and
combination (relative, inside the vault, without `--notes-vault`, `--print-notes-backup` with
`--print`); `--print-notes-backup` creates nothing on disk; without `--notes-backup-dir` the other
two documents are unchanged. A new pure script, `scripts/test-notes-backup.mjs`, needing `sqlite3` on
`PATH`: against a temporary database made with `sqlite3` in WAL mode and holding a row, and a backup
folder whose name holds a space and an apostrophe, seeded with nine older copies
(`notes-2020-01-01.db` to `notes-2020-01-09.db`) and one unrelated file, a run leaves today's copy,
on which `PRAGMA integrity_check` answers `ok` and the row is found; exactly seven `notes-*.db`
remain, today's and the six newest seeded; the unrelated file survives and no `.partial` is left; a
second run on the same day succeeds and leaves seven; a missing database exits non-zero and deletes
nothing. Broken on purpose: keeping eight turns the retention case red, and writing straight to the
final name turns the second-run case red.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `node scripts/test-notes-backup.mjs` exits 0 with every case listed under Proof in the Specification, run with `sqlite3` on `PATH`.
- [ ] Keeping eight copies turns the retention case red, and writing straight to the final name turns the second-run case red, both recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `node scripts/test-install-services.mjs` exits 0 with the third document's cases, and without `--notes-backup-dir` the other two documents are unchanged.
- [ ] `docs/work-side-setup.md`, in its "Notes service" section, gives the option, where the copies go, that seven are kept and why, and how to restore one.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: an installed agent leaves at most seven daily copies of the notes database in the chosen folder, each passing `PRAGMA integrity_check`, proven by the tests.

## Tests
- unit: `scripts/test-notes-backup.mjs`, pure, against a temporary WAL database and a folder whose name holds a space and an apostrophe.
- unit: the third document's cases in `scripts/test-install-services.mjs`, parsed with `plistlib`.

## Recovery path
Uninstalling is `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/houston.notes-backup` and removing its plist from `~/Library/LaunchAgents`; the copies already in the folder are plain files. Restoring a copy is the procedure the setup guide gains: stop `houston.notes`, remove the `-wal` and `-shm` files beside the database, copy the backup over it, and start the service again.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `scripts/notes-backup.sh`, `scripts/test-notes-backup.mjs`, `scripts/install-services.sh`, `scripts/test-install-services.mjs`, `docs/work-side-setup.md`
**Reads only:** `scripts/update.sh`

A new script and its test, a third definition in the install script and its test, and the setup guide. Size M.
close_reason: scripts/notes-backup.sh copies the notes database with VACUUM INTO under a .partial name (apostrophes doubled), renames it to notes-YYYY-MM-DD.db and keeps the seven newest dated copies; install-services.sh learns houston.notes-backup through --notes-backup-dir (daily at 12:00 plus RunAtLoad, no KeepAlive, refusals for relative, inside the vault and missing --notes-vault, --print-notes-backup); the setup guide gives the option, retention, the reason and the restore steps. Keeping eight copies failed 'seven copies remain' and writing straight to the final name failed the second-run case. Review found the retention glob notes-*.db counting an undated notes-archive.db as the newest copy and deleting a real one; fixed with a dated glob and a seeded undated file that must survive (red before the fix). Review breaks: no apostrophe escaping, no missing-database check, a KeepAlive on the backup agent, all red. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build, test-notes-backup and test-install-services pass.

title: List an epic's planning, implementation and evidence notes in its Relacionados panel
description:
## What changes for the user
Today an epic's "Relacionados" panel shows its tracker story, beads and pipeline but none of the notes written about it. Once this lands the panel lists the planning, implementation and evidence notes that cite the epic, any of its beads or their tickets, plus the notes one link away, and still works, saying the notes are unavailable, when the notes service is stopped; an agent asking the hub about an identifier gets its notes too.

## Outcome
`lib/chain.ts` stays pure and gains `collectChainRefIds` and a `notes` part; both chain routes call the notes client in batches of 200 with the merge rules of the Specification; `GET /api/links/[id]` adds a top-level `notes`; the panel shows the notes groups in Portuguese in the bead drawer and the expanded epic, also when only notes are configured; `docs/chain.md` gains the fields.

## Context
The chain is phase 2's: a pure resolver that builds a bead's tracker item, its epic or descendants and its pipeline state, two routes that serve it (by project and bead, and by identifier for agents), and the panel the user named "Relacionados" on 2026-11-25 (it was "Cadeia"), shown in the bead drawer and in an expanded epic. This bead adds the notes, read from the notes service's refs route through the hub's notes client with `hop=1`, so the one-hop notes come in the same call; it builds against that route's pinned answer with a stub service. The refs route accepts at most 200 identifiers and splits its list on commas, which sets the batch size and is why an identifier holding a comma is left out.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's

  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead wires notes into the hub. It builds against the answers the notes service pins, with stub services or fixtures, and does not wait for the engine's own steps.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is B3. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A8** adds the `kind` and `refs` frontmatter fields, the `note_refs` table and the refs route, GET /api/notes/refs.
- **phase 2** ties each bead to its tracker story and pipeline: `external_ref` on beads, the value validators of `lib/config-values.ts`, the chain resolver `lib/chain.ts` (its step 7), the chain routes by project and by identifier, GET /api/links/[id] among them, with `docs/chain.md` (its step 8), and the "Relacionados" panel in the bead drawer and the expanded epic.

## Specification
`lib/chain.ts` stays pure, so `scripts/test-chain.mjs` keeps loading it without `server-only`:

- it exports `collectChainRefIds(bead, beads)`: for an epic, its id, every descendant's id and every
  `external_ref` among them; for any other bead, its id and its `external_ref`, never its siblings';
  de-duplicated without regard to case; an identifier containing `,`, which the `ids` list of A8
  would split, is left out;
- `resolveChain` takes an optional notes answer and adds a `notes` part: the notes grouped by `kind`
  (`plano`, `implementacao`, `evidencia`, `nota`), then `linked` and `linkedOmitted`.

Both route handlers call `lib/notes-service.ts` with `hop=1`, in batches of 200 identifiers, and stop
calling for the rest of the HTTP request (every batch, and in `GET /api/links/[id]` every bead and the
top-level lookup) after the first `unavailable`. With more than one batch, the direct notes are merged
by id (their `matchedRefs` joined), direct notes are dropped from the merged `linked`, `linked` is
de-duplicated by id, sorted by path and cut to 20, and `linkedOmitted` is the sum of each batch's
`linkedOmitted` plus what the cut removed. Each batch returns only its first 20 linked notes, so
across batches that sum is an upper bound, not a count; with one batch, the usual case, it is
exact. With the service unconfigured the part is
absent; stopped, `unavailable`, and everything else in the chain unchanged. `GET /api/links/[id]`
adds the notes part to each bead's chain and a top-level `notes` for the identifier itself, so an
identifier no bead carries still returns its notes. The chain section, phase 2's panel labelled
"Relacionados", is shown when `capabilities.chain || capabilities.notes`, in both places phase 2
gates it on `chain` alone, the drawer (`components/bead-detail-drawer.tsx`) and the expanded epic
(`components/epics-view.tsx`), with the groups in Portuguese ("Planejamento", "Implementação",
"Evidências", "Notas", "Notas ligadas"). With `chain` false there is no snapshot to confirm
anything, so the section shows the notes part alone, without the tracker and pipeline items phase 2
would mark "não confirmado"; and its quiet notice for a bead with nothing to show (phase 2) counts
notes too. `docs/chain.md` gains the `notes` fields.
