title: Add the search page, its sidebar link, launcher card and shortcut
description:
## What changes for the user
Today there is no way to search the work notes from the hub. Once this lands a "Busca" page, reached from the sidebar, the launcher or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F, finds any note with ranked results and highlighted snippets, filters by tag, folder and kind, pages through the results, and keeps the query in the address so back and reload keep it.

## Outcome
A /search page with the same minimal shell as the work page, a read-only proxy route to the notes service's search, the sidebar link and the launcher card shown when notes are configured, a shortcut component mounted for every page, the shortcut listed in the help dialog and in settings only when notes are configured, and the fixture the sprint and project browser tests need now that every page reads the capabilities.

## Context
It builds against the search answer and the snippet markers the notes service pins (STX and ETX around each match, rendered here as `<mark>` elements from React text, never as HTML), with fixtures for the proxy. The work page, its minimal shell, the sidebar's link group and the launcher's work card are phase 1's: /work is a page of its own with a minimal `AppProvider` and sidebars with no views, and the link group holds links shown by capability. The proxy validates its parameters with the service's own rules because the hub's notes client turns every non-2xx answer into "unavailable", and a bad address would otherwise read as a stopped service. The shortcut lives in a small component of its own, `components/search-shortcut.tsx`, inside the query provider, because the per-project keyboard layer is mounted only by the project pages.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name goes into any file, commit, pull request or
  bead; fixtures are synthetic. Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the
  internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's
  private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time.
- A bead that edits anything under `notes/`, or `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, also passes the Go gate,
  which needs Go 1.26 or later: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/houston`,
  each run inside `notes/`, and `scripts/check-notes-deps.sh`, which runs `go list -deps ./cmd/houston`
  inside `notes/` and fails, naming each offender, on any package the copy leaves out. `-o /dev/null`
  because a plain `go build ./cmd/houston` leaves a binary `notes/houston` behind.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that
  went red.
- This phase adds notes to Houston. The notes engine is a copy of kernl's (kernl is the user's own notes
  application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.
- This bead wires notes into the hub. It builds against the answers the notes service pins, with stub services or fixtures, and does not wait for the engine's own steps.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is B4. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

- **A9** adds the ranked search route, GET /api/search, with snippets, filters, paging and exact identifiers.
- **phase 1** frames the work dashboard: the loopback URL validator (`lib/loopback-url.ts`), the config machinery with atomic owner-only writes through PUT /api/config, the capabilities route that tells pages which optional features exist, a server-side reachability probe, the /work page with its minimal shell (its step 5), the sidebar's link group and the launcher's work card, and the doc checker `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`.

## Specification
- `/search`, a page of its own, built with the same minimal shell as `/work` (phase 1 step 5):
  `AppProvider` with a minimal value, `<Sidebar>` and `<MobileSidebar>` with no views,
  `SEARCH_PAGE_ID = "@search"` beside `ALL_PROJECT_ID`, the switcher reading "Busca" with the second
  line "busca de notas" (`components/project-switcher.tsx:70`) and no status dot,
  `projectTitle("Busca")`, `lang="pt-BR"`, and Portuguese unconfigured and unavailable states.
  Unlike `/work`'s shell, this one reads `useSearchParams()`, so `app/search/page.tsx` wraps it in
  `<Suspense>` with a Portuguese fallback; without the boundary the prerender of the page fails
  `npm run build`, which is why phase 1 notes that `/work` needs none.
- A query box, filters for tag, folder and kind, and ranked results with title, path, kind, tags and
  snippet; paged by the service's `limit` and `offset`. The query, the filters and the offset live in
  the URL, so back and reload keep them, and a change of the query or of a filter sets the offset
  back to 0; each request passes TanStack's `signal`, so a slower earlier search never overwrites a
  newer one.
- The hub proxies through `GET /api/notes/search`, a read (viewer mode leaves it alone) answered with
  `Cache-Control: no-store`, forwarding only `q`, `tag`, `folder`, `kind`, `limit` and `offset`;
  400 on an empty `q` and on a `kind`, `limit` or `offset` that A9 would refuse, checked here with
  A9's rules, because `lib/notes-service.ts` turns every non-2xx answer into `unavailable` and a bad
  address would otherwise read as a stopped service; 503 with
  `{ status: "unconfigured" | "unavailable", reason }`, which the page tells apart from zero hits.
- Reached by a "Busca" link in the sidebar's link group of phase 1 (a `Link`, never a button, so
  `scripts/test-all-sidebar.mjs:132-136` holds, calling `onProjectNavigate` to close the mobile
  sheet) and a launcher card after the built-in cards and "Trabalho", before the project cards,
  whatever the number of projects; both shown when `capabilities.notes`.
- The shortcut is handled by a small client component mounted inside the `QueryClientProvider` of
  `components/providers.tsx`, so it can read the capabilities; not in the per-project keyboard layer
  (`hooks/use-app-keyboard.ts`, mounted only by the project shell). It matches Cmd or Ctrl with
  Shift and `F`, compared after lower-casing `event.key`, which Shift makes `"F"`, and without Alt,
  a repeat or an event already handled; it acts only when `capabilities.notes` is true, no dialog or
  overlay is open (the check of `hooks/use-app-keyboard.ts:41-47`, exported), and the focus is not
  in an `input`, `textarea`, `select` or editable element, and calls `preventDefault()`. On
  `/search` itself it focuses the query box instead of navigating, which would drop the filters in
  the URL. It cannot fire while the focus is inside the framed dashboard, which is why the link
  exists. The shortcut list (`lib/keyboard-shortcuts.ts:33-45`) is rendered in two places, the help
  dialog (`components/keyboard-help-dialog.tsx:43`) and the settings view
  (`components/settings-view.tsx:293`); both show the entry only when `capabilities.notes` is true.
- Because `components/providers.tsx` wraps every page, the capabilities read now also happens on
  `/sprints` and `/sprints/[id]`, which phase 1 did not touch. The browser scripts that record or
  refuse unrouted reads get a fixture for it (`{ workDashboardUrl: null, chain: false, notes: false,
  obsidianVault: null }`): `scripts/test-sprint-run-ui.mjs` (its fallback at `:83` records every
  unrouted request, asserted exactly at `:130,188,272,287`), `scripts/test-sprints-ui.mjs`,
  `scripts/test-sprint-planning.mjs` and `scripts/test-all-projects-ui.mjs`.
- The command palette is left alone: it is mounted only in the project shell and filters its
  entries in the browser, which would hide a hit whose title does not contain the query.
- The snippet is rendered as React text, split on A9's STX and ETX markers into `<mark>` elements,
  never through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.

Proof: a browser script, `scripts/test-search-page.mjs`, with fixtures for the proxy route: typing
runs one request after a pause; filters and paging reach the request and the URL; reload keeps them;
changing a filter on the second page asks for offset 0; a slow first answer does not replace a later
one; the shortcut opens the page from a project page and from `/all`, focuses the query box on
`/search` without changing the URL, and does nothing while typing in an input, while a dialog is
open, or when `notes` is false; `kind=bogus` in the address answers 400 from the proxy, shown as an
invalid search and not as an unavailable service; after the capabilities answer arrives, the link,
the card and the shortcut's entry in the help dialog and the settings view are hidden without the
service; the unconfigured and unavailable states; a snippet carrying `<script>` is shown as text;
`npm run build` passes with the page. `scripts/test-all-sidebar.mjs`
gains "Busca" in the desktop and mobile navigation; `scripts/test-sprint-run-ui.mjs`,
`scripts/test-sprints-ui.mjs`, `scripts/test-sprint-planning.mjs` and
`scripts/test-all-projects-ui.mjs` pass with their new fixture.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `scripts/with-server.sh 3211 node scripts/test-search-page.mjs` exits 0, and again under `SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1`, with every case listed under Proof in the Specification.
- [ ] `scripts/test-all-sidebar.mjs` passes with "Busca" in the desktop and mobile navigation, and `scripts/test-sprint-run-ui.mjs`, `scripts/test-sprints-ui.mjs`, `scripts/test-sprint-planning.mjs` and `scripts/test-all-projects-ui.mjs` pass with their new fixture, each under the launch mode `AGENTS.md` gives it.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: a search from the hub returns ranked notes with snippets, filters and pages, proven with fixtures in both launch modes.

## Tests
- e2e: `scripts/test-search-page.mjs`, Playwright with fixtures for the proxy route, in both launch modes.
- regression: `scripts/test-all-sidebar.mjs` and the four sprint and project browser scripts with their new fixture.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `app/search/page.tsx`, `components/search-shell.tsx`, `app/api/notes/search/route.ts`, `lib/aggregate.ts`, `components/sidebar.tsx`, `components/launcher.tsx`, `components/project-switcher.tsx`, `components/providers.tsx`, `components/search-shortcut.tsx`, `hooks/use-app-keyboard.ts`, `lib/keyboard-shortcuts.ts`, `components/keyboard-help-dialog.tsx`, `components/settings-view.tsx`, `scripts/test-search-page.mjs`, `scripts/test-all-sidebar.mjs`, `scripts/test-sprint-run-ui.mjs`, `scripts/test-sprints-ui.mjs`, `scripts/test-sprint-planning.mjs`, `scripts/test-all-projects-ui.mjs`
**Reads only:** `lib/notes-service.ts`, `hooks/use-capabilities.ts`, `scripts/with-server.sh`, `AGENTS.md`

A page with its shell and proxy route, the shortcut component, the shared components and hooks it shows up in, and six browser tests. Size L. A split was considered, the page and proxy apart from the navigation and the shortcut, and rejected: both halves edit `scripts/test-search-page.mjs`, so it is one bead labelled by the wider radius.

## Context
Until a later phase adds an editor to the hub, Obsidian is where notes are edited. `encodeURI` would leave `#`, `&`, `+` and `?` unencoded, and `URLSearchParams` turns spaces into `+`, which Obsidian reads as a plus; both break paths a work vault really holds.   application, a separate repository) as it is at commit `488fbbe`, and it lives in `notes/` as a Go
  module of Houston's own, `github.com/gabrielassisxyz/houston/notes`. That module builds the `houston`
  executable: a notes service that indexes the work vault and serves it over loopback, answering which
  notes cite an identifier and a ranked search, and a CLI for it. The copy is a fork that kernl does not
  share: fixes made here do not travel to kernl, kernl's later fixes do not reach the copy, and nothing is
  ever written in kernl's repository or tracker. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this
  bead carries everything it needs from it.

## Names used below
The plan behind this bead numbers its steps: A1 to A13 build the notes engine in `notes/`, B1 to B7 wire it into the hub, and this bead is B5. Each step is a bead of this phase's epic, under the title that says what it does. The other steps and phases named below:

## Specification
A search result and a note in the chain open in Obsidian through
`obsidian://open?vault=<obsidianVault>&file=<path>`, both values encoded with `encodeURIComponent`
(never `encodeURI`, which leaves `#`, `&`, `+` and `?`, nor `URLSearchParams`, which turns spaces
into `+`), until the editor of phase 5 exists. The link has no `target="_blank"`, which would leave

description:
## What changes for the user
Until this is done the notes service has only indexed synthetic vaults. Once it passes it runs on the real work vault as a login service, every note has an id committed to the vault's git, and the cost of the first index is known.

## Outcome
The setup guide's "Notes service" section has been followed on the work machine up to the end of the first index: the vault's git committed, the binary built from this repository's `notes/` module, `houston preflight` run with no error, both login agents installed, and the id injection reviewed as one commit; the preflight's counts, the size of the injection commit and the cold start's duration are recorded in generic words. The hub's two notes settings are not set here: that comes with the search measurement, once the hub has those settings.

## Context
The notes service is the `houston` executable built from this repository's `notes/` module, a copy of the user's kernl notes engine. Its first run writes an id into every note that lacks one, which is why the vault's git is committed first and the preflight runs before anything is written. This waits for the CLI step, which brings in every fix of the engine (all but the `links` verb, which the first run does not use), for the request guard, and for the install step. The work machine pulls this public repository and never pushes, so the user reports the result in generic words and the bead is closed on the development machine in a tracker-only pull request. The public tracker never gets a note's name, a question asked, a count that identifies the vault, or any other work data beyond generic numbers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The vault's git was committed before the first run, and the id injection is reviewed as one commit.
- [ ] `houston preflight`, with `HOUSTON_VAULT` set, reported no error before the service was installed.
- [ ] The service runs as the login agent `houston.notes`, and `houston health` reports indexing finished.
- [ ] The preflight's counts, the injection commit's size and the cold start's duration are recorded in generic words.
- [ ] Done when: the notes service answers health with the first index finished on the work vault.

## Tests
- e2e: the first run, by hand, on the work machine.

## Recovery path
The commit made before the first run is the way back: stop the service with `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/houston.notes`, restore the vault to that commit, and delete the notes database, which a later run rebuilds.

## Blast radius
Confined to the work machine: the vault's git, the notes service's definition and its database. No file of
this repository is edited.

title: Set the hub's notes settings and measure search against about fifteen real questions
description:
## What changes for the user
Until this is done the hub does not know where the notes service is, and nobody knows whether text search is good enough for the work notes and documentation extracts. Once it is done the search page and the Obsidian links work on the work machine, and there is a number: how many of about fifteen real questions found what was wanted in the first five results.

## Outcome
The hub's `notesServiceUrl` (the service's root on 127.0.0.1, port 3301) and `obsidianVault` are set by the setup guide's procedure, through the settings API and never by editing the hub's config file while it runs; about fifteen real questions have been asked through the search page, each marked found or not found in the first five results, with the count recorded; the questions themselves stay on the work machine.

## Context
Search is text search with ranking, not semantic; this measurement is what says whether that is enough. The two settings are set here rather than at the first run because they need the hub's notes settings, and the results open in Obsidian, so this waits for the first run and for the Obsidian links step. The work machine pulls this public repository and never pushes, so the user reports the result in generic words and the bead is closed on the development machine in a tracker-only pull request. The public tracker never gets a note's name, a question asked, a count that identifies the vault, or any other work data beyond generic numbers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both settings were set through `PUT /api/config`, and the search page shows neither the unconfigured nor the unavailable state.
- [ ] A result opened from the search page opened the right note in Obsidian.
- [ ] About fifteen questions were asked through the search page.
- [ ] The count of questions answered in the first five results is recorded, and no question text is.
- [ ] The Relacionados panel of one real epic lists the notes that cite it or its beads.
- [ ] Done when: the hit count over about fifteen questions is known.

## Tests
- e2e: the questions, asked by hand on the work machine.

## Blast radius
Confined to the work machine: the hub's settings. No file of this repository is edited.

title: Check the sync client's placeholders and the service's open-file limit
description:
## Outcome
Two facts about the work machine are known: whether the sync client shows undownloaded files as empty
placeholders, and the notes service process's open-file limit.

## Context
The notes service skips empty placeholders without dropping their notes from the index, and on macOS its file watcher holds one descriptor per note; the service's login definition raises the soft limit to 16384 and the hard limit to 65536. Neither fact was ever checked on the work machine, and both need the service running there first. The work machine pulls this public repository and never pushes, so the user reports the result in generic words and the bead is closed on the development machine in a tracker-only pull request. The public tracker never gets a note's name, a question asked, a count that identifies the vault, or any other work data beyond generic numbers.

## Options
- **A · Placeholders are empty files and the limit is ample.** What changes: nothing; the defaults hold.
- **B · Placeholders exist or the limit is low.** What changes: the vault is kept fully downloaded, or the service definition's limit is raised, and a bead records the change.

## What decides it
`ls -l` on an undownloaded file in the vault, and the limit reported for the running service process.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both facts are recorded in generic words.
- [ ] Done when: the vault and the service are known to fit within the limits.

title: Phase 1: frame the work dashboard in Houston
description:
## Outcome
One site on the work machine shows the beads boards and the work dashboard: the collector's own page is
framed at /work, reached from the sidebar and the launcher only when its address is configured, and when
the collector does not answer the page says so instead of showing an empty frame.

## Context
The direction plan (outside the repository) splits the work hub into phases; phase 0 published this
repository, phase 1 is this epic, phase 2 adds the chain from a bead to its tracker story and pipeline.
The plan for this phase, reviewed in three rounds by two reviewers, is kept outside the repository;
each child carries what it needs from it.

## Success criteria
- [ ] A work dashboard address is validated as a 127.0.0.1 loopback URL — hou-rw9.1
- [ ] The config file holds the address, is written atomically with mode 0600, and can drop a key — hou-rw9.2
- [ ] Pages learn whether the dashboard is configured from an allowlisted capabilities answer — hou-rw9.3
- [ ] Houston's server tells a reachable collector from a stopped one in two seconds at most — hou-rw9.4
- [ ] The dashboard is framed at /work with its loading, unconfigured, self and unreachable states — hou-rw9.5
- [ ] The sidebar and the launcher lead to /work only when the address is configured — hou-rw9.6
- [ ] The setup guide covers the dashboard and a test guards every documented path — hou-rw9.7
- [ ] The full test matrix is green on main after the code lands — hou-rw9.8
- [ ] The real dashboard works framed on the work machine — hou-rw9.9

title: Validate the work dashboard URL as a 127.0.0.1 loopback address
description:
## What changes for the user
Today nothing checks an address Houston will connect to or frame: any string would be taken. Once
this lands, the address of the work dashboard is accepted only when it points at this machine on
127.0.0.1, without credentials, query or fragment, and is stored in one normalised form, so a typo or
a foreign host can never end up framed or probed.

## Outcome
A new pure module, `lib/loopback-url.ts`, exports `checkWorkDashboardUrl(value: unknown)`, which answers
`{ ok: true, url }` with the parser's normalised `href`, or `{ ok: false, reason }` with a non-empty
reason, by the rules below, and a pure test proves every rule and every refusal.

## Context
The existing request guard's `isAllowedHost` (`lib/request-guard.ts:65-74`) accepts any IP literal,
which is right for answering requests and wrong for choosing where the server connects, so it is not
reused. The module has no imports at all, like `lib/request-guard.ts`, so a pure test imports it
directly the way `scripts/test-request-guard.mjs:6` does. The config key that uses it lands in the next
bead.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the
  branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and
  commit messages, with the list kept in the user's private notes outside the repository; a failed or
  unavailable sweep blocks the push, and the close reason records only that it passed.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time, so two
  landings never carry different copies of `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
- Read before writing a route or a page, because this Next.js differs from older versions:
  `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md` and
  `.../03-file-conventions/page.md`.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after
  the last one); pure-script guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- The phase this bead belongs to frames the work dashboard, a page served by a local collector program
  on the work machine, inside Houston at the route /work, and adds the config key `workDashboardUrl`
  that holds that page's address. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries
  everything it needs from it.

## Specification
A new module, `lib/loopback-url.ts`, with no imports at all, like `lib/request-guard.ts`
(`:20-21`), so a pure test can import it directly the way `scripts/test-request-guard.mjs:6`
does. It uses no TypeScript syntax that type stripping cannot erase (no `enum`, no parameter
properties, no `namespace`).

It exports one function, `checkWorkDashboardUrl(value: unknown)`, which answers
`{ ok: true, url }` or `{ ok: false, reason }`, `reason` a non-empty sentence. Rules, in order:

- a primitive string, checked before anything is coerced: an array, or an object whose
  `toString` returns a valid URL, is refused;
- trimmed, then not empty;
- no ASCII control character (`U+0000` to `U+001F`, `U+007F`) left after the trim: the URL
  parser silently drops a tab, a line feed or a carriage return inside the value, and the trim
  has already removed the ones around it;
- parsed by `URL`; a parse failure is refused;
- protocol `http:` or `https:`;
- empty `username` and `password`;
- `hostname` exactly `127.0.0.1` after the URL parser's own normalisation. That accepts
  spellings the parser turns into `127.0.0.1` (`http://2130706433/`), which name the same
  host, and refuses `localhost`, `127.0.0.2`, `[::1]` and `127.0.0.1.nip.io`. The hub is opened
  on `127.0.0.1` and the browser frames this address, so the two share the host;
- no query and no fragment, including a bare `?` or `#`: `URL.search` and `URL.hash` are empty
  strings for `http://127.0.0.1/?` and `http://127.0.0.1/#`, so the check is that the
  serialised `href` contains neither character (a percent-encoded `%3F` or `%23` in the path
  stays allowed). The page appends its own fragment (step 5);
- a port from 1 to 65535, or the default; `:0` parses but can never be reached, so it is refused;
- any path;
- `url` is the parser's `href`, so what is stored is normalised (trimmed, integer IPv4 written
  as `127.0.0.1`, a default port dropped, a trailing slash added to an empty path).

`isAllowedHost` in `lib/request-guard.ts:65-74` is not reused: it accepts any IP literal,
which is right for answering a request and wrong for choosing where the server connects.

Proof: `node scripts/test-loopback-url.mjs` passes. For every accepted case it asserts the exact
normalised `url`; for every refused case, a non-empty `reason`; and for `""` and `"   "` a
reason distinct from the parse-failure one (it matches `/empty/i`, while the reason for
`not a url` does not). The URL parser itself strips surrounding whitespace and throws on an
empty string, so without that distinction removing the empty check or the trim would change
nothing a test sees. Cases: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`, `https://127.0.0.1/dash`,
`http://2130706433:8000`, `http://127.0.0.1:80/`, `http://127.0.0.1:8000/a%3Fb%23c`, a value with
surrounding spaces, a value with a trailing line feed; refused `""`, `"   "`, `not a url`,
`http://user:pw@127.0.0.1:8000/`, `http://user@127.0.0.1/`, `http://:pw@127.0.0.1/`, `ftp://127.0.0.1/`, `javascript:alert(1)`,
`http://localhost:8000/`, `http://127.0.0.2/`, `http://[::1]/`, `http://127.0.0.1.nip.io/`,
`http://127.0.0.1:8000/?a=1`, `.../?`, `.../#x`, `.../#`, `.../?#`, `http://127.0.0.1:0/`, a number,
`null`, `["http://127.0.0.1:8000/"]` (an empty array would coerce to `""` and test the empty check
instead), and an object with a URL-shaped `toString`; and, for the control-character rule, an
embedded tab (`"http://127.0.0.1:8000/a\tb"`), line feed and carriage return, and a `\x00` and a
`\x7f` anywhere in the value. The accepted trailing line feed pins the rule after the trim.
Broken on purpose, one at a time, each turns a named case red: the primitive check, the empty
check, the trim, the control-character check (removed, and separately moved before the trim),
the parse failure, the protocol list, each half of the credential check, the exact host
(accepting any hostname starting with `127.0.0.1`), the query and fragment check (decoding
before checking), the `:0` port check, and returning the input instead of `href`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `lib/loopback-url.ts` has no import statement and uses no syntax type stripping cannot erase (no `enum`, no parameter properties, no `namespace`).
- [ ] `node scripts/test-loopback-url.mjs` exits 0 and asserts the exact normalised URL for each of the 6 accepted cases and a non-empty reason for each refused case listed in the Specification.
- [ ] The empty and whitespace-only inputs are refused with a reason matching /empty/i, and that reason differs from the one for an unparseable string.
- [ ] Each deliberate break listed in the Specification turns a named assertion red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: the validator and its pure test are on `main` and every refusal case in the Specification is a named assertion.

## Tests
- unit: `scripts/test-loopback-url.mjs`, a pure table test over accepted and refused inputs, run with `node` directly.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `lib/loopback-url.ts`, `scripts/test-loopback-url.mjs`
**Reads only:** `lib/request-guard.ts`, `scripts/test-request-guard.mjs`

Two new files, no existing file changes. Size S: one module and its test.
close_reason: lib/loopback-url.ts and its pure test scripts/test-loopback-url.mjs. Every break the Specification lists turned a named assertion red (13 rows, e.g. exact host loosened to startsWith -> '127.0.0.1.nip.io' refused case failed). Review added ws and file URLs on 127.0.0.1 after a protocol check rewritten as an ftp-only denylist survived; it now fails 'websocket protocol on the loopback host should be refused'. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build and the test pass.

title: Add the workDashboardUrl config key with atomic owner-only writes
description:
## What changes for the user
Today Houston's config file is rewritten in place, readable by anyone on the machine, with any write
failure silently swallowed, and there is no way to remove a key. Once this lands the work dashboard's
address can be set and cleared through the config route or by hand, an invalid value on disk is
ignored with a warning instead of silently, and the file is replaced atomically and kept readable by
its owner only, which the secret a later phase stores there needs.

## Outcome
`lib/config.ts` knows `workDashboardUrl` (validated on read with a one-time warning, absent rather than
`undefined` when unset), writes the file through a temporary file of mode `0600` and a rename, can delete
a key from the file, and `saveConfig` validates the new key; the config route accepts, refuses and
clears it. `scripts/test-actor-default.mjs` moves to a loader that survives `lib/config.ts`'s new
relative import, and a new `scripts/test-work-config.mjs` proves every rule.

## Context
`lib/config.ts` reads the file once per server start into a module-level cache and merges the file under
the in-memory config on every write (`:219-234`), so a key added by hand since the start survives an
unrelated write; that rule must keep holding. The validator comes from the bead that adds
`lib/loopback-url.ts`.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the
  branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and
  commit messages, with the list kept in the user's private notes outside the repository; a failed or
  unavailable sweep blocks the push, and the close reason records only that it passed.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time, so two
  landings never carry different copies of `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
- Read before writing a route or a page, because this Next.js differs from older versions:
  `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md` and
  `.../03-file-conventions/page.md`.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after
  the last one); pure-script guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- The phase this bead belongs to frames the work dashboard, a page served by a local collector program
  on the work machine, inside Houston at the route /work, and adds the config key `workDashboardUrl`
  that holds that page's address. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries
  everything it needs from it.

## Two facts every config test needs

- `lib/config.ts` imports only `server-only` and `node:*` today, which is why
  `scripts/test-actor-default.mjs:23-36` can load it with a native `import()` under
  `--conditions=react-server`. Step 2 makes it import `./loopback-url`. Node's native ESM
  loader refuses an extensionless relative import (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, checked on Node
  v24.18.0), and writing `./loopback-url.ts` breaks `npm run build` because `tsconfig.json`
  does not set `allowImportingTsExtensions`. So every script that loads `lib/config.ts`
  switches to the TypeScript-transpile-then-`vm` loader of `scripts/test-sprints.mjs:14-24`,
  which resolves `./name` to `lib/name.ts` and stubs `server-only`, run inside a child process
  so each case keeps its own `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, working directory, module cache and stderr.
  Three adjustments to that loader:
  1. its resolver knows only `./sprint-model` (`:21`); it resolves any `./name` to `lib/name.ts`
     instead, memoized by name, and keeps stubbing `server-only`;
  2. its `vm.runInNewContext` sandbox (`:22`) passes only `exports`, `require`, `structuredClone`,
     `Date` and `process`, so `console` and `URL` are added (`lib/config.ts` will call
     `console.warn`, `lib/loopback-url.ts` calls `new URL`). Errors built inside that context are
     not `instanceof` the host's `Error`: a test checks `code === "invalid_config"` and the
     `ConfigError` the loaded module exports. Objects and arrays built there carry that
     context's prototypes too, so a deep-equality assertion compares them through `plain()`
     (`scripts/test-sprints.mjs:25-26`);
  3. the child runs with a throwaway working directory outside the repository, where a bare
     `import "typescript"` in a `node -e` script cannot be resolved (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`). The
     test re-executes itself as the child (`process.argv[1]`, with an environment variable naming
     the case), so no helper file lands among the test scripts and `typescript` resolves from the
     script's own location. The check for that variable comes first, before any of the parent's
     setup: `scripts/test-actor-default.mjs:12-19` creates a scratch directory and runs
     `git init` at the top level, which a child must neither repeat nor leak. The parent starts
     each child with `spawnSync` and `encoding: "utf8"`, not the `execFileSync` of `:34`, which
     returns only stdout on success, so the stderr assertions of step 2 can read the warning.
- `getConfig()` registers `repoPath` from the file, else `BEADS_REPO`, else the working directory
  as a project, and writes the file, when the file has no `projects` and that directory has a
  `.beads/` (`lib/config.ts:274-291`). This repository has one. Every child process runs in a
  throwaway directory without `.beads/`, as `scripts/test-actor-default.mjs:14-16` already does,
  and with `BEADS_REPO` removed from its environment, as that script removes `BEADS_ACTOR`
  (`:33`). It does not remove `BEADS_REPO` today, so it gains that removal beside the other one.

## Specification
In `lib/config.ts`:

- `AppConfig` (`:25-42`) gets `workDashboardUrl?: string`. It is a string or absent; `null` is
  never stored or returned.
- Read, in `getConfig` (`:236-293`): when the key is present on disk, a value that passes the
  validator is kept in its normalised `url` form; one that fails is left out and logged once
  with `console.warn`, as `[houston] config: workDashboardUrl ignored: <reason>`; the server
  keeps starting. Today an invalid value on disk falls back silently (`:263-270`), which is the
  pattern this key does not follow.
- When unset, the property is absent from the object, never present as `undefined`. `persist`
  spreads the in-memory config over the file (`:229`), and an own property holding `undefined`
  would make `JSON.stringify` drop a value added to the file by hand since the start, which
  breaks the rule that an unrelated write keeps it.
- Write, in `persist` (`:219-234`), the pattern `lib/sprints.ts:57-67` already uses: write a
  UUID-named temporary file in the config directory with mode `0o600`, rename it over
  `config.json`, and remove the temporary file in `finally`. The previous file stays intact
  until the rename succeeds. Both `getConfig` and `persist` look into what they read from disk
  only when it is a plain, non-null, non-array object, so a corrupt `null`, `[]` or string never
  throws or spreads indices. A failure is logged with `console.warn`, prefixed
  `[houston] config:`, instead of swallowed by the empty `catch` (`:231-233`); `persist` stays best-effort and keeps the new value in
  memory, because `touchProject` and `addProject` call it on every project open and must not
  start failing.
- `persist` takes an optional list of keys to delete from the file after the merge. Only the
  removal below passes one. Every other write keeps merging the file under the in-memory
  config, as today.
- `saveConfig` (`:308-315`) takes a save-patch type of its own, in which `workDashboardUrl` is
  `string | null`. A string is validated and normalised through `checkWorkDashboardUrl`; a
  refusal throws `ConfigError` with code `invalid_config` and changes nothing. `null` clones the
  cached config, deletes the property, and passes `["workDashboardUrl"]` to `persist`. A patch
  property whose value is `undefined` is ignored rather than copied.

In `app/api/config/route.ts`, `patchSchema` (`:8-13`) gets
`workDashboardUrl: z.string().nullable().optional()`. Exactly `""` or `null` becomes `null` before
`saveConfig`; any other string goes to `saveConfig`, whose
`ConfigError` answers 400 through `fail()` (`lib/api.ts:39-41`). `GET` keeps answering the
whole config, the new key included.

Proof: `scripts/test-work-config.mjs`, a script with a pure half and a server half, run once
bare and once through `scripts/with-server.sh`.

- `scripts/test-actor-default.mjs` moves to the loader of "Two facts every config test needs"
  and still passes.
- Pure half, one child process per case, throwaway config directory and working directory,
  `process.umask(0o022)` set and asserted in the child so the mode check does not depend on
  the caller's umask:
  - a valid value on disk is read, normalised; an invalid string, and separately a falsy invalid
    value (`null`, `""`), are each left out with `[houston] config: workDashboardUrl ignored:`
    written exactly once on stderr across two `getConfig()` calls; an absent one leaves no own
    property; a file holding `null`, `[]` or a string is read as empty without throwing; and a
    `saveConfig` over a file holding `"corrupt"`, and separately `["x"]`, writes a plain object
    with no index keys (`"0"`, `"1"`, ...), which is what the guard in `persist` prevents
    (today `lib/config.ts:225,229` spreads whatever the file held; `[]` spreads nothing, so it
    would not catch the mutation);
  - starting from an existing `config.json` of mode `0644`, after `saveConfig` the file has mode
    `0600` and the directory holds no temporary file;
  - starting from a file that already holds `pollIntervalMs: 30000`, a key the test adds to the
    file by hand and a `workDashboardUrl` it adds by hand after the first `getConfig` both
    survive an unrelated `saveConfig({ pollIntervalMs: 15000 })`, and the file records
    `pollIntervalMs: 15000` (only a key on both sides with different values catches a reversed
    merge);
  - `saveConfig({ pollIntervalMs: 15000, workDashboardUrl: undefined })` leaves an existing
    `workDashboardUrl` intact in memory and on disk;
  - `saveConfig({ workDashboardUrl: null })` removes the key from the file, and
    `Object.hasOwn(getConfig(), "workDashboardUrl")` is false (assigning `undefined` instead of
    deleting would pass a plain equality check and break the next unrelated save);
  - starting with a valid `workDashboardUrl` and `pollIntervalMs: 30000`,
    `saveConfig({ pollIntervalMs: 15000, workDashboardUrl: "http://localhost/" })` throws the
    loaded `ConfigError` with `code === "invalid_config"`, the file is byte-for-byte unchanged, and
    neither value changes in `getConfig()`;
  - starting from an existing `config.json`, with `fs.renameSync` replaced, through the loader's
    `node:fs` hook before `lib/config.ts` loads, by one that throws: the old file's bytes are
    unchanged, the `[houston] config:` warning is on stderr, no temporary file remains,
    `saveConfig` does not throw, and `getConfig()` returns the new value. This case fails if
    `persist` writes `config.json` directly.
- Server half, under `SCOTTY_TEST_URL`: `PUT` with a valid value answers 200 and `GET` returns
  it normalised; an unrelated `PUT` (`{ pollIntervalMs: 15000 }`) keeps `workDashboardUrl`
  intact; `PUT` with `http://localhost:8000/` and `PUT` with `"   "` each answer 400
  `invalid_config` and leave the value unchanged; `PUT` with `""`, and separately with `null`,
  removes it from `GET`. It clears the key and restores `pollIntervalMs` in `finally`.
- Broken on purpose, one at a time, each turns a named case red: the warning, the plain-object
  guard in `persist`, the absence of an own property for an unset value, the merge order
  (in-memory over disk), the rename (writing directly), the mode, the failure warning, the
  clean-up of the temporary file, keeping the value in memory after a failed write, the
  normalisation, refusal without mutation, the removal in `lib/config.ts`, and the conversion of
  `""` to `null` in `app/api/config/route.ts`. The `lib/config.ts` mutations are run against the
  pure half directly, `node scripts/test-work-config.mjs`, as "Preconditions" says of pure
  guards; the route's goes through `scripts/mutate-check.py`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `node scripts/test-actor-default.mjs` exits 0 after moving to the child-process loader described under "Two facts every config test needs".
- [ ] `node scripts/test-work-config.mjs` exits 0 with every pure case of the Specification as a named assertion, including the 0644-to-0600 mode change, the rename-failure case and the merge-order case.
- [ ] `scripts/with-server.sh 3211 node scripts/test-work-config.mjs` exits 0 with the server cases of the Specification, and again under `SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1`.
- [ ] No child process of either script inherits `BEADS_REPO` or runs in a directory holding a `.beads` folder.
- [ ] Each deliberate break listed in the Specification turns a named assertion red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: the key, the atomic write and the removal are on `main`, and both halves of the new script pass.

## Tests
- unit: the pure half of `scripts/test-work-config.mjs`, one child process per case with a throwaway config directory and working directory.
- integration: the server half of the same script, run through `scripts/with-server.sh`, against the config route.
- regression: `scripts/test-actor-default.mjs`, migrated to the new loader.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `lib/config.ts`, `app/api/config/route.ts`, `scripts/test-actor-default.mjs`, `scripts/test-work-config.mjs`
**Reads only:** `lib/loopback-url.ts`, `lib/sprints.ts`, `lib/api.ts`, `scripts/test-sprints.mjs`, `scripts/with-server.sh`

One module and its route, one migrated test and one new test. Size M.
close_reason: lib/config.ts gains workDashboardUrl (absent when unset, validated and normalised through checkWorkDashboardUrl, an invalid value on disk left out with one '[houston] config: workDashboardUrl ignored:' warning), persist writes through a UUID-named 0600 temp file renamed over config.json with the plain-object guard and a logged failure, saveConfig takes string | null with null removing the key from the file; the config route turns "" or null into a removal and answers 400 invalid_config through fail(). Every break the Specification lists turned a named case red, e.g. the removal assigning undefined failed 'removal leaves no own property', the route's "" conversion went red through mutate-check. Review breaks: copying an undefined patch value and a second warning went red; removing the read-side plain-object guard survived as an equivalent mutant (a corrupt file already takes the no-projects path). test-actor-default moved to the new loader. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build, test-work-config both halves and test-actor-default pass.

title: Add the capabilities route that tells pages which optional features exist
description:
## What changes for the user
Today a page has no way to know whether the work dashboard is configured, so it could not decide to
show or hide its link. Once this lands Houston answers that question in one small read that never
exposes the rest of the config.

## Outcome
A route answers GET on the capabilities endpoint with exactly `{ "workDashboardUrl": string | null }`,
built field by field and sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`; its client call and hook come with the
page that first uses them.

## Context
The config route answers the whole config today (`app/api/config/route.ts:15-17,26`), and a later phase
adds a secret to the config, so the browser-facing answer is an explicit allowlist from the start.
Later phases add their own fields to this answer.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the
  branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and
  commit messages, with the list kept in the user's private notes outside the repository; a failed or
