- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time, so two
  landings never carry different copies of `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
- Read before writing a route or a page, because this Next.js differs from older versions:
  `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md` and
  `.../03-file-conventions/page.md`.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after
  the last one); pure-script guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- The phase this bead belongs to frames the work dashboard, a page served by a local collector program
  on the work machine, inside Houston at the route /work, and adds the config key `workDashboardUrl`
  that holds that page's address. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries
  everything it needs from it.

## Specification
`app/api/capabilities/route.ts`: `GET` answers exactly `{ workDashboardUrl: string | null }`,
built field by field, never by spreading the config, through `NextResponse.json` with
`Cache-Control: no-store`, as `app/api/viewer-mode/route.ts:7,10-12` does (`ok()` in `lib/api.ts:7-9`
takes only a status, so using it out of habit would drop the header). It is a
read, so viewer mode does not touch it (`proxy.ts:57-62`). Later phases add their own fields to
this answer; phase 1 adds only this one. Route handlers are dynamic by default in this Next.js
version, so no segment config is needed.

The client call and the hook land in step 5, their first consumer, so this step and step 4
touch disjoint files.

Proof: the server half of `scripts/test-work-config.mjs` asserts that `cache-control` contains
`no-store` and deep-equals the whole body:
`{ workDashboardUrl: null }` before the key is set, `{ workDashboardUrl: <normalised> }` after,
and `{ workDashboardUrl: null }` again after clearing with `""`; one more read, sent with
`Cookie: scotty-viewer-mode=read-only` while the key is set, answers 200 with the same body.
Broken on purpose, one at a time:
spreading `getConfig()` fails the exact body, and answering through `ok()` fails the
`cache-control` assertion.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The route file `app/api/capabilities/route.ts` answers through `NextResponse.json` with a no-store Cache-Control header, never through `ok()`.
- [ ] The server half of `scripts/test-work-config.mjs` deep-equals the whole body before the key is set, after it is set, and after it is cleared, and asserts the no-store header.
- [ ] Spreading `getConfig()` into the answer, and answering through `ok()`, each turn a named assertion red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: the route is on `main` and its answer is proven to carry nothing but the one field.

## Tests
- integration: the server half of `scripts/test-work-config.mjs`, through `scripts/with-server.sh`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `app/api/capabilities/route.ts`, `scripts/test-work-config.mjs`
**Reads only:** `app/api/viewer-mode/route.ts`, `lib/config.ts`, `lib/api.ts`, `scripts/with-server.sh`

One new route and the extension of one test. Size S.
close_reason: app/api/capabilities/route.ts answers exactly { workDashboardUrl: string | null }, built field by field, through NextResponse.json with Cache-Control: no-store; the server half of scripts/test-work-config.mjs deep-equals the body before the key is set, after, after clearing with "", and under the read-only viewer cookie, and asserts the header. Spreading getConfig() failed 'capabilities is null before the key is set' and answering through ok() failed 'capabilities answers no-store'. Review break (dropping the null fallback) also failed the before-set case. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build and both halves of test-work-config pass.

title: Probe the work dashboard's reachability from Houston's server side
description:
## What changes for the user Today a frame whose page refused to connect looks exactly like a frame that loaded, so a stopped collector would leave an empty box on screen. Once this lands Houston can tell, in two seconds at most, whether the collector answers, without ever being usable by another web page to hammer it. ## Outcome A POST route under the work API namespace probes the configured address once with a two-second timeout and the page's own cancellation, never follows a redirect, refuses Houston's own address, and answers `{ configured, reachable, reason? }` with `Cache-Control: no-store`; a server-backed test proves each rule with test-owned HTTP servers. ## Context A browser cannot distinguish a refused connection from a loaded frame (both fire `load`), so the check runs on the server. It is a POST, although it changes nothing, so it goes through the request guard's `Origin` and `Sec-Fetch-Site` checks (`lib/request-guard.ts:65-73,76-88`); a GET could be triggered by any open page. ## Rules for this work - Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host, repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and commit messages, with the list kept in the user's private notes outside the repository; a failed or unavailable sweep blocks the push, and the close reason records only that it passed. - Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md` ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches, each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time, so two landings never carry different copies of `.beads/issues.jsonl`. - Read before writing a route or a page, because this Next.js differs from older versions: `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md` and `.../03-file-conventions/page.md`. - Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after the last one); pure-script guards are broken and run directly with `node`. - The phase this bead belongs to frames the work dashboard, a page served by a local collector program on the work machine, inside Houston at the route /work, and adds the config key `workDashboardUrl` that holds that page's address. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries everything it needs from it. ## Specification `app/api/work/probe/route.ts`, `POST`, answered through `NextResponse.json` with `Cache-Control: no-store`. It lives under `/api/work/`, the namespace phase 4's collection proxy uses. A `POST`, not a `GET`, although it changes nothing: the request guard lets every safe method through after checking only the host (`lib/request-guard.ts:65-73,76-88`), so a `GET` could be triggered by any page open in the browser, over and over, making Houston open two-second requests to the collector. A `POST` goes through the guard's `Origin` and `Sec-Fetch-Site` checks. Viewer mode does not cover `/api/work/` (`proxy.ts:57-62`), so it stays available there. - Key unset: `{ configured: false }`, without any outbound request. - A configured URL whose origin is Houston's own is refused as `{ configured: true, reachable: false, reason: "self" }` without any outbound request: the hub and the collector are distinct services, and framing Houston inside itself helps nobody. Houston's own address is taken two ways, because Next may put its internal listening host name in `request.url` (`app/api/viewer-mode/route.ts:17-21` meets the same problem): `new URL(request.url)`, and a URL parsed (inside a `try`) from the request's protocol and the `Host` header, so default ports and case are normalised by the parser and not compared as strings. The target is self when its origin equals either, or when its scheme and port match either one's and that one's `hostname`, with surrounding brackets stripped, is a local alias (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`, `0.0.0.0`, `::`). The parser keeps the brackets of an IPv6 literal (`new URL("http://[::1]:3300/").hostname` is `"[::1]"`, checked on Node v24.18.0), so without the strip neither IPv6 alias ever matches. This closes the gap of a server opened on `localhost` or `[::1]`, or listening on `0.0.0.0` or `::`. The decision is a pure function, `isSelfTarget(target, requestUrl, hostHeader)`, in a new `lib/work-probe.ts` with no imports, like `lib/loopback-url.ts` (step 1), so a pure test reaches every combination of `request.url` and `Host`, which a test server listening on one address cannot; the route only calls it. - Otherwise one `fetch` of the configured URL with `method: "GET"`, `redirect: "manual"`, `cache: "no-store"` and `signal: AbortSignal.any([request.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(2000)])`: the per-attempt timeout the launcher uses (`bin/houston-web.mjs:126-146`), and the page's own cancellation, so a probe the page gave up on stops at once. Once `fetch` resolves, the collector is reachable, whatever the status, a redirect included; a redirect is never followed, so the probe never connects anywhere but the validated address. When `response.body` is not null it is cancelled as best-effort clean-up (`await response.body.cancel().catch(() => {})`); a missing body or a failed cancellation does not change the answer. A network error or the timeout is unreachable. Answer: `{ configured: true, reachable }`. The browser cannot do this itself: a frame whose connection was refused and a frame that loaded fire the same `load` event. Proof: `scripts/test-work-probe.mjs`, a script with a pure half and a server half, run once bare and once through `scripts/with-server.sh`. The pure half imports `lib/work-probe.ts` directly, as `scripts/test-request-guard.mjs:6` does, and asserts `isSelfTarget` for a target of `http://127.0.0.1:

/`: true for a `requestUrl` of that origin; true for a `requestUrl` on `http://0.0.0.0:

` and on `http://[::]:

`, each with a `Host` of `127.0.0.1:

` and with no `Host`; true for a `Host` of `localhost:

` and of `[::1]:

` with a `requestUrl` on `localhost:

`; true for a `requestUrl` on another port with a `Host` of `127.0.0.1:

`, where only the `Host` candidate decides; true for the target `http://127.0.0.1/` against a `Host` of `127.0.0.1:80`, the default port written on one side only; false for another port and for another scheme; and no throw for a malformed `Host`. Its mutations, each turning a named case red (the bracket strip, the alias branch, the `Host` candidate, the `try` around its parse), are run directly with `node scripts/test-work-probe.mjs`, as "Preconditions" says of pure guards. The server half, under `SCOTTY_TEST_URL`, uses its own HTTP servers on `127.0.0.1:0`, the pattern of `scripts/test-tracker-texts.mjs:51-61`, each closed with `closeAllConnections()` and then an awaited `close()`, because the server's `fetch` keeps connections alive and an unawaited close races the next probe (and a later re-bind of the same port). Every request the test sends to the probe carries `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(4000)`, so breaking the server's timeout on purpose fails quickly instead of waiting for Node's 300-second header timeout: - every answer the `POST` handler gives carries `cache-control: no-store` (the refusals below come from Next and from `proxy.ts:52`, not from the handler, and are not checked for the header); - a `POST` carrying `Cookie: scotty-viewer-mode=read-only` still probes and answers 200; - `GET /api/work/probe` is not implemented; a `POST` carrying a foreign `Origin` is refused before any request reaches the collector (the collector fixture counts none), while a `POST` with no `Origin`, as the test's own, probes; - unset: `configured: false`; - Houston's own address (`SCOTTY_TEST_URL` first, so a broken check fails before `${SCOTTY_TEST_URL}/api/work/probe` could call itself; then that one; and a request carrying `Host: localhost:`, sent through `node:http`'s `request` with `setHost: false` as `scripts/test-request-guard.mjs:44-55` does, because Node's `fetch` replaces a custom `Host` with the address it connects to, checked on Node v24.18.0): exactly `{ configured: true, reachable: false, reason: "self" }`, without waiting for the timeout. Without the check the first answers `reachable: true` and the second calls itself. The wrapper's server listens on `127.0.0.1` (`scripts/with-server.sh:74`) and Next builds `request.url` from that, so here the third case proves the route's wiring, and the alias and `Host` branches are proven by the pure half. (The production server does not log incoming requests, so the proof is the answer, not a log); - answering 200, 500 and 204 (no body): reachable; - answering 302 to a second test server: reachable, and the second server records no request; - headers followed by a body that never ends (`writeHead(200)` and `flushHeaders()`): reachable promptly, and the fixture sees its socket close within 1,000 ms. The probe's two-second timeout would close it at about two seconds even with the cancellation removed (measured on Node v24.18.0), so a longer wait would let that mutation pass; - the first server closed: unreachable; - a server that accepts the connection and never answers: unreachable in under 3 seconds, and the fixture sees the accepted socket close after the abort; - the same hanging server, with the test's own `POST` aborted about 150 ms after it is sent: the fixture sees the accepted socket close well inside 1,000 ms, which only `request.signal` in `AbortSignal.any` can do before the two-second timeout. It clears the key and closes every server in `finally`. Broken on purpose, one at a time, each turns a different case red: the unset short-circuit, the self refusal, "any status is reachable", `redirect: "manual"`, the timeout, forwarding `request.signal`, the null-body guard (broken as `response.body!.cancel()`, since deleting the guard would not type-check under `strict`), the body cancellation, and the `Cache-Control` header. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `node scripts/test-work-probe.mjs` exits 0 with the pure `isSelfTarget` cases of the Specification. - [ ] `scripts/with-server.sh 3211 node scripts/test-work-probe.mjs` exits 0, and again under `SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1`, with every case of the Specification as a named assertion. - [ ] A GET to the probe route is not implemented, and a POST with a foreign Origin is refused before any request reaches the collector fixture. - [ ] The hanging-server case answers unreachable in under 3 seconds and the endless-body case sees its socket close within 1,000 ms. - [ ] Every request the test sends to the probe carries a 4-second abort signal, and every fixture server is closed with closeAllConnections and an awaited close. - [ ] Each deliberate break listed in the Specification turns a different named assertion red, recorded in the close reason. - [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass. - [ ] Done when: the probe route is on `main` and every rule of the Specification has a case that fails without it. ## Tests - unit: the pure half of `scripts/test-work-probe.mjs`, over `isSelfTarget`. - integration: its server half, with its own HTTP servers on 127.0.0.1 port 0 (200, 500, 204, redirect, endless body, closed, hanging). ## Blast radius **Edits:** `app/api/work/probe/route.ts`, `lib/work-probe.ts`, `scripts/test-work-probe.mjs` **Reads only:** `lib/config.ts`, `lib/request-guard.ts`, `app/api/viewer-mode/route.ts`, `bin/houston-web.mjs`, `scripts/test-tracker-texts.mjs`, `scripts/with-server.sh` One new route, its pure helper and one new test. Size S.
close_reason: POST /api/work/probe answers { configured: false } when no address is set, refuses Houston's own address as self (lib/work-probe.ts isSelfTarget, over the request URL and the Host header, local aliases with brackets stripped), and otherwise fetches the configured address once with redirect manual, a 2-second timeout joined to the page's signal, and the body cancelled: any status is reachable, an error or the timeout unreachable, Cache-Control no-store. Every listed break red, e.g. following redirects failed '302: the redirect target saw no request', dropping the body cancel failed 'endless-body socket close', the self refusal removed failed 'SCOTTY_TEST_URL as the key: exactly self'. Review breaks: the alias branch ignoring the port failed 'another port: not self', ignoring the scheme failed 'another scheme: not self'. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build, the pure half and the server half both default and SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1 pass.

title: Frame the work dashboard on its own page, with its loading and failure states
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the work dashboard lives in a separate browser tab, apart from the boards. Once this lands it opens
inside Houston, at full height, beside the same sidebar as every other page; a link to a given incident
opens that incident inside the frame; and when the collector is stopped or the address is not set, the
page says so in Portuguese and offers to try again instead of showing an empty box.

## Outcome
A route /work renders a client shell with Houston's sidebar (no view buttons, the switcher reading
"Trabalho"), the probe-driven states, and an iframe of the configured page that receives the hub's URL
fragment one way; the capabilities and probe client calls and hooks exist; a browser test against the
real server and a synthetic dashboard proves the states, the frame, the fragment and the layout.

## Context
The all-projects page is the closest model, but it mounts the full provider with live data; /work mounts
the same `AppProvider` with a minimal value of its own. The sidebar gets optional `view` and `onView`
because this page has neither. Everything visible here is Portuguese; the inherited board stays English.
The capabilities route and the probe route come from the two preceding beads.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the
  branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and
  commit messages, with the list kept in the user's private notes outside the repository; a failed or
  unavailable sweep blocks the push, and the close reason records only that it passed.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time, so two
  landings never carry different copies of `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
- Read before writing a route or a page, because this Next.js differs from older versions:
  `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md` and
  `.../03-file-conventions/page.md`.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after
  the last one); pure-script guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- The phase this bead belongs to frames the work dashboard, a page served by a local collector program
  on the work machine, inside Houston at the route /work, and adds the config key `workDashboardUrl`
  that holds that page's address. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries
  everything it needs from it.

## Specification
Files:

- `app/work/page.tsx`: metadata title through `projectTitle("Trabalho")` (`lib/app-title.ts`),
  rendering the client shell `components/work-shell.tsx`. The shell calls no
  `useSearchParams()`, so the page needs no `<Suspense>` and carries no English fallback text.
- `lib/api-client.ts`: `capabilities()` with `{ cache: "no-store" }` like `viewerMode` (`:159`),
  and `workProbe()`, a `POST` with `{ cache: "no-store" }`, both through `request()` (`:133-149`),
  passing TanStack's `signal`.
- `hooks/use-capabilities.ts`: one query under `["capabilities"]`, with `retry: false` and the
  app's global defaults otherwise (`components/providers.tsx:13`: two-second stale time,
  refetch on focus). A tab left open therefore sees a restarted or reconfigured server, without
  TanStack's default three retries (about seven seconds of backoff) when the read fails. A
  successful body without a
  string `workDashboardUrl` that is non-empty after trimming is normalised to unset, because
  some browser fixtures
  answer an unknown read with `{}` (`scripts/test-all-sidebar.mjs:76`); a failed request stays a
  query error.
- `hooks/use-work-probe.ts`: one query under `["work-probe", url]`, enabled only when the
  capabilities read succeeded with a URL, with `staleTime: Infinity`,
  `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, `refetchOnReconnect: false`, `retry: false` and `gcTime: 0`.
  Returning to the tab or reconnecting never probes again while `/work` is mounted, so a collector
  that is slow for a moment never unmounts a frame the user is working in; leaving `/work` drops the
  cached answer, so coming back probes afresh instead of trusting an answer up to five minutes old.

Shell:

- A pseudo id, `WORK_PAGE_ID = "@work"`, beside `ALL_PROJECT_ID` (`lib/aggregate.ts:13`).
- `AppProvider` with a value of its own: that id, no beads, an empty index, no `meta`, an empty
  human allowlist, not read-only, not loading, no selection and handlers that do nothing (the
  fields of `components/app-context.tsx:12-33`). The sidebar reads `meta`, `beads` and `index`
  from it (`components/sidebar.tsx:45`); with no `meta`, the gamification read stays off
  (`:51`).
- The layout of `components/all-projects-shell.tsx:364-374`, without its `<ReadOnlyBanner />`
  (which polls the viewer-mode route), `<Header />`, `<SprintBoardBar />` and `<FailedNotice />`:
  an outer `flex h-full flex-col overflow-hidden bg-background text-foreground text-sm`, as at
  `:364` and `components/app-shell.tsx:204`; `<MobileSidebar>`; then an inner row,
  `flex min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-hidden` (`:367-369`), holding `<Sidebar>` and a content column
  with a `main` of `relative flex min-h-0 min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col` (`:374`; `relative` keeps the
  visually hidden heading inside it). Both sidebars get
  `projectId={WORK_PAGE_ID}` and `views={[]}`. Without the row the sidebar and the main area would
  stack vertically. Without
  `<MobileSidebar>` a narrow screen has no navigation at all, because `<Sidebar>` is
  `hidden md:flex` (`components/sidebar.tsx:60`).
- `view` and `onView` become optional in `SidebarProps` (`components/sidebar.tsx:17-31`),
  because a page without views has neither. Both call sites guard: the view button
  (`:85`, `onView?.(n.key)`) and `MobileSidebar`'s `chooseView` (`:168-176`). Under
  `strict: true` an unguarded call fails `npm run build`.
- No `actorName` is passed, so the footer shows the sidebar's own fallback, "you" (`:46`).
- The switcher (`components/project-switcher.tsx:39-42`, the dot at `:66`, the second line at
  `:70`): for `WORK_PAGE_ID` the name is "Trabalho", the second line "painel do trabalho", and
  no status dot, as for `ALL_PROJECT_ID`.

Main area, with `lang="pt-BR"` (the root document says `lang="en"`, `app/layout.tsx:20`), an
accessible name "Trabalho", and an `h1` "Trabalho", visually hidden while the frame is shown.
State and failure text sit in one polite `role="status"` region, the same element across
every state, so a test's `getByRole("status")` never finds two. In state 8 it is empty and
`sr-only`, so it takes no layout height and the frame can fill the main area. A URL shown in a
message breaks anywhere (`break-all`, as `components/settings-view.tsx:129`), so a long one
cannot widen a 390 px screen. States, checked in this order, because a disabled TanStack query
stays `isPending` forever:

1. capabilities loading, before any answer: "Verificando o painel do trabalho…";
2. capabilities failed with no data yet (`isError && !data`, so a failed background refetch on
   focus never unmounts a live frame): "Não foi possível verificar a configuração." and a
   "Tentar de novo" button that refetches it; while it refetches the button stays mounted and
   disabled and the status region reads "Verificando o painel do trabalho…", as in state 7;
3. no URL: "O painel do trabalho não está configurado." and a line naming `workDashboardUrl` in
   the config file and the restart;
4. first probe pending, before any probe has settled: "Verificando o painel do trabalho…";
5. `reason: "self"`: "O endereço configurado em `workDashboardUrl` (<url>) é o do próprio
   Houston." and a line naming the config file and the restart; no retry, since retrying cannot
   fix it;
6. the probe answered `{ configured: false }` (the key was cleared after the page read it): the
   unconfigured state of item 3. The probe's `queryFn` invalidates `["capabilities"]` when the
   answer has `configured: false`, never the render, so the sidebar and the page learn that the
   key is gone;
7. unreachable, or the probe failed (`probe.isError`, or an answer whose `reachable` is not
   `true`): "O painel do trabalho não respondeu em <url>.", "Inicie o servidor do collector e
   tente de novo.", and "Tentar de novo", which calls `refetch()`. During
   that refetch the same state stays mounted: the button stays in place, disabled, and the status
   region reads "Verificando o painel do trabalho…". A state that replaced the button while
   fetching would leave nothing to disable and nothing to click twice;
8. reachable, and only on an answer with `configured: true` and `reachable: true`: an `iframe`
   sized `h-full w-full flex-1 border-0`, with `title="Painel do trabalho"` and
   `allow="clipboard-write"`.

The fragment goes one way. `window.location.hash` is read through `React.useSyncExternalStore`
with `""` as the server snapshot, as `components/read-only-banner.tsx:17-24,36` reads its
preferences, subscribed to `hashchange` and `popstate`, and notified after every
`history.pushState` and `history.replaceState` (a `Link` to `/work#...` while already on `/work`
changes the hash without either event). That banner only listens to events, so the history part
has no pattern in the repository yet. The App Router wraps both history methods itself
(`node_modules/next/dist/client/components/app-router.js:274-325`) and writes history from a
`useInsertionEffect` (`:74-110`). So the reader keeps a module-level set of listeners and wraps
each method once, lazily, on the first subscription: the wrapper calls the function it replaced
and then notifies through `queueMicrotask`, because a synchronous notification inside that
insertion effect would schedule a React update where React forbids one. It never restores the
originals on unsubscribe, since doing so could discard a wrapper installed after it. A
`setState` inside an effect would fail the lint, whose React Compiler rules forbid it
(`components/app-shell.tsx:40-41`). The frame's `src` is the configured URL with that fragment set through `URL`, so a link to `/work#incident/<id>` opens
that incident in the frame, and the configured path is kept. Changing only the fragment of a
loaded frame fires `hashchange` inside it without a reload. Nothing reads the frame's location,
which the browser forbids across origins; moving around inside the frame never changes the
hub's address.

No `sandbox` attribute. The frame is the user's own local page, and a sandbox needs the list of
what that page does (scripts, its own requests, forms, popups, downloads), which is known only
once it is tried on the work machine. `clipboard-write` is allowed because a cross-origin frame
cannot write to the clipboard without it, and the dashboard's draft editors are the likely
place to copy text from.

Proof: browser `scripts/test-work-page.mjs`, against the real server, with no stub for the
capabilities read or the probe outside the cases below that name one. It registers no project.
It serves a synthetic dashboard only at `/dashboard/view` on `127.0.0.1:0`, records the paths it
is asked for, writes its own `location.hash` into its body on load and on `hashchange`, and has
a link that changes the hash. The test sets the key through `PUT /api/config` and reloads the
page after every such `PUT`, because the request does not touch the page's query cache; the one
exception is the `{ configured: false }` case, which exists to clear the key under a live page.

- The title is exactly `Trabalho | Houston`.
- No view buttons (the sidebar's `<nav>` holds no button, leaving room for step 6's link); the
  switcher's accessible name is `Select project, current project Trabalho`,
  its second line `painel do trabalho`, and no status dot; the footer reads `you`; no request
  path matches `/(@|%40)work/i` (`lib/api-client.ts:151-152` percent-encodes the `@`, and
  `scripts/test-all-sidebar.mjs:117` checks `@all` the same way) and none names gamification.
  The same in the mobile sheet.
- The main area has the name "Trabalho", the `h1`, and `lang="pt-BR"`.
- With the synthetic server holding its answer: "Verificando o painel do trabalho…" in the
  status region; released well inside the probe's two-second timeout: the frame.
- The frame has exactly `title="Painel do trabalho"`, grants `clipboard-write`, has no
  `sandbox`; its height matches the main area's within 1 px and is at least the viewport height
  minus 100 px, which a collapsed default 150 px frame fails; its body reads
  "synthetic dashboard"; the synthetic server saw `/dashboard/view` and nothing at `/`.
- `/work#incident/INC00000001` loaded cold (from another page, not as a hash change on `/work`), so
  the server render and hydration with a hash are exercised: the frame reports
  `#incident/INC00000001` and the path stays `/dashboard/view`.
- Clicking the link inside the frame changes the frame's hash and leaves `page.url()` as it was.
- Setting the hub's hash to `#incident/INC00000002` from the page: the frame reports it, and the
  synthetic server receives no new request (a hash change, not a reload). Then
  `history.pushState(null, "", "/work#incident/INC00000003")` from the page, which fires neither
  `hashchange` nor `popstate`: the frame reports `#incident/INC00000003`, again with no new
  request.
- With the frame live, a marker set on `window`, `/work` left through the switcher's Demo item,
  the synthetic server stopped, and `page.goBack()`: the marker is still there (a client-side
  return, not a reload), a new probe request is sent, and the unreachable state shows with no
  frame, instead of a cached `reachable: true` (which is what `gcTime: 0` protects).
- The synthetic server stopped (`closeAllConnections()` then `close()`, since both the probe and
  the frame hold keep-alive sockets to it), `/work` reloaded: the unreachable sentence with the
  URL, the "Inicie o servidor do collector e tente de novo." sentence, and the retry button. The
  server started again on the same port, holding only its next request (the probe's), and
  "Tentar de novo" clicked: the checking text shows in the status region and the button stays
  mounted and disabled; a second click (`{ force: true }`, since Playwright otherwise waits for a
  disabled button) starts no second probe request, counted before the release, since once
  released the frame also requests `/dashboard/view`; released well inside the probe's two-second
  timeout: the frame is back.
- With the synthetic server stopped and `/work` showing the unreachable state, the next
  `GET /api/capabilities` intercepted and held, the key cleared through `PUT /api/config` without
  a reload, and "Tentar de novo" clicked: the probe answers `{ configured: false }`, the
  unconfigured sentence shows while that capabilities read is still held, and the read was
  requested after the click; released, the unconfigured state stays.
- `POST /api/work/probe` intercepted to answer 500, `/work` reloaded with the key set: the
  unreachable state and no frame.
- `workDashboardUrl` set to Houston's own address: the self state, with no retry button.
- With the key back on the synthetic server and the frame live, `GET /api/capabilities`
  intercepted to answer 500; after the two-second stale time,
  `window.dispatchEvent(new Event("visibilitychange"))` refetches it. TanStack Query 5.101.2's
  focus manager listens only to `visibilitychange` on `window`
  (`node_modules/@tanstack/query-core/build/modern/focusManager.js:10-12`), so a `focus` event
  would refetch nothing and the case would wait forever. The 500 arrives, no new
  `POST /api/work/probe` is sent, and the frame stays, with no error shown (which is what
  `isError && !data` protects).
- Reloaded with `GET /api/capabilities` answering 500 once: the capabilities-failed sentence and
  its button; the next read then held and the button clicked: the button stays mounted and
  disabled and the status region reads "Verificando o painel do trabalho…"; the read released to
  the real server: the frame.
- On a 390 px wide screen: the frame is visible, fills the main area, and the page does not
  scroll sideways. With the key set to a port the test opened and closed, followed by a path of
  200 characters with no break opportunity, the unreachable state's status region has a
  `scrollWidth` no larger than its `clientWidth` and a right edge inside the viewport. The
  document's own width would pass without `break-all`, because the outer `overflow-hidden` clips
  rather than scrolls.
- The key cleared: the exact unconfigured sentence and the line naming `workDashboardUrl` and the
  restart.
- No `pageerror` in the whole run, and no console error outside the deliberate 500 cases, which
  also catches a hydration mismatch.
- In `finally` it clears the key, closes the browser, and closes the synthetic server
  (`closeAllConnections()` then an awaited `close()`), so a failure mid-run leaves no keep-alive
  socket holding the process open. It writes only `/api/config`, which viewer mode allows
  (`proxy.ts:17-19`; the check at `:57-62` covers only `/api/p/` and `/api/sprints`), so it
  passes under both launch modes and joins neither list in `AGENTS.md`.

Broken on purpose, one at a time, each turns a named case red: the fragment subscription, the
history notification (the `pushState` case), the kept path, the title, `clipboard-write`, adding
a `sandbox`, the full height, a status region that keeps its height in state 8, the state order
(the unconfigured case stuck on "Verificando"), the `{ configured: false }` state and,
separately, its invalidation, a probe failure falling through to the frame, `gcTime: 0`, the
disabled retry, the self state, the capabilities-failed state and its disabled retry, the
`isError && !data` guard, and `break-all`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `scripts/with-server.sh 3211 node scripts/test-work-page.mjs` exits 0, and again under `SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1`, with every case listed under Proof in the Specification as a named assertion.
- [ ] The page title is exactly "Trabalho | Houston" and the main area carries lang pt-BR, the accessible name "Trabalho" and one status region.
- [ ] The frame's height matches the main area's within 1 px and is at least the viewport height minus 100 px, and on a 390 px screen the page does not scroll sideways.
- [ ] A cold load with an incident fragment, a hash change from the page and a click inside the frame each behave as the Specification states, with no reload on a hash change.
- [ ] The run records no page error and no console error outside the deliberate 500 case.
- [ ] Each deliberate break listed in the Specification turns a named assertion red, recorded in the close reason.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: /work frames a reachable dashboard and shows each non-frame state, all proven by the browser test on `main`.

## Tests
- e2e: `scripts/test-work-page.mjs`, a Playwright script against the real server (no stub for the capabilities read or the probe) with a synthetic dashboard served by the test.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `app/work/page.tsx`, `components/work-shell.tsx`, `lib/api-client.ts`, `hooks/use-capabilities.ts`, `hooks/use-work-probe.ts`, `lib/aggregate.ts`, `components/sidebar.tsx`, `components/project-switcher.tsx`, `scripts/test-work-page.mjs`
**Reads only:** `components/all-projects-shell.tsx`, `components/app-context.tsx`, `components/read-only-banner.tsx`, `components/providers.tsx`, `lib/app-title.ts`, `app/all/page.tsx`, `scripts/with-server.sh`

Nine files across the page, two hooks, the client, the sidebar's props and the switcher's label. Size L:
it cannot split along a seam that shares no file, because the page, its hooks and the sidebar prop
change land together or the build breaks.
close_reason: /work frames the configured work dashboard (app/work/page.tsx, components/work-shell.tsx, hooks use-capabilities and use-work-probe, api-client calls): title "Trabalho | Houston", main area lang pt-BR named Trabalho with one status region, a full-height iframe with clipboard-write and no sandbox, the fragment kept in sync without reloads, and the checking, unconfigured, unreachable, self and capabilities-failed states with disabled retries while refetching; the sidebar and switcher render a viewless page. Every listed break turned a named assertion red through mutate-check (19 rows, e.g. a sandbox added failed 'frame attributes: no sandbox', gcTime Infinity failed 'gcTime step: unreachable after back'). Review break: main lang en failed 'main lang pt-BR'. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build, test-work-page default and SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1, and the regressions test-mobile-navigation, test-project-chip and test-keyboard (read-only) pass.

title: Link the work dashboard from the sidebar and the launcher when it is configured
description:
## What changes for the user
Today nothing in Houston leads to the work dashboard. Once this lands, a "Trabalho" link sits in its own
group in the sidebar of every page that has one, and a "Trabalho" card on the launcher, both only when
the dashboard's address is configured, so it is one click away from anywhere.

## Outcome
The sidebar's navigation gains a destinations group after the view buttons holding a "Trabalho" link,
the launcher gains a "Trabalho" card after the built-in cards, both driven by the capabilities read; the
browser tests that intercept every API request get an explicit capabilities fixture; the sidebar and
work-page tests prove placement, visibility and mobile behaviour.

## Context
Decided with the user: the link is a group of its own in the sidebar, below the view buttons, not an item
of the project switcher's dropdown, where "All projects" and "Sprints" stay; a later phase adds a search
link to the same group. Playwright runs matching `context.route` handlers in reverse order of
registration, which decides where each fixture goes. The /work page comes from the preceding bead.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the
  branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and

components, or the entry tests go red.

The entry and texts scripts answer the capabilities read in their fixtures. Every listed break red, e.g. the link shown with the key unset failed 'unconfigured has no Trabalho', the card gated on a project count failed 'launcher with only demo'. Internal-name sweep passed; lint, build, test-work-page default and SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1, test-all-sidebar, test-all-projects-entry, test-sprints-entry, test-tracker-texts and test-mobile-navigation pass.

title: Document the work dashboard setup and check every documented path
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the setup guide says nothing about the work dashboard, and nothing checks that the paths the
documents name still exist. Once this lands the guide says how to set, clear and troubleshoot the
dashboard's address on the work machine, and a test fails whenever a document points at a file that is
gone.

## Outcome
`docs/work-side-setup.md` gains a "Work dashboard" section, the README names the key and the page,
`AGENTS.md` lists the new scripts, and a new pure script checks every markdown link and every
repository path inside code spans of those documents.

## Context
The setup guide is what the user follows on the work machine, which only pulls from this public
repository. Re-running the installer rewrites the service definition, and `KeepAlive` restarts a stopped
service at once, which is why the guide names `launchctl bootout` and `bootstrap`.

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,
  repository, team, the internal work-item tracker's real name) goes into any file, commit, pull
  request or bead; fixtures are synthetic (`INC00000001`, `org/repo-a`, `example.com`). Before the
  branch's first push, the agent landing it runs the internal-name sweep over the branch's diff and
  commit messages, with the list kept in the user's private notes outside the repository; a failed or
  unavailable sweep blocks the push, and the close reason records only that it passed.
- Work in a worktree of your own and land through a pull request, with the local gate of `AGENTS.md`
  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,
  each under the launch mode it expects. Beads developed in parallel land one at a time, so two
  landings never carry different copies of `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
- Read before writing a route or a page, because this Next.js differs from older versions:
  `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md` and
  `.../03-file-conventions/page.md`.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after
  the last one); pure-script guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- The phase this bead belongs to frames the work dashboard, a page served by a local collector program
  on the work machine, inside Houston at the route /work, and adds the config key `workDashboardUrl`
  that holds that page's address. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries
  everything it needs from it.

## Specification
- `docs/work-side-setup.md`: a section `## Work dashboard` after "Verify the service"
  (`:66-82`) and before "Updating" (`:84`):
  - the key and its rules: exactly `127.0.0.1`, `http` or `https`, no credentials, no query, no
    fragment;
  - the config file's path, derived from the `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` the service definition pins
    (`scripts/install-services.sh:186-199`);
  - two safe ways to set it: while Houston runs, `PUT` only `workDashboardUrl` to the config
    route (and `{"workDashboardUrl": ""}` to clear it); or unload the service with
    `launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/houston.hub"` (not `kill` or `launchctl stop`, which
    `KeepAlive` undoes at once), edit the existing JSON object without replacing other fields, and
    load it again with `launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/houston.hub.plist"`. The file is read once and is not edited while the service runs, as
    the document's operational rules already say (`:98-110`);
  - what `/work` shows when the collector is not running;
  - when the collector serves `https` with a certificate that only the macOS keychain trusts and
    `/work` says it is not answering: `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca` in
    the plist's `EnvironmentVariables`, never a bare flag in `ProgramArguments`, which
    `bin/houston-web.mjs` does not pass on to `next start`; the plist checked with `plutil -lint`
    and reloaded with `bootout` and then `bootstrap`; and a note that re-running
    `scripts/install-services.sh` rewrites the plist and drops the edit;
  - when the frame stays blank or shows a refusal (a 403, say): the collector's server refuses
    to be framed. `X-Frame-Options` cannot name one allowed origin (its values are `DENY` and
    `SAMEORIGIN`), so an origin-specific allowance is a `Content-Security-Policy:
    frame-ancestors http://127.0.0.1:3300` on that document's response, with `X-Frame-Options`
    removed for it; a check on the request's fetch-metadata headers is relaxed the same way,
    for that document load only.
  - The "Updating" section's claim that `scripts/update.sh` runs from anywhere is corrected: it
    is run from the checkout, or by its absolute path (`docs/work-side-setup.md:84-90`).
- `README.md`: the key under "Configuration" (`:53`) and the page under "Features" (`:8`).
- `AGENTS.md`: `node scripts/test-loopback-url.mjs` and `node scripts/test-doc-links.mjs` join the
  pure scripts (`:79-81`), written in that form like the two already there; the sentence about
  scripts with a pure and a server half (`:88-89`) names `scripts/test-work-config.mjs` and
  `scripts/test-work-probe.mjs` as two, with the `scripts/` prefix, so the doc checker below
  checks them; `test-work-probe.mjs` and `test-work-page.mjs` pass under both launch modes, so
  neither launch-mode list changes.
- A new pure script, `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`. It finds the repository root from
  `import.meta.url`, not the working directory, and reads `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and every
  `*.md` under `docs/`, recursively. Fenced code blocks (`README.md:79-88`,
  `docs/work-side-setup.md:35-37`) are removed before anything else is scanned, so a fence never
  pairs with an inline backtick. Every markdown link that has no scheme (`https:`, `mailto:`) and
  is not a same-file `#anchor` exists relative to its own file's directory once any `#fragment`
  or `?query` is cut off (so `[...](../scripts/update.sh)` in `docs/work-side-setup.md` resolves
  from `docs/`), and every path-shaped token inside an inline code span exists relative to the
  repository root. A code span holding a command
  (`scripts/with-server.sh 3211 node scripts/test-br-store.mjs`,
  `AGENTS.md:84-86,121-124`) is split into tokens, never read as one path; each token that starts
  with `app/`, `bin/`, `components/`, `design/`, `docs/`, `hooks/`, `lib/` or `scripts/`, or is
  exactly `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `SECURITY.md` or `LICENSE`, is checked, with ordinary
  surrounding shell punctuation stripped, nothing expanded and nothing run. It ignores paths built
  from `$HOME` or
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, route paths like `/all` or `/work`, and `node_modules/`, which exists only
  after an install. Later phases keep using it.

Proof: `node scripts/test-doc-links.mjs` passes, run from the repository root and again from
another directory. One broken Markdown link, and separately one broken path token inside a
command span, each turn a named assertion red; a link with a `#fragment` to an existing file and
a fence holding a path that does not exist each leave it green. The internal-name sweep
of "Preconditions" runs once more over every commit of the phase and the whole diff, and finds
nothing; it is the last check, not the first.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `node scripts/test-doc-links.mjs` exits 0 over `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `docs/work-side-setup.md`.
- [ ] Breaking one markdown link, and separately one path token inside a multi-token command span, each turn a named assertion red.
- [ ] `docs/work-side-setup.md` has a "Work dashboard" section between "Verify the service" and "Updating" covering the rules, the config file's path, both ways to set and clear the key, the not-running state and the framing refusal.
- [ ] The internal-name sweep over every commit of the phase and the whole diff finds nothing.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] Done when: the documents describe the feature and the link checker guards them on `main`.

## Tests
- unit: `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`, a pure scan of markdown links and code-span path tokens, run with `node` directly.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `docs/work-side-setup.md`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `scripts/test-doc-links.mjs`
**Reads only:** `scripts/install-services.sh`, `scripts/update.sh`

Three documents and one new pure script. Size M.
close_reason: docs/work-side-setup.md gains a "Work dashboard" section after "Verify the service" (address rules, where the config file lives, setting and clearing the key through Settings and PUT /api/config, the not-running state, an https collector with a keychain-only certificate, a collector that refuses framing); README and AGENTS.md point at it; scripts/test-doc-links.mjs checks every markdown link and every path token in code spans of the three documents. A broken README link failed 'markdown links resolve to files' and a bad path inside the multi-token AGENTS command span failed 'code-span path tokens exist'. The internal-name sweep over every commit since the phase began (90 commits, 249 files) and this branch's diff found nothing. Lint, build and test-doc-links pass.

title: Run the full test matrix on main after the phase 1 code lands
description:
## Outcome
Every test script of the repository has run once on `main`, after the phase 1 code beads landed and
before the work machine updates, each under the launch mode it expects, and each row's command and exit
status is recorded in the epic.

## Context
Phase 1 touches shared code (the config module, the sidebar, the launcher, the routing of four browser

## Rules for this work

- Houston is a public repository. No employer-internal name (company, internal system, host,

  ("Landing work"): `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and every test script the change adds or touches,

  `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md` and
  `.../03-file-conventions/page.md`.
- Every new guard is broken once on purpose before landing, and the close reason names the assertion
  that went red. Server-backed and browser guards go through `scripts/mutate-check.py` (rebuild after
  the last one); pure-script guards are broken and run directly with `node`.
- The phase this bead belongs to frames the work dashboard, a page served by a local collector program
  on the work machine, inside Houston at the route /work, and adds the config key `workDashboardUrl`
  that holds that page's address. The phase's plan is kept outside the repository; this bead carries
  everything it needs from it.

## Specification
- Step 1, then 2. Steps 3 and 4 may be developed in parallel after 2 (they touch disjoint files)
  and land one at a time. Step 5 needs 3 and 4; step 6 needs 5; step 7 needs 6.
- After step 7 lands, and before the work machine updates, a verification bead runs the full test
  matrix once on `main`, in its own checkout of `main`, starting with `npm run lint` and
  `npm run build` there: steps 1 to 7 were built in their own worktrees, `.next/` is not
  versioned, and the wrapper serves whatever that checkout last built (`AGENTS.md:93-94`). Then:
  pure scripts bare; scripts with a pure and a server half bare, then through the wrapper in
  their launch mode (without `SCOTTY_READ_ONLY=1` for the three that are
  also edit-only, `test-label-edits`, `test-sprint-run` and `test-sprints`, and both ways for the

- Step 8 needs that verification bead and phase 0's installation.

Beads:

- seven implementation beads for steps 1 to 7, each one pull request;
- one verification bead for the full test matrix after step 7, blocking step 8;
- one work-side bead for step 8, assigned to the user, so `br ready --unassigned` never offers
  it to an agent;
- phase 0's installation on the work machine, one work-side bead assigned to the user, outside
  this epic; step 8's bead depends on it;
- one epic over steps 1 to 8.

The work machine pulls and never pushes, and closing a bead rewrites `.beads/issues.jsonl`,
which `AGENTS.md` lands with a pull request. So a work-side bead is closed on the development
machine, from the result the user reports there in generic words, in a pull request that

## Acceptance criteria

title: Check the framed work dashboard on the work machine
description:
## What changes for the user
Until this is done, the framed dashboard has only ever run against a synthetic page. Once it passes, the
real dashboard opens inside Houston on the work machine, its actions work inside the frame, and a link to
an incident opens it there.

## Outcome
Each item of the checklist below has passed on the work machine, and the result is recorded in generic
words; a failed item opens the smallest fixing bead and this bead waits on it.

## Context
The work machine pulls this public repository and never pushes, so the user reports the result and the
bead is closed on the development machine in a tracker-only pull request. The public tracker never gets
a real incident number, the collector's address or port, a header value, an error text, a screenshot, a
label or a cookie name. What the collector's server does with a framed load was never measured; if it
refuses, the smallest origin-specific relaxation is made in the collector's own local code, never in
this repository.

## Specification
The user's, on the work machine, after steps 1 to 7 are on `main` and phase 0's installation is
done.

1. From the Houston checkout, `scripts/update.sh`; set `workDashboardUrl` by one of the two ways
   of step 7.
2. With the collector running, open `/work`. Record the actual headers of the framed document
   load and of one of the dashboard's own requests. Do not assume the load is `same-site`: an
   `https` collector framed by Houston on `http` is cross-site by scheme. If the collector
   refuses the framed load, relax it as step 7 says, in its local code. If it serves `https`
   with a certificate only the keychain trusts and `/work` says it is not answering, apply one
   durable fix to the hub's service and record which: `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<absolute PEM bundle>`,
   or `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca`, added to the plist's `EnvironmentVariables`, the plist
   checked with `plutil -lint "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/houston.hub.plist"`, then unloaded with
   `launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/houston.hub"` and loaded with
   `launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/houston.hub.plist"`, the order
   the installer uses (`scripts/install-services.sh:269-270`): bootstrapping a service that is
   still loaded fails, and `kickstart` would not read the edited plist. Never a
   `--use-system-ca` flag in `ProgramArguments`: the launcher starts `next start` as a child
   without passing its own Node flags on (`bin/houston-web.mjs:234-238`), while environment
   variables do reach it. Then probe again. The service definition today carries exactly `PATH`
   and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (`scripts/install-services.sh:225-231`, pinned by
   `scripts/test-install-services.mjs:68-71`), and re-running the installer rewrites the plist
   (`:262-270`), so a hand edit is local machine state that the next install loses; if the fix
   stays, a follow-up bead teaches the installer the option, with its pinned test.
3. Exercise what the dashboard does inside the frame: it loads its data; a manual refresh of its
   data works; `/work#incident/<a real incident>` opens that incident; copying text from it
   reaches the clipboard; its draft editors work; any popup or download it offers works. Watch
   the browser console and network panel for failures.
4. Cookies, listed in the user's private notes only, never in the tracker, since the collector's
   cookie names may carry work names: the cookies both services set on `127.0.0.1` (names, path,
   `Secure`, `SameSite`, expiry). Cookies are not separated by port, so Houston's
   `scotty-viewer-mode` (`path=/`, not `Secure` over `http`, `SameSite=Strict`,
   `app/api/viewer-mode/route.ts:27-31`) reaches an `http` collector once it is set, which is
   expected. Not being `Secure`, it also reaches an `https` collector's own top-level loads;
   `SameSite=Strict` withholds it only from the framed load, which is cross-site by scheme when
   Houston is on `http`. The blockers are a collector cookie with that name, a collector that
   misbehaves when it receives it, or a collector session cookie sent to Houston.
5. With the collector stopped, `/work` says so; after starting it, "Tentar de novo" shows the
   dashboard.

Proof: each item passed, in generic words. A failed item keeps the work-side bead and the epic
open: the failure is recorded in generic words, the smallest bead that fixes it is created in the
repository that owns the fix, the work-side bead depends on it, and after it lands the failed item
and any item it affects are run again. Only a fully passing run closes step 8. The public tracker
never gets a real
incident number, the collector's address or port, a header value, an error text, a screenshot,
a label, or any other work data.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Items 1 to 5 of the Specification each passed, recorded in generic words.
- [ ] A failed item kept this bead open, produced a fixing bead this one depends on, and was run again after the fix with every item it affects.
- [ ] Nothing in the close reason or any comment is work data.
- [ ] Done when: the real dashboard works framed in Houston on the work machine.

## Tests
- e2e: the five-item checklist, run by hand against the real collector on the work machine.

## Blast radius
Confined to the work machine: the hub's config file, its service definition, and the collector's
own local code if a framing rule has to be relaxed there. No file of this repository is edited by this
bead; a fix it needs here is its own bead.

title: Install Houston as a login service on the work machine
description:
## What changes for the user
Until this is done, Houston has only been built and tested on the development machine. Once it passes,
it starts by itself at login on the work machine, on 127.0.0.1 port 3300, and shows the work
repositories' real trackers.

## Outcome
The work machine runs Houston as the `houston.hub` user agent, verified by the checks below, with the
work repositories registered as projects.

## Context
This is the last step of phase 0, the repository's birth, which was published on 2026-11-24 at commit
`df02e21`. It belongs to no phase 1 epic; the phase 1 work-side check depends on it. The procedure is in
`docs/work-side-setup.md`. Answering on the port is not the check: a child left behind by a killed
launcher also answers. The bead is closed on the development machine from the result the user reports,
since the work machine never pushes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Clone, `npm ci`, `npm run build` and `scripts/install-services.sh` ran on the work machine as `docs/work-side-setup.md` describes.
- [ ] After a login, Houston answers on 127.0.0.1 port 3300.
- [ ] Before any registration the project list shows only the built-in Demo, not the Houston checkout.
- [ ] After `launchctl kickstart -k`, `launchctl print` shows the service running under a new process id.
- [ ] The work repositories are registered, the board shows their trackers, and a bead created there appears in `br list` in its repository.
- [ ] Done when: Houston runs on the work machine against the real trackers, recorded in generic words.

## Tests
- e2e: the checks above, run by hand against the real service manager on the work machine.

## Blast radius
Confined to the work machine: a clone of this repository, its build, the `houston.hub` service
definition the install script writes, and Houston's config file. No file of this repository is edited.
